docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
Event detection: Repository Events API (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/events).

PR backfill: Events API truncates PR payloads. The poller fetches the full PR via GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number} for all PR-related events. For PullRequestEvent/closed, the merged field distinguishes pr.closed from pr.merged.

Base URL resolution: GitHubUrls.resolve turns the stored baseUrl into a web URL (used to build refs) and a REST API URL (used for polling). The stored value is kept as entered and resolved on each poll. Scheme and host are case-insensitive, a missing scheme means https, and trailing slashes, query and fragment are ignored. A repository path in the URL is ignored; repositories always come from configuration.

baseUrl Web URL API URL github.com, www.github.com or api.github.com (any path) https://github.com https://api.github.com <org>.ghe.com or api.<org>.ghe.com https://<org>.ghe.com https://api.<org>.ghe.com Other host with /api/v3 in the path everything before /api/v3 up to and including /api/v3 Any other host (GitHub Enterprise Server) <scheme>://<host> <scheme>://<host>/api/v3

A value that is not an http(s) URL with a host fails validation and is recorded as a configuration error when polled. In the ref formats below, {baseUrl} is the resolved web URL.

ref construction:

Event Category Format Issue events {baseUrl}/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number} PR events {baseUrl}/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{number} Push events {baseUrl}/{owner}/{repo} Branch events {baseUrl}/{owner}/{repo}/tree/{branchName} Tag/release events {baseUrl}/{owner}/{repo}/releases/tag/{tagName}

Deduplication: Each Events API event has a unique id. The poller tracks seen IDs per event source + repo in memory and deduplicates in the database via the source_event_id unique index.

Polling: ETag-based conditional polling (304 on no change). Default 60-second interval.

docs.title: Jira
docs.text:
Event detection: JQL search with expand=changelog, ordered by updated. The search requests the fields used for snapshots (summary, description, status, assignee, reporter, labels, priority, resolution, resolutiondate, duedate, fixVersions, components, issuetype, project, comment, created, updated, parent) plus the IDs of the configured extraFields. Truncated changelogs are completed with GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/changelog; incomplete comment lists (total greater than the number returned) with GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment. A 404/403 on either falls back to the embedded data; 5xx, 429 and network errors abort the poll window without advancing the checkpoint.

Per-poll lookups: once per event source and poll, GET /rest/api/3/status builds a status ID → category key map, and (only when extraFields is configured) GET /rest/api/3/field resolves field names to IDs, ignoring case. Unknown extraFields names are ignored with a warning. If the status lookup fails, a warning is logged and status names done, closed and resolved (case-insensitive) are treated as done. In this degraded mode a transition into a custom done status (for example Shipped) is emitted as issue.updated while the snapshot's state may already be closed.

Issue state as of each event: JiraIssueHistory sorts the changelog newest first, starts from the current issue, and for each entry records the state after that entry and then undoes the entry's items (to → from). What remains is the state at creation, used by issue.created. Comment events use the state in effect at the comment's timestamp. Tracked: status (name, ID, category → state/stateDetail), summary, description, assignee, labels, resolution and closedAt, priority, due date, fix versions, components and every configured extra field. updatedAt of a snapshot is the timestamp of the entry that produced it (created for the creation state). closedAt is the time of the most recent resolution change to a non-null value at or before the snapshot, and null while the resolution is empty.

Limits: - Fields without changelog history keep their current values in every snapshot. - A rebuilt description is the changelog's plain/wiki text; the current one is converted from ADF. - Comment bodies are always the current text (Jira keeps no comment history). - Jira exposes only a comment's latest updated time, so several edits of one comment within one poll window produce a single issue.comment.updated; intermediate edits are not recorded individually. - Extra-field values from the changelog are Jira's display strings (toString); current values are rendered from the field JSON (value, name, displayName or key of objects, arrays joined with ,, integral numbers without a fraction).

Open/closed: state is closed exactly when the status category key is done. A status change into the done category emits issue.closed, out of it issue.reopened, anything else issue.updated.

Changelog classification:

Changelog field (case-insensitive) Event Type status into the done category issue.closed status out of the done category issue.reopened other status changes issue.updated with change summary, description, priority, resolution, duedate, Fix Version, Component issue.updated with change a name listed in configuration.extraFields issue.updated with change assignee set issue.assigned (assignee.login = account ID from to) assignee cleared issue.unassigned (assignee.login = account ID from from) labels added issue.labeled (one per label) labels removed issue.unlabeled (one per label) Comment with fromString and no toString issue.comment.deleted (comment id and author null, body = deleted text; actor = history author)

sourceEventId formats:

Trigger sourceEventId Issue created {KEY}-created Changelog entry producing one event {KEY}-{historyId} Changelog entry producing several events {KEY}-{historyId}-{i} (item order) Comment created {KEY}-comment-{commentId} Comment edited {KEY}-comment-{commentId}-updated-{updatedEpochMillis} (one per observed edit, keyed by the latest updated)

Timestamps: every timestamp in the payload (createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt, comment timestamps) and the event timestamp are ISO-8601 UTC ending in Z.

sourceData (a selected set, not validated by the event schemas; values follow the snapshot of the event where history exists):

{
  "jiraId": "7358053",
  "project": {"key": "APICURIO", "name": "Apicurio"},
  "issueType": {"name": "Task"},
  "status": {"name": "Closed", "categoryKey": "done"},
  "priority": {"name": "Major"},
  "resolution": {"name": "Done"},
  "dueDate": "2026-10-30",
  "components": [{"name": "core"}],
  "fixVersions": [{"name": "1.2.0"}],
  "extraFields": {"Story Points": "5"}
}

extraFields is present only when configured; a configured field with no value is null.

ref construction: {baseUrl}/browse/{issueKey}

Upgrade notes: - Existing events and IDs are kept. - A comment edit that already has an old-format {KEY}-comment-{id}-updated event gets one more event under the new format after the upgrade (accepted one-time effect). - Changelog entries that now produce more events (for example a status change plus a resolution change) use -{i} suffixes; such an entry re-read in the first poll window after the upgrade is stored once more under the new IDs (accepted one-time effect, limited to the two-minute query overlap). - Whether an entry gets {KEY}-{historyId} or -{i} IDs depends on how many events it produces, which depends on configuration.extraFields; changing extraFields can likewise re-key an entry re-read inside the two-minute overlap, which is then stored once more. - GitHub and Jira event sources whose baseUrl lacks http:// or https:// (for example github.ibm.com/api/v3) now fail validation when edited or imported and must be updated.

Verification tool: tools/jira-groundtruth.py compares raw Jira activity with the stored events and reports field-quality problems and schema-validation results (see the script's --help).

docs.title: Extending Axiom
docs.text: Axiom is designed to be extended at several key points: AI agents, event sources, and notification channels. Extension points generally follow the same pattern — define an interface in an SPI module, implement it in a sibling module, and let CDI discover it at runtime.

docs.title: The SPI Pattern
docs.text:
Extension points that use a formal SPI follow this structure:

component/
├── spi/          Interface definition + registry
└── impl-name/    Concrete implementation

Implementations are @ApplicationScoped CDI beans. A registry or CDI Instance<T> discovers all implementations at startup. The active implementation is selected by configuration or, for agent pool work, by capability matching.

docs.title: Adding an AI Agent
docs.text: An agent provides the ability to invoke an LLM for task execution (workflow action nodes) and AI Assistant sessions (including the Workflow Workbench chat). Axiom ships with three agent implementations: Claude Code, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot CLI.

docs.title: Interface: Agent
docs.text:
Location: agents/spi/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/agents/spi/Agent.java

Method Purpose String getType() Agent type identifier (e.g. "claude-code", "opencode", "copilot") String getLabel() Human-readable display label List<String> getAvailableModels() Models available for the UI model picker String getModelSource() "configured" (default) or "dynamic" (models discovered at runtime) void refreshAvailableModels() Refresh a cached model list (default: no-op) boolean supportsInteractiveSessions() Whether this agent can back AI Assistant sessions (default: false) CompletableFuture<AgentResult> execute(AgentRequest request) Invoke the agent with a prompt void cancel(String executionId) Best-effort cancellation of a running execution List<AgentCheckResult> healthCheck() Startup health checks

Implementations are @ApplicationScoped CDI beans discovered via CDI Instance<Agent>.

docs.title: Discovery: AgentRegistry
docs.text: AgentRegistry discovers all Agent beans via CDI Instance<Agent> and provides type-based lookup. The default agent type is selected by the axiom.agent.default-type configuration property, and can be changed at runtime from Settings > AI Engine in the UI.

docs.title: Configuration Objects
docs.text:
• AgentRequest — builder-based configuration passed to every agent call: prompt, system prompt, model, allowed/disallowed tools, working directory, environment variables, timeout, max steps, budget, MCP config file
  • AgentResult — returned from agent calls: output text, session ID, cost, tokens, success flag, execution log

docs.title: MCP Support (Optional)
docs.text:
If your agent supports MCP tool servers, implement AgentMcpManager:

Method Purpose Path configureMcpServers(Long workItemId, Map<String, String> environment, List<String> allowedTools) Generate MCP config file; return path or null void cleanup(Long workItemId) Clean up after work item completion

AgentRegistry.getMcpManager(agentType) resolves the MCP manager for a given agent type when the Agent implementation also implements AgentMcpManager.

docs.title: Reference Implementations
docs.text:
• Claude Code: agents/claude-code/src/main/java/.../ClaudeCodeAgent.java — subprocess-based, launches claude CLI
  • OpenCode: agents/opencode/src/main/java/.../OpenCodeAgent.java — HTTP client against a running OpenCode server
  • GitHub Copilot CLI: agents/copilot/src/main/java/.../CopilotAgent.java — subprocess-based, launches copilot CLI

docs.title: The Agent Pool
docs.text: Registered agents don't self-select work — AgentPool leases an enabled, idle AgentEntity to a caller based on a requested capability string (e.g. action:Auto-Label Issue). TaskExecutionService requests action:<action type> for every task created by a workflow action node, together with the action type's engine: when the engine is set, only agents of that agentType are considered (an explicit agent assignment of another type is ignored); when it is blank, any type may run the task. If a suitable agent exists but is busy the task waits; if no enabled agent of the engine exists the task fails with a message naming the missing engine. See AI Agents for the capability-matching model.

docs.title: Interactive Assistant Session Drivers
docs.text:
The AI Assistant runtime uses InteractiveSessionDriver as an agent-neutral contract for session lifecycle, prompt submission, permission handling, and interrupt/teardown behavior. InteractiveSessionDriverFactory selects the concrete driver per session (ClaudeInteractiveSessionDriver or OpenCodeInteractiveSessionDriver) based on the session's resolved agent type, and enforces fail-closed OpenCode compatibility checks before allowing session startup. Only Claude Code and OpenCode have interactive session drivers; the GitHub Copilot CLI agent runs tasks only.

Workflow Workbench compositions use the same session runtime with the built-in axiom-workbench session template and @axiom-workbench MCP server (see Stack & Architecture).

docs.title: Adding an Event Source Type
docs.text: An Event Source polls an external system for activity and produces normalized events for the event stream. Axiom ships with GitHub and Jira event source types.

docs.title: Pattern
docs.text: Event source pollers are @Scheduled beans that use EventStreamService to persist normalized events. There is no formal SPI interface — the pattern is convention-based, built around a shared normalized event model (NormalizedEvent and its typed payload records) defined in core.

docs.title: Key Service: EventStreamService
docs.text:
Location: events/core/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/events/core/EventStreamService.java

Method Purpose boolean persistEvent(NormalizedEvent event) Persist a normalized event, deduplicated by source event ID; fires an SSE update on success

docs.title: Implementation Pattern
docs.text:
1. Create a scheduled poller with @Scheduled and concurrentExecution = SKIP
  2. Find enabled event sources of your source type from EventSourceEntity
  3. Check if the event source's poll interval has elapsed since lastPolledAt
  4. Fetch activity from the external API
  5. Normalize each item into a NormalizedEvent with a typed payload and call eventStreamService.persistEvent()
  6. Update lastPolledAt on the event source
  7. Record the poll result in EventSourcePollLogEntity

New event sources do not need any corresponding Subscription configuration to start recording events — subscriptions are what route recorded events onward to workflows (create-workflow and workflow-dispatch routing rules).

docs.title: Reference Implementations
docs.text:
• GitHub: events/github/src/main/java/.../v2/GitHubEventSourcePoller.java — polls the GitHub Repository Events API, backfilling PR payloads as needed
  • Jira: events/jira/src/main/java/.../v2/JiraEventSourcePoller.java — polls the Jira REST API using JQL search with changelog expansion

See Event System — Design Document for the full event schema and per-source normalization details.

docs.title: Adding an Axiom SDK Function
docs.text:
The Axiom SDK is the set of axiom_* functions agents call through the axiom-sdk MCP server and that workflows call directly from sdk: action nodes (see Axiom SDK Functions for the current list). An SDK change must update all of these consistently:

Location Purpose core/src/main/resources/axiom-sdk-functions.json Authoritative function definitions (name, description, parameters) core/.../SdkFunctionRegistry.java Loads the definitions app/.../SdkCallService.java Implementations used by sdk: action nodes app/.../rest/SdkResource.java REST endpoint used by the MCP server app/src/main/resources/templates/axiom-mcp-server/sdk-server.js The axiom-sdk MCP server app/src/main/resources/templates/axiom-assistant-mcp/server.js, templates/assistant-templates/axiom-config-assistant.json Assistant templates that reference SDK tools core/.../services/ActionTypeValidator.java Validates SDK tool names in an action type's allowed tools ui/src/config/sdkTools.ts, ui/src/components/assistant/toolNames.ts UI tool pickers and display names SdkResourceTest, McpConfigGeneratorTest, ActionTypeValidatorTest Tests

SDK functions must not start work outside a workflow: there are no functions for creating tasks directly, closing or reopening subjects, or reports.

docs.title: Adding a Notification Channel
docs.text: Notification channels deliver alerts to humans (e.g. when a task requires human input).

docs.title: Current State
docs.text: The notification SPI (notifications/spi/) is currently a stub — no formal interface is defined yet, and the notifications/slack/ and notifications/telegram/ modules are placeholders with no implemented delivery logic. Human-completed tasks are currently surfaced through the Inbox UI regardless of whether a notification channel is configured.

docs.title: Module Setup
docs.text:
When adding a new extension module:

  1. Create the Maven module directory under the appropriate parent (e.g. agents/my-agent/ or events/my-source/)

  2. Create pom.xml with the parent reference and dependencies, following the pattern of an existing sibling module (e.g. agents/opencode/pom.xml)

  3. Add to root pom.xml modules list and dependencyManagement

  4. Add the Jandex plugin to your module's pom.xml — required for CDI bean discovery in Quarkus:

    <plugin>
    <groupId>io.smallrye</groupId>
    <artifactId>jandex-maven-plugin</artifactId>
</plugin>

  5. Add as a dependency in app/pom.xml so the app module includes your implementation

docs.title: Configuration Item Validation
docs.text:
io.apitomy.axiom.app.validation.ConfigItemValidationService is the single place where configuration items (tools, action types, toolsets, session templates, workflows, event sources, and subscriptions) are validated. It is called by:

  • ToolsResourceImpl — tool validate and create endpoints
  • ActionResourceImpl — action type validate and create endpoints
  • SubscriptionsResourceImpl — subscription create and update
  • ImportExportService — configuration-pack import (including import from the UI) and assistant Apply
  • AssistantItemValidator — the Configuration Assistant's live feedback, the axiom_validate_item MCP tool, and POST /api/v1/assistant/sessions/{sessionId}/validate
  • CompositionValidator and CompositionPublisher — Workflow Workbench draft validation and publishing

Workflow publishing does not call the service. WorkflowPublisher calls WorkflowContentRules.engineProblems and WorkflowContentRules.startInputViolation directly. The service's workflow validation uses those same WorkflowContentRules checks and adds cross-reference checks: referenced action types exist, sdk: functions are valid, and receive-event event types are known.

When adding or changing a rule: graph and Start-input rules belong in WorkflowContentRules (shared by publishing and the service); cross-reference checks belong in ConfigItemValidationService. Do not add ad-hoc checks in REST resources.

Configuration-pack import and assistant Apply validate the whole pack before writing anything. Any error aborts the operation with nothing written (REST import returns 400 with {message, problems}). Items are then written in dependency order — tools, toolsets, action types, session templates, workflows, event sources, subscriptions — workflows are published (skipped when unchanged), and workflowDefinitionName in subscription routing rules is resolved to workflowDefinitionId by SubscriptionRoutingResolver.

The Configuration Assistant's system prompt reference is generated by AssistantReferenceGenerator and substituted for the {{reference}} placeholder. Its worked examples live under app/src/main/resources/templates/assistant-reference/examples/ and are listed in index.txt. AssistantReferenceTest validates and applies every listed example, so any new example must be added to index.txt and must pass validation.

docs.title: How to Contribute
docs.text:
This guide covers the development workflow, coding conventions, and pull request process for contributing to Axiom.

For a quick overview of ways to get involved, see the Getting Started > How to Contribute page.

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository on GitHub
  2. Clone your fork: 
    git clone https://github.com/your-username/apitomy-axiom.git
cd apitomy-axiom
  3. Start development mode: 
    ./dev.sh
  4. Open http://localhost:9191 and verify the UI loads

See the Building Axiom guide for prerequisites and build details.

docs.title: Code Organization
docs.text:
When making changes, use this guide to find the right module:

Change Module REST API endpoint common/api (OpenAPI spec) + app/rest/ (implementation) Domain entity or SDK function definitions core/ Claude Code agent agents/claude-code/ OpenCode agent agents/opencode/ GitHub Copilot CLI agent agents/copilot/ GitHub polling events/github/ Jira polling events/jira/ Event stream routing, workflow, and pipeline orchestration app/ (EventStreamOrchestrator, TaskExecutionService, WorkflowExecutionService, etc.) Workflow Workbench (compositions, AI turns, test runs, publishing) app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/composition/ + CompositionsResourceImpl AI Assistant sessions and engine drivers app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/assistant/ Built-in MCP servers and assistant templates app/src/main/resources/templates/ UI page or component ui/src/pages/ (workbench: ui/src/pages/workbench/) or ui/src/components/ API client functions ui/src/config/api.ts (workbench: ui/src/config/compositions.ts) Database schema app/src/main/resources/db/migration/ (V1__baseline.sql is frozen; add V<n>__… migrations)

docs.title: Java (Backend)
docs.text:
• Follow existing Quarkus patterns: @ApplicationScoped, @Inject, @ConfigProperty, @Scheduled
  • Use Panache active record for entities (no separate DAO/repository layer)
  • Use builders for configuration objects (AgentRequest.Builder, etc.)
  • Async work returns CompletableFuture
  • Keep transactional boundaries small — one @Transactional method per database operation

docs.title: TypeScript (Frontend)
docs.text:
• Use PatternFly components — don't introduce other UI libraries
  • API calls go in ui/src/config/api.ts
  • Pages go in ui/src/pages/, reusable components in ui/src/components/
  • Run npm run build (tsc -b && vite build) to catch type errors before committing

docs.title: Commit Message Format
docs.text:
Use conventional commits:

Prefix Usage feat: New feature fix: Bug fix docs: Documentation only refactor: Code restructuring without behavior change test: Adding or updating tests chore: Dependencies, tooling, CI

Examples:

feat: add Jira event source polling
fix: resolve timeout in Claude Code subprocess
docs: add extending-axiom developer guide

docs.title: Pull Request Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a branch from main: 
    git checkout -b feature/my-feature
  2. Make your changes following the conventions above
  3. Test locally:
  4. mvn test — run backend unit tests (or one test: mvn -q -pl app -am test -Dtest=MyTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false)
  5. cd ui && npm run build — type-check the frontend
  6. cd ui && npm test — run the UI unit tests
  7. ./dev.sh — verify the change works end-to-end
  8. Commit with a conventional commit message
  9. Push and open a pull request against main
  10. Describe what the PR does and why, and reference related issues (e.g. "Fixes #42")

docs.title: PR Guidelines
docs.text:
• Keep PRs focused on a single feature or fix
  • Update documentation if the change affects user-facing behavior
  • Ensure CI checks pass
  • Be responsive to review feedback

All submissions require code review before merging.

docs.title: Unit Tests
docs.text:
Standard JUnit 5 tests — run with mvn test from the project root. To run one test class in a module and build the modules it depends on:

mvn -q -pl app -am test -Dtest=MyTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false

docs.title: UI Tests
docs.text: UI unit and component tests use Vitest — run them with cd ui && npm test. They also run as part of ./build.sh -Pui.

docs.title: Integration Tests
docs.text:
Some tests start a real AI agent CLI (opencode or claude) and may consume tokens. They are tagged live-cli and excluded by default. Enable them with the live-cli-tests profile:

mvn test -Plive-cli-tests

This requires the agent CLI on your PATH and valid credentials for it.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: The documentation site uses MkDocs with the Material for MkDocs theme.

docs.title: Local Preview
docs.text:
./serve-docs.sh

This starts a local server at http://localhost:8000 with live reload.

docs.title: Adding a Page
docs.text:
1. Create a Markdown file in the appropriate docs/ subdirectory
  2. Add a nav entry in mkdocs.yml
  3. Verify the build: python3 -m mkdocs build --strict

Install the tools with pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material.

docs.title: Lineage
docs.text:
The lineage API answers "where did this come from, and what did it lead to?" for any unit of work. It follows the links described in Correlation, Tracing and the event sourcing design in both directions, so a user does not have to hop between the event, ledger, trace, workflow run, task and usage pages.

The implementation is LineageService (app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/LineageService.java), exposed by LineageResourceImpl. The UI component is LineagePanel (ui/src/components/LineagePanel.tsx).

docs.title: API
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/lineage/{entityType}/{id}?direction=both&depth=5&maxNodes=200
Parameter Values Default entityType event, trace, workflow-run, task — id UUID for event and trace, a number otherwise — direction upstream (origin), downstream (results) or both both depth Hops walked in each direction, 1–10 5 maxNodes Maximum number of nodes, 1–1000 200

An unknown entity type, a malformed ID or an out-of-range or non-numeric parameter returns 400. A root that does not exist returns 404. Both carry the JSON Error body (message, errorCode). A non-numeric depth or maxNodes fails JAX-RS parameter conversion, which JAX-RS reports as 404; LineageResourceImpl declares a @ServerExceptionMapper for NotFoundException that turns it into 400. The mapper is declared on the resource class, so it applies to this resource only.

Subjects are not a root type: a subject holds too much unrelated work to give a useful graph.

The response is a LineageGraph:

Field Meaning root Key of the root node nodes LineageNode list edges LineageEdge list truncated true when the depth or node limit cut the walk short depth, maxNodes The limits that were applied totalCostUsd Sum of the nodes' costUsd

Each LineageNode has a key (type:id, used by edges), type, id, label, status, subtype (trace type, action type, trigger or outcome item type), linkPath (UI route), costUsd, direction (root, upstream or downstream), depth (hops from the root), available and createdOn.

Node types are the four root types plus outcome: a routing outcome item that is not a task or a workflow run (for example no-match).

Each LineageEdge has from, to and relation. Edges always point downstream, from the cause to the result, whichever direction was walked:

Relation From → to triggered event → trace, event → workflow run created trace / workflow run / task → task resumed event → workflow run it resumed produced trace or event → outcome item (e.g. no-match) part-of owning workflow run → its trace (only when a trace is the root)

docs.title: Link paths
docs.text:
Type linkPath event /events/stream/{id} trace /logs/traces/{id} workflow-run /runs/{id} task /logs/tasks?taskId={id} outcome none

Tasks have no detail page; the Tasks page opens a lineage modal for ?taskId=.

docs.title: Traces and Their Owners
docs.text:
Workflow runs own their trace (workflow trace type). Such a trace is shown as its owner, not as a separate node, so a run and its trace never appear twice. Traces of any other type are trace nodes. If an owned trace's owner was deleted, the trace itself is shown.

When an owned trace is the root (GET /lineage/trace/{id}), the trace stays the root and its owner is linked upstream with part-of.

docs.title: Upstream (origin)
docs.text:
Each node has at most one origin, except workflow runs, which can also have resume events.

Node Origin task First that applies: workflowRunId → workflow run; the parent of the task's task trace node is another task's node → that task; traceId → trace or its owner; eventId → event trace Owned: its owner (part-of). Otherwise eventId → event workflow run trigger_event_id → event (triggered); each workflow_run_resume.event_id → event (resumed) event none

trigger_event_id is set for every run started from an event: by a create-workflow routing rule, manually from the event detail page, or as a re-run of a run that was started from an event. Manual runs from an event have no ledger entry or routing outcome, so they are linked only through trigger_event_id. A re-run is not linked to the run it repeats; that link exists only as the run's rerunOf:<runId> label.

docs.title: Downstream (results)
docs.text:
Node Results event traces with eventId (owned ones as their owner); workflow runs with trigger_event_id; runs resumed by the event; routing_outcome_item rows reached through event_processing_ledger → routing_outcome: workflow-run and workflow-resumed items link the run; items of outcomes without a trace link a task or an outcome node trace the work in the trace (below); items of routing_outcome rows with this trace_id (tasks and outcome nodes) workflow run tasks with workflow_run_id; the work in its trace task tasks whose task trace node is a child of this task's node (created by its agent)

"The work in a trace" is every task with that trace_id. A task whose trace node is a child of another task's node is linked to that task instead of to the trace owner.

Nodes reached from more than one place are included once, with every edge. With direction=both the upstream walk runs first, so a node found by both walks keeps upstream.

docs.title: Limits and Truncation
docs.text:
The walk is breadth-first. depth limits the hops in each direction.

  • maxNodes also bounds the rows read: every expansion query (tasks of a trace or run, traces of an event, outcome items, resumes, child tasks) uses setMaxResults with the room left in the graph plus one. When a query returns that many rows, truncated is set. This is conservative: truncated can be true when the extra row was a node that was already in the graph.
  • Every IN list is split into chunks of at most 500 IDs (LineageService.IN_CHUNK).
  • A node is added only when the other end of its edge is already in the graph, so a truncated graph has no unconnected nodes. When a new node would exceed maxNodes, it is skipped and truncated is set; edges to skipped nodes are left out, so every edge refers to a node in the response.
  • When the depth limit is reached, the last level is expanded once more: edges between nodes that are already in the graph are kept, and truncated is set if any neighbour lies beyond the limit.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
costUsd is the direct AI cost of a node, so costs can be added up without counting anything twice:

Node Sum of ai_usage.cost_usd where task task_id = the task trace, workflow run trace_id = the (run's) trace and task_id is null event, outcome no cost

docs.title: Query Batching (No N+1)
docs.text:
Every level of the walk does a fixed number of queries per node type, using IN (...) lists:

  1. Load the frontier: one query per type (stream_event, trace, workflow_run, task, routing_outcome_item). Events, tasks and workflow runs are read as projections of the label and link columns only, so event payloads, task input, output and logs, and workflow instance state are never loaded.
  2. Resolve trace owners: one query per owned trace type present.
  3. Expand: for example, for events one query each for traces, workflow runs, resumes, ledger rows, outcomes and items; for traces and owners one query each for tasks, the tasks' trace nodes and their parent nodes.

Entities found while expanding are cached, so they are not loaded again in the next level. Costs are computed once at the end with one grouped query per cost key (task, trace). The number of queries therefore depends on the depth and the node types, not on the number of nodes. LineageTest checks this with Hibernate statistics (%test.quarkus.hibernate-orm.statistics=true): a graph with 2 tasks and one with 12 tasks must use the same number of statements. It also checks that no StreamEventEntity, TaskEntity, or WorkflowRunEntity is loaded as an entity (entity load count 0), and that a trace with 30 tasks and maxNodes=5 reads at most 6 task rows (query execution row count).

docs.title: Dangling References
docs.text: All the links are soft references, and retention deletes events, traces and runs independently (see Data Retention). A reference to a missing row becomes a node with available: false, status: "unavailable", a label such as Event 3f2a... (deleted or unavailable) and no linkPath. The walk does not continue from such a node. Only a missing root returns 404.

docs.title: UI
docs.text:
LineagePanel takes an entityType and id. It has Show origin (direction=upstream) and Show results (direction=downstream) views, rendered as an indented tree from the root with a link, status and cost on each node. Nothing is fetched until the panel is opened, and each view is fetched once. A node reached twice is expanded only the first time.

Page Placement Event detail Expandable Lineage section below the tabs Workflow run detail Lineage tab Logs > Tasks, subject Tasks tab Lineage button, opens LineageModal

docs.title: Stack & Architecture
docs.text: This guide provides a high-level overview of Axiom's technology stack and runtime architecture. For the current module layout and entity model, read the source under core/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/core/entities/ and the root pom.xml — those are the authoritative reference and change more often than documentation should chase.

docs.title: Tech Stack
docs.text: Layer Technology Language Java 25 Framework Quarkus 3 Database H2 (in-memory for dev, file-based for prod) ORM Hibernate with Panache (active record pattern) Migrations Flyway Frontend TypeScript, React 19, PatternFly 6 Workflow engine and editor Apitomy Flow 3.0.2 (apitomy-flow-engine, @apitomy/flow-ui) Build (frontend) Vite Build (backend) Maven API Contract-first OpenAPI with Apitomy Codegen AI Agents Claude Code CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI (pluggable)

docs.title: Module Layout
docs.text:
The root pom.xml lists these modules:

Module Contents common/api openapi.json and the JAX-RS interfaces and beans generated from it core Entities, SSE events, filters, tracing and other shared services agents/spi The Agent SPI agents/claude-code, agents/opencode, agents/copilot Agent implementations events/core Event stream persistence and the event source SPI events/github, events/jira Event source pollers notifications/spi The notification channel SPI notifications/slack, notifications/telegram Notification channels app The Quarkus application: REST resources, workflow execution, AI Assistant sessions and the workbench ui-bundle Packages the React UI from ui/ into the JAR (only with the ui profile)

docs.title: Runtime Architecture
docs.text: The app module wires everything together using Quarkus CDI. At runtime, several scheduled pollers and services cooperate to process events and execute work.

docs.title: Event Ingestion
docs.text:
GitHubEventSourcePoller / JiraEventSourcePoller
  │  @Scheduled — polls external APIs at each event source's configured interval
  │
  ▼
EventStreamService.persistEvent()
  │  Persists a normalized StreamEventEntity, deduplicated by source event ID
  │
  ▼
stream_event table

docs.title: Subscription Evaluation and Routing
docs.text:
EventStreamOrchestrator
  │  @Scheduled — evaluates unprocessed (event, subscription) pairs each tick
  │
  ▼
SubscriptionFilterEvaluator
  │  Evaluates the subscription's EL filter expression against the event
  │
  ▼
Routing dispatch (in order, per matched subscription)
  ├── create-workflow    → finds/creates the Subject from the event ref, starts a new workflow run
  │                        (skipped and recorded if the subject already has an active run of that definition)
  └── workflow-dispatch  → broadcasts the event to every waiting run parked at a matching receive-event node

A durable processing ledger records the outcome of every (event, subscription) pair (skipped, completed, or failed), so processing survives restarts and failed routing is retried automatically on each tick.

docs.title: Task Execution
docs.text:
TaskQueuePoller
  │  @Scheduled — finds subjects with pending tasks
  │
  ▼
TaskExecutionService.executeNextTask(subjectId)
  │  Requests a lease from AgentPool using a capability string (e.g. "action:Name")
  │  Builds an AgentRequest (tools, prompt, env, MCP config)
  │  Enforces subject-level serialization (one task at a time per subject)
  │
  ▼
Agent.execute(request)
  │  Runs the agent's subprocess/HTTP call, or completes via human input
  │  Returns AgentResult (output, cost, tokens, log)
  │
  ▼
TaskEntity updated with result
AiUsageEntity created with cost/token data
AgentPool lease released

Tasks are created only by workflow action and human-task nodes. Because tasks are serialized per subject, concurrent runs of different definitions on the same subject take turns executing their tasks.

docs.title: Workflow Execution
docs.text:
WorkflowExecutionService.triggerWorkflow(subjectId, definitionId, RunRequest)
  │  A subscription's "create-workflow" rule, a manual start from an event (Event Stream),
  │  a schedule trigger, or a re-run of a failed run
  │  RunRequest carries only the optional title and labels; runs cannot be started with supplied inputs
  │  StandardInputs resolves the inputs the Start node declares (subject, event) into the initial context;
  │  the run stores the resolved inputs (subject only; the event is linked as the run's trigger event)
  │  Rejects a second active (running/waiting) run of the same definition on the subject
  │  (WorkflowRunConflictException → HTTP 409, or a recorded "skipped" for routing and schedules)
  │
  ▼
WorkflowEngine (from the shared flow-engine library)
  │  Advances the workflow instance through its node graph
  │  action / human-task nodes create TaskEntity rows via TaskExecutionService
  │  wait nodes park the instance until a resume time
  │  receive-event nodes park the instance until a matching event is dispatched
  │
  ▼
WorkflowRunEntity updated with instance state, current node, and status

docs.title: Schedule Triggers
docs.text:
WorkflowScheduleTriggerScheduler
  │  @Scheduled every axiom.workflow.schedule-poll-interval (default 30s)
  │  Claims due, enabled WorkflowScheduleTriggerEntity rows (nextRunAt <= now)
  │  Computes the next firing from the 5-field Unix cron expression (UTC)
  │
  ▼
Find or create the fixed Subject (ref "schedule:<subjectName>")
  │
  ▼
WorkflowExecutionService.triggerWorkflow(subjectId, definitionId, inputs, label trigger=schedule)
  │  lastOutcome = started | skipped (active run exists) | failed: <reason>

Schedule firing assumes a single Axiom node; there is no cross-node locking.

See Workflows for the authoring and run-time reference.

docs.title: AI Assistant Sessions
docs.text:
AssistantSessionManager
  │  Creates session from template
  │  Resolves agent type, MCP servers, allowed tools, working directory
  │  Runs optional init script
  │
  ▼
InteractiveSessionDriver (ClaudeInteractiveSessionDriver or OpenCodeInteractiveSessionDriver)
  │  ProcessBuilder or HTTP session with stream-json / SSE I/O
  │  Virtual threads: stdout reader, stderr reader, process monitor
  │
  ▼
AssistantEventParser
  │  Normalizes engine-specific events into typed SseEvent records
  │  Auto-approval rules intercept permission requests
  │
  ▼
JAX-RS SSE endpoint (per-session)
  │  Streams events to browser EventSource
  │  Full event history replay on reconnect

Live sessions are held in memory, and the agent process does not survive a server restart. Each session's events are also appended to a JSON Lines history journal (HistoryJournal), so a conversation can be shown again after a restart. Cost and token usage are accumulated per session and persisted to AiUsageEntity when the session is destroyed (only if the session had at least one turn).

Each session gets an MCP token. REST routes that only a session's own MCP server may call check the X-Axiom-Session-Token header with SessionTokenGuard and return 401 if it is missing or wrong. The token keeps sessions apart; it does not protect Axiom from the agent itself, which can read the token from its environment.

docs.title: Workflow Workbench
docs.text:
CompositionsResourceImpl (REST, /compositions)
  │
  ▼
CompositionService          → saves composition items (workflow, action types, tools) as drafts,
  │                           checks the base revision, records revisions, fires composition-item-changed
  ├── WorkbenchSessions     → binds each composition to one agent session (template "axiom-workbench")
  ├── CompositionTurns      → runs AI turns; collects workflow change sets, fires composition-turn and
  │                           composition-changeset
  ├── TurnUndo              → undoes an AI turn
  ├── CompositionValidator  → validates drafts with the same rules as publishing
  ├── CompositionTestRuns   → runs node/script action type and tool drafts, fires composition-test-run
  └── CompositionPublisher  → publishes selected drafts as one configuration pack in one transaction

The workbench agent reaches Axiom through the built-in @axiom-workbench MCP server (app/src/main/resources/templates/axiom-workbench-mcp/server.js). Its tools read the composition, write action types and tools (upsert_item, remove_item), propose workflow changes (propose_workflow_changes), validate, suggest tests (suggest_test), and look up events, runs, traces and existing components. The agent cannot run tests or change the workflow directly: workflow change sets are applied by the user's editor when the turn ends, and only the user runs tests. Calls from the MCP server to the /compositions/{compositionId}/agent/... routes are checked by SessionTokenGuard.

See Workflow Workbench for the user-facing description.

docs.title: Init Script Security
docs.text:
Session templates support optional init scripts (bash or Node.js) that run once when a session is created. These scripts run via ProcessBuilder with no sandboxing — the script runs as the same OS user as the Axiom server process, with full filesystem and network access. The only safeguard is a 60-second timeout.

Trust model: The init script content comes from session templates stored in the database (user-defined) or in built-in JSON files bundled with the application. There are currently no authentication or role-based access controls on the template CRUD endpoints. Any user with network access to Axiom can create a template containing an arbitrary init script, which will execute with server privileges when a session is created from that template. Template authors are therefore implicitly trusted with server-level code execution.

Future hardening options (not currently implemented):

  • Add role-based access control to the template CRUD endpoints so only administrators can create or modify templates with init scripts
  • Run init scripts in a container or as a restricted OS user to limit their blast radius
  • Validate or restrict init script content (e.g., command allowlists or static analysis)

docs.title: Real-Time Updates (SSE)
docs.text:
Event types include subject-updated, task-updated, workflow-updated, stream-event, trace-updated, inbox-updated, notification, activity, assistant-session-event, the workbench events composition-item-changed, composition-turn, composition-changeset and composition-test-run, and heartbeat. See core/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/core/events/SseEvent.java for the full list.

Any service fires CDI event: Event<SseEvent>
  │
  ▼
SseResource (@Observes SseEvent)
  │  Broadcasts to all connected clients
  │
  ▼
ui/src/config/sse.ts (browser)
  │  Shared connection (sse-worker.ts) with auto-reconnect
  │  UI components update reactively

docs.title: SPI / Provider Pattern
docs.text:
Extension points (AI agents, notification channels) use a consistent pattern:

  1. An SPI module defines the interface (e.g. Agent)
  2. Implementation modules provide concrete classes annotated with @ApplicationScoped
  3. A registry or CDI Instance<T> discovers implementations at runtime
  4. Selection is driven by configuration (e.g. axiom.agent.default-type=claude-code) or, for agent pool leasing, by capability matching

See the Extending Axiom guide for details.

docs.title: Panache Active Record
docs.text:
All entities extend PanacheEntity (or PanacheEntityBase for entities with non-Long primary keys) and use the active record pattern — queries are static methods on the entity class:

SubjectEntity subject = SubjectEntity.findById(id);
List<TaskEntity> tasks = TaskEntity.find("subjectId", subjectId).list();
entity.persist();

docs.title: Builder Pattern
docs.text:
Configuration objects use builders for clean, immutable construction:

  • AgentRequest.Builder — agent invocation settings
  • AgentResult.Builder — execution results

docs.title: Async Execution
docs.text: Agent execution returns CompletableFuture, keeping the scheduled pollers non-blocking.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text:
Every workflow run produces a trace — a tree of lightweight nodes recording each step. The tracing subsystem follows several key design principles:

  • TraceService lives in core — producers of traces inject it directly, avoiding circular dependencies
  • Stack-based context — TraceContext maintains a mutable node stack. Call push(nodeId) when descending into a child scope and pop() when returning. The current top of the stack is the parent for new nodes.
  • Independent transactions — all trace writes use QuarkusTransaction.requiringNew(), so trace data persists even if the caller's transaction rolls back
  • Non-fatal — all trace operations are wrapped in try/catch. Tracing failures never interrupt the main pipeline
  • SSE broadcast — every trace mutation fires SseEvent.traceUpdated(traceId) for real-time UI updates
  • UUID primary key — TraceEntity uses a UUID PK. The trace ID doubles as the correlation identifier threaded through environment variables and API callbacks.

See the Tracing developer guide for the full data model, service API, and REST endpoint reference.

docs.title: Scheduled Pollers
docs.text: All background processing uses Quarkus @Scheduled with concurrentExecution = SKIP to prevent overlapping executions, including the event source pollers, the event stream orchestrator, the task queue poller, the workflow wait scheduler, and the workflow schedule trigger scheduler.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text:
Axiom's tracing subsystem records a hierarchical tree of every step that occurs during a workflow run. Each trace is a tree of lightweight trace nodes that reference more detailed records elsewhere in the system, keeping nodes small and fast to query while providing full drill-down capability.

This guide covers the data model, service API, REST endpoints, and how to instrument new pipeline stages with tracing.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
• Lightweight breadcrumbs — trace nodes carry a summary, status, and timing, but delegate detail to referenced entities (activity logs, tasks, tool executions, etc.)
  • Non-fatal — all trace operations are wrapped in exception handlers. Tracing never interrupts the main pipeline.
  • Independent transactions — trace writes use QuarkusTransaction.requiringNew() so data persists even if the caller's transaction rolls back
  • Real-time — every trace mutation fires an SSE event for live UI updates
  • Correlation by UUID — TraceEntity uses a UUID primary key that doubles as the correlation identifier threaded through environment variables and API callbacks

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text: Trace entities live in core/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/core/entities/. Read TraceEntity.java, TraceNodeEntity.java, and ToolExecutionEntity.java directly for the exact field list — the concepts below are what you need to work with the API and build new instrumentation.

docs.title: TraceEntity
docs.text:
The root of a complete execution trace (table trace). It uses a UUID primary key (traceId) instead of the standard auto-increment Long used elsewhere, because that ID doubles as the correlation identifier threaded through subprocess environment variables and API callbacks. Each trace has a traceType (see below), a status (in-progress, completed, or failed), a human-readable summary, optional eventId/subjectId associations, and start/completion timestamps. eventId is the UUID of the originating stream_event row. It is a soft reference (no foreign key): stream events are purged by the event retention policy while traces are retained, so the UUID may outlive its event.

Every trace is currently of type workflow, created when a workflow run starts (manually on a subject, manually from a stream event, by a create-workflow routing rule, by a schedule trigger, or as a re-run of a failed run). Tasks created by the run's action and human-task nodes, and tool calls made by their agents, are recorded as nodes of the run's trace.

docs.title: TraceNodeEntity
docs.text: A single step/span within a trace tree (table trace_node). Nodes form a parent-child tree via parentNodeId (null for the root node). Each node has a nodeType, a status, a summary, start/completion timestamps with a computed durationMs, and an optional entityType + entityId pair that points to a more detailed record elsewhere in the system. entityId is stored as a string (VARCHAR) so it can hold either a numeric ID (e.g. task, activity-log) or a UUID (e.g. event, which references a stream event).

docs.title: Node Types
docs.text:
Node type strings are chosen by whichever service creates the node — there is no enum, so treat this as the currently observed set rather than an exhaustive contract:

Node Type Meaning Typical Entity Reference workflow Workflow run started (root node of a workflow trace) workflow-run task A workflow step: a task created by an action or human-task node, or a run parked at a wait or receive-event node task, workflow-wait, or workflow-event-subscription tool-execution An MCP tool was invoked tool-execution

docs.title: Entity Types
docs.text:
The entityType field determines which entity table the entityId references:

Entity Type Referenced Entity Detail Content event StreamEventEntity Raw normalized event payload activity-log ActivityLogEntity Log entry with type, summary, execution log task TaskEntity Task details — action type, agent, status, output tool-execution ToolExecutionEntity Full JSON input and output ai-usage AiUsageEntity Token counts, cost, model workflow-run WorkflowRunEntity Run status, current node, times, definition and subject names workflow-wait WorkflowWaitEntity Wait type, resume time, status (waiting/resolved/cancelled), run workflow-event-subscription WorkflowEventSubscriptionEntity Awaited event type, status, run, subject

GET /traces/{traceId}/nodes/{nodeId} resolves these into the node's detail object (see TraceResourceImpl.resolveDetail). An unknown entity type, a malformed ID or a deleted record yields the node with a null detail. The one exception is workflow waits and event subscriptions: their rows are deleted when the parked node resumes, so the detail is rebuilt from the trace node and its workflow run, with status resolved (node completed) or cancelled. The event that satisfied a subscription is not recorded, so matchedEventId is always null. The workflow-run detail omits the engine's instanceState.

docs.title: ToolExecutionEntity
docs.text: Detailed record of an MCP tool invocation (table tool_execution), storing the full JSON input and output for debugging. Referenced by trace nodes via entityType="tool-execution". Each record carries the associated traceId, the tool name, its JSON input/output, a status, and a duration.

docs.title: TraceService API
docs.text:
TraceService is the central service for creating and managing traces. It lives in the core module so any module can use it without circular dependencies.

Location: core/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/core/tracing/TraceService.java

docs.title: createTrace()
docs.text:
Creates a new trace and its root node in a single transaction, then fires an SSE event.

public TraceContext createTrace(
    String traceType,        // e.g. "workflow"
    String summary,          // human-readable trace description
    UUID eventId,            // associated stream event ID (nullable)
    Long subjectId,          // associated subject ID (nullable)
    String rootNodeType,     // node type for the root node
    String rootNodeSummary,  // summary for the root node
    String rootEntityType,   // entity type for the root node (nullable)
    Long rootEntityId        // entity ID for the root node (nullable)
)

Returns a TraceContext with the root node already pushed onto the stack.

docs.title: addNode()
docs.text:
Adds a child node under the current parent (top of the context stack).

public Long addNode(
    TraceContext ctx,   // current trace context
    String nodeType,    // node type identifier
    String status,      // initial status (e.g. "in-progress", "completed")
    String summary,     // human-readable description
    String entityType,  // referenced entity type (nullable)
    Long entityId       // referenced entity ID (nullable)
)

Returns the new node's ID. The parent is determined by ctx.currentParentNodeId().

To reference a UUID-keyed entity (such as a stream event, entityType="event"), use addUuidEntityNode(), which has the same parameters except that entityId is a UUID:

Long nodeId = traceService.addUuidEntityNode(traceCtx, "event-received", "completed",
    "Event received: " + event.type, "event", event.id);

docs.title: completeNode()
docs.text:
Marks a node as completed with a final status and calculated duration. Has two overloads:

// Basic completion
public void completeNode(Long nodeId, String status)

// Completion with entity reference (when entity isn't known at creation time)
public void completeNode(Long nodeId, String status,
    String entityType, Long entityId)

docs.title: completeTrace()
docs.text:
Marks the trace itself as completed or failed.

public void completeTrace(UUID traceId, String status)

docs.title: Trace lifecycle rules
docs.text:
Every unit of work ends with exactly one trace in a final state (completed or failed). No trace or task node may stay in-progress once its work item is final, and a trace is never completed twice.

Work item Who completes the trace Workflow run WorkflowExecutionService when the run is terminal (completed, failed, or cancelled), including runs that finish synchronously on start

TaskTraceFinalizer is used by both the agent and script task paths (including failTask). It always completes the task's task node and never completes a workflow-owned trace — the workflow run owns its trace lifecycle.

docs.title: Workflow traces and events
docs.text:
• A run started from a stream event gets a workflow trace with eventId set to the stream event, so the trace appears in GET /traces?filterEventId=.... This covers runs started by a create-workflow routing rule, manual runs started from the event (POST /stream/events/{eventId}/runs), and re-runs of a failed run that was started from an event. All of them go through EventStreamOrchestrator.startRunFromEvent. For a routing rule, the routing outcome's traceId is the run's trace. Manual runs from an event have no ledger entry or routing outcome.
  • Runs started manually on a subject or by a schedule trigger have no eventId. A re-run of such a run has none either.
  • A re-run (POST /workflow/runs/{runId}/rerun) is a new run with its own trace. It is linked to the original run only by its rerunOf:<runId> label, not through the trace.
  • A create-workflow rule that is skipped because the subject already has an active run of the definition creates no run and no trace.
  • When a stream event resumes a run parked at a receive-event step, the receive-event task node (entity type workflow-event-subscription) is completed and its summary gets "— resumed by event ". The workflow-resumed routing outcome item's trace_node_id points to that node, and a workflow_run_resume row records the event (see the event sourcing design).

docs.title: TraceContext
docs.text:
TraceContext is a mutable context object threaded through workflow and task processing. It tracks the current position in the trace tree using an internal stack.

Location: core/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/core/tracing/TraceContext.java

Method Description UUID traceId() Returns the trace UUID Long currentParentNodeId() Returns the top of the stack (current parent) void push(Long nodeId) Pushes a node onto the stack, making it the current parent Long pop() Pops the current parent, returning to the previous level

docs.title: Push/Pop Pattern
docs.text:
When descending into a child scope, push the new node onto the stack so that any nodes created within that scope become its children. Pop when returning to the parent level.

// Create a parent node
Long parentId = traceService.addNode(traceCtx, "my-step",
    "in-progress", "Doing something", null, null);
traceCtx.push(parentId);

try {
    // Any nodes created here become children of parentId
    traceService.addNode(traceCtx, "my-child-step",
        "completed", "Child step", "activity-log", logId);
} finally {
    traceCtx.pop();
    traceService.completeNode(parentId, "completed");
}

docs.title: REST API Reference
docs.text: All trace endpoints are defined in the OpenAPI specification at common/api/src/main/resources/openapi.json and implemented in app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/rest/TraceResourceImpl.java.

docs.title: List Traces
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/traces

Returns a paginated list of traces with optional filtering.

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description page integer 1 Page number (1-indexed) limit integer 20 Page size filterTraceType string — Filter by trace type (currently always "workflow") filterStatus string — Filter by status (comma-separated, e.g. "in-progress,completed") filterEventId string (UUID) — Filter by stream event ID (400 if not a valid UUID) filterSubjectId integer — Filter by subject ID

Response: TraceSearchResults

{
  "items": [
    {
      "traceId": "a1b2c3d4-...",
      "traceType": "workflow",
      "status": "completed",
      "summary": "Workflow: Auto-Label New Issues",
      "eventId": null,
      "subjectId": 7,
      "startedOn": "2026-06-29T10:00:00Z",
      "completedOn": "2026-06-29T10:00:05Z"
    }
  ],
  "totalCount": 1,
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 20
}

docs.title: Convenience: List Traces by Entity
docs.text:
The API also provides a convenience endpoint that returns the traces for a specific subject as a JSON array of Trace objects (not paginated):

GET /api/v1/subjects/{subjectId}/traces

This is equivalent to calling GET /traces?filterSubjectId=..., but are more convenient when you already have the entity ID.

docs.title: Get Trace Detail

GET /api/v1/traces/{traceId}

Returns a trace and all of its nodes.

Path Parameters:

Response: TraceDetail

    "startedOn": "2026-06-29T10:00:00Z",

    {
      "id": 1,
      "traceId": "a1b2c3d4-...",
      "parentNodeId": null,
      "nodeType": "workflow",
      "status": "completed",
      "summary": "Workflow: Auto-Label New Issues",
      "startedOn": "2026-06-29T10:00:00Z",
      "completedOn": "2026-06-29T10:00:00Z",

      "entityType": null,
      "entityId": null
    },
    {
      "id": 2,

docs.title: Get Trace Node Detail
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/traces/{traceId}/nodes/{nodeId}

Returns a trace node with its resolved entity detail. The detail object's structure depends on the node's entityType.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Type Description traceId string (UUID) The trace UUID nodeId integer The node ID

Response: TraceNodeDetail

{
  "node": {
    "id": 5,
    "traceId": "a1b2c3d4-...",
    "parentNodeId": 3,
    "nodeType": "tool-execution",
    "status": "completed",
    "summary": "Tool: github_list_issues",
    "durationMs": 1200,
    "entityType": "tool-execution",
    "entityId": "7"
  },
  "detail": {
    "toolName": "github_list_issues",
    "toolInput": "{\"repo\": \"owner/repo\", \"state\": \"open\"}",
    "toolOutput": "[{\"number\": 1, \"title\": \"Bug report\"}]",
    "status": "completed",
    "durationMs": 1200
  }
}

docs.title: Create Tool Call
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/traces/tool-calls

Creates a new tool-call trace node and its associated ToolExecutionEntity. Called by MCP tool wrappers during task execution.

Request Body: ToolCallRequest

{
  "traceId": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "parentNodeId": 3,
  "toolName": "github_list_issues",
  "toolInput": "{\"repo\": \"owner/repo\", \"state\": \"open\"}"
}
Field Type Required Description traceId string (UUID) Yes The parent trace UUID parentNodeId integer No Parent node ID for tree nesting toolName string Yes Name of the MCP tool being invoked toolInput string No Tool input as JSON

Response: ToolCallCreated

{
  "nodeId": 5
}

docs.title: Complete Tool Call
docs.text:
PUT /api/v1/traces/tool-calls/{nodeId}

Completes a tool-call trace node with the execution result.

Path Parameters:

Parameter Type Description nodeId integer The trace node ID returned by the create call

Request Body: ToolCallCompletion

{
  "toolOutput": "[{\"number\": 1, \"title\": \"Bug report\"}]",
  "status": "completed",
  "durationMs": 1200
}
Field Type Required Description toolOutput string No Tool output as JSON status string No Final status ("completed" or "failed") durationMs integer No Execution duration in milliseconds

docs.title: Instrumenting New Pipeline Stages
docs.text: To add tracing to a new pipeline stage or service:

docs.title: Step 1: Inject TraceService
docs.text:
@Inject
TraceService traceService;

docs.title: Step 2: Create a Trace or Add a Node
docs.text:
If your code is the entry point for a new kind of traced work (like WorkflowExecutionService), create a new trace:

TraceContext traceCtx = traceService.createTrace(
    "my-pipeline",
    "Processing something: " + description,
    eventId, subjectId,   // eventId is the stream event UUID (nullable)
    "my-root-node", "Root: " + description,
    null, null);

If your code runs within an existing trace (like task execution within a workflow run), receive the TraceContext as a parameter and add nodes to it:

Long nodeId = traceService.addNode(traceCtx, "my-step", "in-progress",
    "Doing something important", null, null);

docs.title: Step 3: Push/Pop for Child Scopes
docs.text:
If your node will have child nodes, push it onto the stack:

traceCtx.push(nodeId);
try {
    // child nodes created here become children of nodeId
    doWork(traceCtx);
} finally {
    traceCtx.pop();
}

docs.title: Step 4: Complete Nodes and the Trace
docs.text:
// Complete a node
traceService.completeNode(nodeId, "completed");

// Complete a node and set its entity reference
traceService.completeNode(nodeId, "completed", "activity-log", logEntry.id);

// Complete the trace
traceService.completeTrace(traceCtx.traceId(), "completed");

docs.title: Step 5: Pass Correlation Data to Subprocesses
docs.text:
If your stage launches a subprocess that should report tool calls back to the trace, inject the trace correlation data as environment variables:

Map<String, String> env = new HashMap<>();
env.put("AXIOM_TRACE_ID", traceCtx.traceId().toString());
env.put("AXIOM_PARENT_NODE_ID", String.valueOf(nodeId));

The subprocess (or its MCP tool wrapper) reads these variables and calls back to POST /api/v1/traces/tool-calls and PUT /api/v1/traces/tool-calls/{nodeId}.

docs.title: Non-Fatal Pattern
docs.text:
Always wrap trace operations in try/catch when called from the main pipeline:

Long nodeId = null;
if (traceCtx != null) {
    try {
        nodeId = traceService.addNode(traceCtx, "my-step", "in-progress",
            "Description", null, null);
        traceCtx.push(nodeId);
    } catch (Exception e) {
        LOG.warnf(e, "Failed to add trace node");
    }
}

// ... do the actual work ...

if (traceCtx != null && nodeId != null) {
    try {
        traceCtx.pop();
        traceService.completeNode(nodeId, "completed");
    } catch (Exception e) {
        LOG.warnf(e, "Failed to complete trace node");
    }
}

docs.title: MCP Tool Call Integration
docs.text:
When Axiom generates MCP server configurations for AI agent tasks, it includes the trace correlation environment variables (AXIOM_TRACE_ID and AXIOM_PARENT_NODE_ID). The generated MCP tool wrappers use these to register tool calls as trace nodes:

AI Agent starts task
  │
  ├─ Axiom sets AXIOM_TRACE_ID and AXIOM_PARENT_NODE_ID in subprocess env
  │
  ▼
MCP Tool Wrapper executes
  │
  ├─ Reads AXIOM_TRACE_ID and AXIOM_PARENT_NODE_ID from environment
  ├─ POST /api/v1/traces/tool-calls  →  receives nodeId
  ├─ Executes the actual tool
  └─ PUT /api/v1/traces/tool-calls/{nodeId}  →  sends output + status

This flow is implemented in TaskExecutionService, which looks up the trace node ID for the current task and injects it as AXIOM_PARENT_NODE_ID so tool calls become children of the correct node in the tree.

If the trace callback fails (network error, missing trace, etc.), the tool execution continues normally — tracing is best-effort and never blocks work.

docs.title: Correlation
docs.text:
The trace ID is also Axiom's correlation ID. Activity log rows, AI usage rows, tasks and workflow runs store the trace ID of the work that produced them, and agents can join their caller's trace through the X-Axiom-Trace-Id and X-Axiom-Parent-Node-Id headers. See Correlation by Trace ID.

Server log lines also carry the trace ID (MDC key traceId), so a trace can be followed in the logs with grep traceId=<uuid>. See Correlation by Trace ID.

docs.title: UI Development
docs.text: This guide covers the frontend architecture, development workflow, and patterns used in the Axiom React UI.

docs.title: API Layer (api.ts)
docs.text:
Backend communication goes through ui/src/config/api.ts. The Workflow Workbench API (/compositions) has its own client in ui/src/config/compositions.ts. api.ts contains:

  • TypeScript interfaces for every API entity (Subject, Task, ActionType, ToolDefinition, etc.)
  • Fetch functions for every REST endpoint (fetchSubjects(), createTool(), updateActionType(), etc.)
  • Pagination type — SearchResults<T> with items, totalCount, page, limit

docs.title: Base URL Resolution
docs.text:
export function getApiBaseUrl(): string {
    // window.AXIOM_API_URL if defined, otherwise "" (same origin;
    // in development the Vite proxy forwards /api to the backend)
}

const API = `${getApiBaseUrl()}/api/v1`;

docs.title: API Function Pattern
docs.text:
Functions follow the same pattern:

export async function fetchSubjects(
    page = 1, limit = 20, filterName?: string, filterActive?: boolean, filterLabels?: string
): Promise<SearchResults<Subject>> {
    const params = new URLSearchParams();
    params.set("page", String(page));
    params.set("limit", String(limit));
    if (filterName) params.set("filterName", filterName);
    if (filterActive !== undefined) params.set("filterActive", String(filterActive));
    if (filterLabels) params.set("filterLabels", filterLabels);
    const response = await fetch(`${API}/subjects?${params}`);
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Failed to fetch subjects: ${response.status}`);
    return response.json();
}

When adding a new API function, follow this pattern — plain fetch(), check response.ok, return typed JSON. Use extractErrorMessage() when the server returns a useful error message (for example a 422 validation error).

docs.title: SSE System
docs.text: Axiom uses Server-Sent Events for real-time UI updates (task status changes, new activity log entries, workflow run updates, etc.).

docs.title: Frontend: SseClient (sse.ts)
docs.text:
A class-based singleton (sseClient) managing a persistent EventSource connection:

  • When the browser supports SharedWorker, one worker (sse-worker.ts) owns the connection and broadcasts events to all tabs, so there is exactly one SSE connection per browser; otherwise each tab opens its own
  • Auto-reconnects with exponential backoff (1 second to 30 seconds max)
  • Parses nested JSON (data serialized as a string within JSON)
  • Subscriber pattern — components subscribe to events and receive callbacks; subscribeSession() delivers the events of one AI Assistant session
// In App.tsx:
sseClient.connect();

// In a component:
const unsub = sseClient.subscribe((event) => {
    if (event.type === "task-updated") {
        // refresh data
    }
});

docs.title: Backend: SseResource.java
docs.text:
• Endpoint: GET /api/v1/sse (produces text/event-stream)
  • Maintains a map of active client emitters
  • Observes CDI SseEvent events and broadcasts to all connected clients
  • Any service can fire an SSE event with one of the SseEvent factory methods, e.g. sseEvents.fire(SseEvent.traceUpdated(traceId))
  • Event types include subject-updated, task-updated, workflow-updated, stream-event, assistant-session-event and the workbench events composition-item-changed, composition-turn, composition-changeset and composition-test-run

docs.title: 1. Create the Page Component
docs.text:
Create a new file in ui/src/pages/:

// ui/src/pages/MyFeaturePage.tsx
import { PageSection, Title } from "@patternfly/react-core";

export function MyFeaturePage() {
    return (
        <PageSection>
            <Title headingLevel="h1" size="lg">My Feature</Title>
            {/* page content */}
        </PageSection>
    );
}

docs.title: 2. Add the Route
docs.text:
In App.tsx, import the component and add a <Route>:

import { MyFeaturePage } from "./pages/MyFeaturePage";

// Inside <Routes>:
<Route path="/my-feature" element={<MyFeaturePage />} />

In AppSidebar.tsx, add a <NavItem> (inside a <NavExpandable> if it belongs to a group such as Events or Components):

<NavItem
    isActive={location.pathname.startsWith("/my-feature")}
    onClick={() => navigate("/my-feature")}
>
    My Feature
</NavItem>

docs.title: 4. Add API Functions
docs.text: In api.ts, add TypeScript interfaces and fetch functions for any new endpoints.
