docs.title: Development Workflow
docs.text:
1. Start the UI dev server: cd ui && npm run dev (or use ./dev.sh which starts both)
  2. The Vite dev server runs on port 9191 and proxies /api requests to the backend on port 9090
  3. Hot module replacement (HMR) updates the browser instantly when you save a file
  4. Run npm run build (which runs tsc -b && vite build) to type-check before committing
  5. Run npm test (Vitest, configured in vitest.config.ts) to run the UI unit and component tests. Tests live next to the code they cover as *.test.ts(x) files (e.g. pages/WorkflowRunsPage.test.tsx). ./build.sh -Pui builds the UI and runs these tests as part of the Maven build

docs.title: Upgrading and Backups
docs.text: Axiom migrates its own database schema automatically on startup (see Database & Migrations), but a schema migration is not the same thing as a safe, reversible upgrade. This guide covers what changes across versions, what to back up, and how to restore an instance.

docs.title: What a Version Upgrade Can Change
docs.text: Schema changes ship as incremental Flyway migrations (see Database & Migrations) that run automatically at startup. They are not designed to be rolled back: review the migration files between your current version and the target version before upgrading a production instance, and take a backup (see below) first. There is no automatic downgrade path.

docs.title: Upgrading From Axiom 2.x
docs.text:
Axiom 3.0 is a clean break from 2.x: it starts from a new database schema and cannot use a 2.x database. If Axiom 3 finds a database created by 2.x (or older) it refuses to start, with a message telling you to remove the old data. To upgrade:

  1. Stop Axiom 2.x.
  2. Back up ~/.axiom (or move it aside) if you want to keep the old data for reference.
  3. Delete the database directory, ~/.axiom/data/ (or <axiom.home>/data/ if you set axiom.home).
  4. Start Axiom 3. It creates a new, empty database.
  5. Recreate your configuration: event sources, secrets, action types, tools, workflows and subscriptions. Many 2.x concepts were removed or reworked (see the 3.0.0 release notes), so 2.x configuration packs are not expected to import cleanly; the Workflow Workbench is the quickest way to rebuild workflows. The 3.0.0 release notes list what was removed and renamed.

Secrets are stored in the database, so they must be re-entered. The rest of ~/.axiom (the encryption key, workspaces and session directories) can stay; old 2.x subject workspaces are no longer referenced and can be removed.

docs.title: What Makes Up a Full Backup
docs.text:
A configuration pack (Settings > Configuration Packs) exports action types, tools, toolsets, MCP servers, session templates, event sources, subscriptions, and workflow definitions as JSON. It is not a full instance backup. A configuration pack does not include:

  • Subjects, tasks, thread entries, or activity history
  • Workflow runs and their state
  • The stream event history and processing ledger
  • Secrets (secret values are never exported by the API)
  • The AI usage/cost history
  • Workbench compositions and their unpublished drafts (only published workflows, action types and tools can be exported)

To fully back up and restore an Axiom instance, you need all of the following, taken together at the same point in time. ~/.axiom is the default Axiom home (axiom.home); if you override it, every location below moves with it, including the database:

Item Location Notes Database <axiom.home>/data/axiom.mv.db (and related H2 files) Only meaningful with persist or prod profiles, which use a file-based database Encryption key <axiom.home>/secret.key Generated automatically on first startup. Secret values in the database are encrypted with this key — without it, encrypted secrets cannot be decrypted, even by restoring the database. Subject workspaces <axiom.home>/workspaces/ (or axiom.workspace.root if overridden) Working directories (subject-<id>) backing each subject Assistant session directories (optional) <axiom.home>/assistant/sessions/ Running agent processes do not survive a restart. Workbench composition session directories are kept and hold the conversation history that the workbench restores after a restart; other stale session directories are removed at startup

Stop the Axiom process before copying the database files to ensure a consistent snapshot (H2 does not support online hot backups of the file store used here).

docs.title: Restoring
docs.text:
1. Install the target Axiom version.
  2. Restore <axiom.home>/data/ and <axiom.home>/secret.key from backup together — the encryption key must match the database it was used to encrypt secrets for.
  3. Restore <axiom.home>/workspaces/ if subject workspaces are needed.
  4. Start Axiom with the persist or prod profile. Restore into the same or a newer 3.x version than the one that created the backup; newer versions migrate the restored database at startup.

docs.title: Configuration Packs Are for Sharing, Not Disaster Recovery
docs.text: Use configuration packs to move a known-good set of tools, action types, event sources, subscriptions, and workflows between instances (e.g. staging to production), or to version-control your configuration outside the database. Don't rely on them as your only backup mechanism — they intentionally exclude runtime history and secret values.

docs.title: Workflow Human-Task Nodes
docs.text: Axiom workflows support human-task nodes, which pause execution until a user completes a form through the Inbox UI. When the engine reaches a human-task node, it parks the workflow instance in WAITING and creates an inbox task with status AwaitingInput. A user completes the task via the unified completion endpoint, and Axiom resumes the workflow with the answers merged into context.

docs.title: Authoring a Human-Task Node
docs.text:
A human-task node in a Flow workflow definition configures these things under config:

  1. Title (title, optional) — an EL expression for the task title shown in the Inbox, for example 'Review ' += context.subject.ref. When it is absent or fails, the node's name is used.
  2. Description (description, optional) — text shown with the task.
  3. Inputs — mapped to read-only details displayed to the user for context.
  4. Outputs — define the completion form fields (outputSchema) that the user fills in.

docs.title: Inputs (Display Context)
docs.text:
A human-task node's inputs is a map from a display name to an EL expression. Each expression is evaluated against the current workflow context, and the result is shown in the Inbox task's details section as a read-only value under its name.

Example (from templates/assistant-reference/examples/workflows/issue-triage.json):

{
  "inputs": {
    "issue": "context.subject.ref",
    "severity": "context.severity"
  }
}

At run time, if the workflow context contains { ref: "https://github.com/apitomy/axiom/issues/7", severity: "high" }, the inbox task's details show issue and severity with those values. Values that are not strings are shown as their string form.

docs.title: Outputs (Completion Form)
docs.text:
A human-task node's outputs list declares the form fields the user must complete. Each output becomes a field in the task's completion form, with its type determining the input widget and validation.

Each output has a name and a semantic type (string, number, boolean or object), and may be marked required. Axiom also supports optional rich metadata on each output:

property purpose default if omitted label Human-readable field label The output's name verbatim description Help text shown below the field Empty widget UI control (text, textarea, number, checkbox, select) text defaultValue Pre-filled value when the form loads Empty options List of { label, value } choices (for the select widget only) Empty array contextKey Context key the answer is stored under The output's name

Example (in Flow authoring UI):

{
  "outputs": [
    {
      "name": "approved",
      "type": "boolean",
      "label": "Approve this change?",
      "widget": "checkbox"
    },
    {
      "name": "comments",
      "type": "string",
      "label": "Review comments",
      "description": "Optional notes for the team",
      "widget": "textarea"
    }
  ]
}

When metadata is omitted, Axiom uses these defaults (WorkflowHumanTaskMapper.toOutputSchema):

  • label defaults to the output's name verbatim (e.g., an output named approvedByManager shows the label approvedByManager).
  • The form field's control comes from widget only; it is not inferred from type. An output without a widget is a text field, so set widget to checkbox for a boolean output and to number for a number output. The widget value boolean is also accepted as checkbox.
  • A node with no outputs gets no outputSchema, and the task takes a free-form response.

docs.title: Task Creation
docs.text:
When a running workflow reaches a human-task node:

  1. The Flow engine transitions the workflow instance to WAITING.
  2. Axiom creates an inbox task (WorkflowExecutionService.createHumanTaskForNode) with:
  3. the task name (actionType) = the evaluated title, or the node's name when there is none
  4. humanContext.title = the node's name, humanContext.description = the node's description (if provided), and humanContext.details = the node's resolved inputs
  5. outputSchema = the completion form derived from the node's outputs
  6. status = AwaitingInput
  7. traceId = the run's trace; a task trace node with summary Human task: <title> is added to it

docs.title: Task Completion
docs.text:
A user completes the task through the unified completion endpoint:

The request body is a flat JSON object whose keys are the output names declared by the node (there is no answers wrapper):

POST /api/v1/inbox/{taskId}/complete
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "approved": true,
  "comments": "Looks good to me"
}

This endpoint is used by:

  • The Inbox page (global task list)
  • The Subject detail page (subject-scoped task list)

On completion, Axiom:

Only a task with status AwaitingInput can be completed; any other task returns HTTP 404.

  1. Validates the submission against the task's outputSchema before completion — missing required fields or wrong-typed values are rejected with HTTP 400.
  2. Coerces the accepted answers to the node's declared semantic types (string, number, boolean, object) so downstream edge conditions compare correctly.
  3. Merges the coerced answers into the workflow's context, each under its output's contextKey (or its name when no contextKey is set).
  4. Resumes the workflow by calling the Flow engine's completeNode with the answers.

Downstream nodes and edge conditions can reference the answers via their keys (e.g., approved, comments).

docs.title: Supported Node Types
docs.text:
Axiom workflows currently support the following node types:

  • start — workflow entry point (see Workflow Input Contract)
  • end — workflow termination
  • action — runs an action type (AI agent, Node.js or script)
  • human-task — pauses for user input (this doc)
  • wait — pauses the instance for a fixed duration before resuming automatically
  • receive-event — pauses the instance until a matching stream event is dispatched to it by a subscription's workflow-dispatch routing rule

For the full authoring and run-time reference across all node types, see Workflows.

docs.title: Example: Approval Workflow
docs.text:
A workflow that waits for manager approval before deploying:

  1. Start node — declares the standard input subject (see Workflow Input Contract).
  2. Action node — runs a build script, outputs buildArtifact.
  3. Human-task node (Manager Approval) —
  4. Inputs: { "ref": "context.subject.ref", "buildArtifact": "context.buildArtifact" } (shown as read-only context)
  5. Outputs: 
    [
  { "name": "approved", "type": "boolean", "required": true, "label": "Approve deployment?",
    "widget": "checkbox" },
  { "name": "notes", "type": "string", "widget": "textarea", "description": "Optional comments" }
]
  6. Conditional edge — if approved == true, advance to Deploy node; else, advance to Notify Owner node.
  7. Action node (Deploy) — uses buildArtifact from step 2.

When the workflow reaches step 3, a manager sees a task titled "Manager Approval" with read-only details showing the subject ref and build artifact, plus a checkbox for approval and a textarea for notes. After they submit, the workflow continues based on their approved answer.

docs.title: Workflow Input Contract
docs.text: A workflow's Start node declares the inputs the workflow needs. Axiom provides a fixed set of standard inputs and puts into a new run's context exactly the standard inputs the Start node declares. The registry of standard inputs is io.apitomy.axiom.app.StandardInputs.

docs.title: Standard inputs
docs.text:
name type presence value subject object always the run's subject: id (number), name, type, ref, refSource, repository (strings); a field with no value is null event object only when the run was started from a stream event the event envelope: id, type, source, eventSourceId, ref, timestamp, actor, payload

A run is started from a stream event (all through EventStreamOrchestrator.startRunFromEvent) by:

  • a subscription's create-workflow routing rule;
  • Run workflow… on the event detail page (POST /stream/events/{eventId}/runs);
  • a re-run of a run that was itself started from an event (POST /workflow/runs/{runId}/rerun).

Runs started by a schedule trigger, or as a re-run of such a run, have no event.

docs.title: Declaring inputs
docs.text:
A Start node declares its inputs under config.inputs (a list of { name, type, required, description }). WorkflowContentRules.startInputViolation checks the declarations at publish and in workbench validation (propose_workflow_changes). It rejects an input when:

  1. its name is not a valid identifier;
  2. its name is not a standard input name (the message lists the standard inputs);
  3. its type is set and differs from the standard type (object for both);
  4. it declares a default value — Axiom provides standard inputs itself.

Either input may be required. Requiring event is how a workflow says it must be started from an event.

New workflows (from the workbench and Components → Workflows) are scaffolded by WorkflowTemplates.emptyWorkflow with subject and event both declared and required. A workflow run by a schedule trigger must remove event or make it optional.

docs.title: Run creation
docs.text:
WorkflowExecutionService.startRun resolves the declared inputs with StandardInputs.resolve:

  • only declared inputs are put into the initial context; undeclared standard inputs are not provided;
  • a declared optional input that is not available is absent from the context;
  • a declared required input that is not available stops the run before it is created, with the message Cannot start workflow "<name>": required input(s) not available: <names>.

How that failure surfaces depends on how the run was started:

started by outcome when a required input is unavailable re-run (POST /workflow/runs/{runId}/rerun) HTTP 400 with the message schedule trigger the firing records lastOutcome failed: <message>, for example failed: Cannot start workflow "<name>": required input(s) not available: event subscription routing, Run workflow… on an event cannot happen: both inputs are always available

A re-run resolves its inputs again from the subject's current state and the original run's triggering event; it does not copy the original run's inputs.

The run's stored inputs (shown in the Inputs field of the run's Overview tab and returned by axiom_get_workflow_run) are the resolved standard inputs without event; the event is linked to the run as its trigger instead.

docs.title: Reading inputs
docs.text:
Expressions read standard inputs from the run context, for example context.subject.ref, context.subject.repository or context.event.payload.pull_request.number.

Reading a standard input that the Start node does not declare (for example context.subject without declaring subject) is not reported, because a node output with that name may legitimately provide the key. Standard input names are not reserved.

docs.title: Shadowing warning
docs.text:
Workflow validation (ConfigItemValidationService.validateWorkflow, which backs the workbench's propose_workflow_changes problems and assistant item validation) reports a warning with code SHADOWS_WORKFLOW_INPUT when a node would write a context key equal to the name of a declared Start input, for example Output 'event' of node 'Review' overwrites the workflow input 'event' for later nodes. The check is WorkflowContentRules.shadowProblems and does not block publish. It considers these output keys:

  • an action node's config.outputs (by their context key);
  • the declared outputs of the node's action type that the node does not rename;
  • a human-task node's form fields (by their context key);
  • a receive-event node's output mapping context keys.

sdk: node results are not declared anywhere and are not checked.

docs.title: Passing context to action types
docs.text: Action types never read the run context directly. Each action node maps values into the action type's declared inputs, for example context.subject.ref into a ref input. Every required action-type input must be mapped, mapping an undeclared input name is an error, and an unmapped optional input is simply absent. See Inputs, Placeholders and Mappings.

docs.title: Action type inputs and outputs at run time
docs.text:
When a workflow task runs, TaskExecutionService checks the task's resolved inputs before it runs the action type:

  1. InputBindingResolver.missingRequiredInputs lists required declared inputs with no value (absent, null or a blank string). If any are missing, the task fails with Missing required input(s): ....
  2. ActionTypeIoValidator.validate checks each supplied value against its declared type. A mismatch fails the task with Input validation failed: ....

When the task completes, WorkflowExecutionService validates its outputs against the action type's declared outputs with the same validator. A mismatch fails the task and the node with Output validation failed: .... Workbench test runs (DraftTestRunner) use the same validator for inputs and outputs.

ActionTypeIoValidator accepts a value that already has the declared type or can be converted without loss:

Type Accepted values string strings, numbers and booleans number numbers, and strings that parse as a number boolean booleans, and the strings true / false (any case) object any JSON structure: an object or an array, or a string that parses as one

Any other declared type is not checked. InputBindingResolver also substitutes {{inputs.NAME}} placeholders in agent prompts and scripts: strings are inserted as-is, null becomes an empty string, and other values are serialized as JSON.

docs.title: Configuring Axiom
docs.text: Axiom is configured through environment variables or Java system properties.

docs.title: Application Properties
docs.text:
Application properties should be set using environment variables or Java system properties (-D flags), not by editing application.properties directly.

Axiom uses the standard Quarkus configuration conventions. To convert a property name to an environment variable: replace dots and hyphens with underscores and uppercase everything. For example:

Property Environment Variable Java System Property axiom.agent.default-type AXIOM_AGENT_DEFAULT_TYPE -Daxiom.agent.default-type=... axiom.agent.claude-code.max-steps AXIOM_AGENT_CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_STEPS -Daxiom.agent.claude-code.max-steps=... axiom.workflow.schedule-poll-interval AXIOM_WORKFLOW_SCHEDULE_POLL_INTERVAL -Daxiom.workflow.schedule-poll-interval=...

For example, to run Axiom with OpenCode as the default agent and a custom timeout:

export AXIOM_AGENT_DEFAULT_TYPE=opencode
export AXIOM_AGENT_OPENCODE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=300
java -jar apitomy-axiom-3.0.0.jar

Or using system properties:

java -Daxiom.agent.default-type=opencode -Daxiom.agent.opencode.timeout-seconds=300 -jar apitomy-axiom-3.0.0.jar

See the Quarkus Configuration Reference for full details on property sources and precedence.

The active default agent can also be changed at runtime from Settings > AI Engine in the UI, without restarting the server. The UI setting takes precedence over axiom.agent.default-type once it has been set.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: Property Default Description quarkus.http.port 9090 (9191 in the prod profile) HTTP port of the UI and REST API (/api/v1) quarkus.http.host 127.0.0.1 in the prod profile Address to listen on. Axiom has no authentication, so it accepts local connections only by default; set 0.0.0.0 to listen on all interfaces and protect access yourself

docs.title: AI Agents
docs.text:
Axiom supports multiple pluggable AI agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot CLI). Set the default agent used for tasks (unless overridden per action type) with:

Property Default Description axiom.home ~/.axiom Home for the database (data/), assistant sessions, task files, MCP servers, workspaces and the encryption key. Override with -Daxiom.home=... or the AXIOM_HOME environment variable axiom.agent.default-type claude-code Default agent type (claude-code, opencode, or copilot)

docs.title: Claude Code Settings
docs.text:
Property Default Description axiom.agent.claude-code.executable claude Path to the Claude CLI binary axiom.agent.claude-code.plugin-dirs (empty) Comma-separated absolute paths passed to the CLI as repeated --plugin-dir flags (paths cannot contain commas). Each path is a plugin directory, a folder of plugins, or a plugin .zip, as the CLI's --plugin-dir accepts; with --bare (Axiom's default) skills load from plugin dirs only axiom.agent.claude-code.model (agent default) AI model override axiom.agent.claude-code.max-steps 50 Maximum agentic turns per task (passed as --max-turns) axiom.agent.claude-code.max-budget-usd 5.0 Maximum cost per task in USD axiom.agent.claude-code.timeout-seconds 600 Subprocess timeout axiom.agent.claude-code.available-models (see application.properties) Comma-separated model list for the UI model picker

Claude Code 2.1.117 replaced the Glob and Grep tools with search through Bash on native macOS and Linux builds (anthropics/claude-code#52004), and under Axiom's headless --bare mode the built-in tool set is exactly Bash, Edit and Read. Allowlists and toolsets should therefore use Bash(grep *) and Bash(find *) for file search; names the CLI does not recognize are silently ignored, which is why the built-in Read-Only Tools toolset lists those two Bash patterns. If your installation seeded that toolset before this change, edit it by hand in the UI and replace Glob and Grep with Bash(grep *); seeded toolsets are only written to an empty database, so upgrades keep the old entries.

A skill loaded from a plugin directory can only use tools that the action type's allowlist grants. An action type without an allowlist runs with --permission-mode acceptEdits, under which the headless CLI denies every tool call that is not an edit, so action types that invoke skills must declare an allowlist.

docs.title: OpenCode Settings
docs.text: Property Default Description axiom.agent.opencode.executable opencode Path to the OpenCode CLI binary axiom.agent.opencode.server.hostname 127.0.0.1 OpenCode server hostname axiom.agent.opencode.server.port 4096 OpenCode server port axiom.agent.opencode.model (see application.properties) Model in provider/model format axiom.agent.opencode.max-steps 50 Maximum agent steps per task axiom.agent.opencode.timeout-seconds 600 HTTP request timeout axiom.agent.opencode.available-models (see application.properties) Comma-separated model list for the UI model picker axiom.agent.opencode.model-discovery.enabled true Enable dynamic model discovery from the OpenCode server axiom.agent.opencode.model-discovery.timeout-seconds 8 Timeout for a model discovery request axiom.agent.opencode.model-discovery.cache-seconds 86400 How long discovered models are cached

docs.title: GitHub Copilot CLI Settings
docs.text: Property Default Description axiom.agent.copilot.executable copilot Path to the Copilot CLI binary axiom.agent.copilot.model (agent default) AI model override axiom.agent.copilot.timeout-seconds 600 Subprocess timeout axiom.agent.copilot.available-models (see application.properties) Comma-separated model list for the UI model picker

docs.title: Event Stream Pipeline
docs.text:
Property Default Description axiom.stream-pipeline.poll-interval 5s How often the event stream orchestrator evaluates unprocessed (event, subscription) pairs axiom.stream-pipeline.max-attempts 3 Maximum routing attempts (first try plus retries) for an (event, subscription) pair; when the last allowed attempt fails the ledger entry becomes exhausted and is no longer retried automatically (it can be retried manually, which allows one more attempt). axiom.stream-pipeline.retry-initial-delay 30s Delay before the first retry of a failed entry; each later retry doubles it (exponential backoff). Quarkus duration format (30s, 5m, PT30S) axiom.stream-pipeline.retry-max-delay 1h Upper bound of the delay between two attempts

Startup fails with an error naming the property if max-attempts is less than 1, retry-initial-delay is not greater than zero, or retry-max-delay is less than retry-initial-delay (values are not clamped).

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text: Property Default Description axiom.workflow.schedule-poll-interval 30s How often to check for due workflow schedule triggers. Schedule triggers fire on a single node only; running several Axiom nodes against one database is not supported for schedule triggers. axiom.workflow.wait-poll-interval 10s How often to resume workflow runs whose wait node has elapsed

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text: Property Default Description axiom.script.timeout-seconds 60 Maximum run time, in seconds, of a Script or Node.js action type; output gets a [Script timed out after Ns] note (Script) or a [Node action timed out after Ns] note (Node.js) when it is exceeded. Tools are not affected: they time out after a fixed 30 seconds.

docs.title: AI Assistant
docs.text:
The interactive AI Assistant allows users to create and update configuration items through conversation.

Property Default Description axiom.assistant.max-sessions 12 Maximum concurrent assistant sessions axiom.assistant.opencode.executable opencode OpenCode CLI executable used for interactive sessions axiom.assistant.opencode.startup-timeout-seconds 30 Per-session server startup timeout axiom.assistant.opencode.server.port (unset) Port for each interactive OpenCode server; when unset, port 0 is used

docs.title: Workflow Workbench
docs.text:
Property Default Description axiom.workbench.interrupt-timeout-seconds 30 When the user stops an AI turn in the workbench and the session has not ended it after this many seconds, the turn is finished as failed

Session availability also depends on which registered agents support interactive sessions — see AI Assistant.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text: Property Default Description axiom.workspace.root ~/.axiom/workspaces Root directory for subject workspaces (one subject-<id> directory per subject)

docs.title: Data Retention
docs.text:
Retention periods are stored in the database (not as static properties) and can be changed at any time from Settings > Data Retention in the UI or with PUT /api/v1/system/retention. Defaults are:

Setting Default What it controls Inactive subjects 90 days How long an inactive subject (no running or waiting run) is kept after its most recent run finished, before it is deleted with its workspace, tasks, thread, workflow runs, activity and AI usage. Subjects that have never had a run are not deleted automatically. Traces and event routing outcomes of the subject are kept. Traces 30 days How long execution traces (and their nodes and tool execution records) are kept Events 90 days How long stream events, their subscription processing ledger entries and routing outcomes are kept. Events that a running or waiting workflow run depends on are kept until the run finishes. Workflow runs 0 (forever) How long finished workflow runs are kept, measured from when they finished. Running and waiting runs are never deleted. Activity log 0 (forever) How long activity log entries are kept AI usage 0 (forever) How long AI usage (cost) records are kept

Inactive subjects, traces and events must be kept for at least 1 day. For the history settings, 0 means "keep forever". They default to 0 so that upgrading Axiom never deletes data you did not ask it to delete.

Cleanup runs hourly in the background. Event source poll logs are always retained for a fixed 3 days and are not configurable.

docs.title: Database Profiles
docs.text:
Axiom uses H2 with different profiles for different environments:

Profile Database Usage dev (default) H2 in-memory Development — schema recreated on restart persist H2 file (<axiom.home>/data/axiom, default ~/.axiom/data/axiom) Persistent dev — Flyway migrations prod H2 file (<axiom.home>/data/axiom, default ~/.axiom/data/axiom) Production — release JAR with Flyway

When running from the release JAR, the prod profile is active automatically. For development with persistent data, activate the persist profile:

mvn quarkus:dev -Dquarkus.profile=persist

Database schema migrations are managed by Flyway and run automatically on startup when using the persist or prod profiles.

docs.title: Secrets and Encryption
docs.text:
Secret values (API tokens, credentials) are encrypted at rest using a key that Axiom generates automatically on first startup and stores at ~/.axiom/secret.key. This key is separate from the database — see Upgrading and Backups for what to back up and restore together.

Axiom loads the key when it starts. If the key file cannot be read or created, or is not a valid 256-bit key (for example, truncated), Axiom logs the problem and exits instead of starting. Restore the key from a backup; deleting it makes Axiom generate a new key, and secrets encrypted with the old key can no longer be decrypted.

docs.title: How to Contribute
docs.text: Apitomy Axiom is open source under the Apache License 2.0. We welcome contributions of all kinds — bug reports, feature requests, documentation improvements, and code contributions.

docs.title: Getting Involved
docs.text:
• Report bugs or request features on GitHub Issues
  • Read the contributing guide at CONTRIBUTING.md for development setup, coding conventions, and pull request guidelines
  • Review the README at README.md for an overview of the project structure and build instructions

docs.title: Building from Source
docs.text:
To build and run Axiom for development, you'll need:

  • Java 25+
  • Maven 3.9+
  • Node.js 20+ and npm (for the UI)
git clone https://github.com/Apitomy/apitomy-axiom.git
cd apitomy-axiom
./dev.sh

This builds the backend, then starts it together with the Vite UI dev server on http://localhost:9191 (backend on http://localhost:9090). See Running Axiom for the dev.sh options and the README for full build instructions and development workflow details.

docs.title: Running Axiom
docs.text: The fastest way to get started with Apitomy Axiom is to use the run-axiom.sh script, which downloads and runs the latest release automatically.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Java 25+
  • curl and jq (for downloading releases)
  • Node.js (the node binary on the PATH; used by Axiom at runtime to run the MCP tool servers it gives to AI agents and the AI Assistant, and Node.js action types). The AI engine CLIs installed with npm also need npm.
  • One of the supported AI engine CLIs:
Engine Config Value Binary Install Claude Code claude-code (default) claude npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code OpenCode opencode opencode curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install \| bash GitHub Copilot CLI copilot copilot npm install -g @github/copilot
  • An API key for your LLM provider (e.g., ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable)

docs.title: Run Axiom
docs.text:
Download and run the script:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Apitomy/apitomy-axiom/main/scripts/run-axiom.sh | bash

Or clone the repo and run it directly:

git clone https://github.com/Apitomy/apitomy-axiom.git
cd apitomy-axiom
./scripts/run-axiom.sh

The script will:

  1. Query GitHub for the latest Apitomy Axiom release (or the release pinned with AXIOM_VERSION)
  2. Download the application JAR (cached in $AXIOM_HOME/releases/, default ~/.axiom/releases/, for future runs). The JAR is downloaded to a temporary .part file and only moved into place once complete.
  3. Check for Java 25+, curl, jq and Node.js (node is required for Axiom 3.x; for older versions a missing node only produces a warning)
  4. Start the application on http://localhost:9191 with the prod profile (file-based H2 database in $AXIOM_HOME/data/, default ~/.axiom/data/)

Open http://localhost:9191 in your browser to access the Axiom UI. The REST API is served under http://localhost:9191/api/v1. Arguments passed to the script are passed on to java -jar.

The script reads these environment variables:

Variable Effect AXIOM_VERSION Release to run, without the leading v (for example AXIOM_VERSION=2.1.2). Default: the latest release AXIOM_HOME Axiom home directory holding the JAR cache (releases/) and the database (data/). Default: ~/.axiom

For example, to stay on Axiom 2.1.2:

AXIOM_VERSION=2.1.2 ./scripts/run-axiom.sh

Offline use. If GitHub cannot be reached (no network, API rate limit, HTTP error), the script falls back to the cache with a warning: the newest cached JAR when no version is pinned, or the cached JAR of the pinned AXIOM_VERSION. It fails only if no suitable JAR is cached.

Upgrade warning. The script records the last version it ran in $AXIOM_HOME/releases/last-run-version. Before starting Axiom 3.x it checks whether $AXIOM_HOME/data/axiom.mv.db exists and appears to come from Axiom 2.x (the recorded version is 2.x, or there is no record but a 2.x JAR is cached). If so, it explains that Axiom 3 cannot use a 2.x database and that you can either back up and delete $AXIOM_HOME/data or pin AXIOM_VERSION=2.1.2, and links to the 3.0.0 release notes. In an interactive terminal it asks for confirmation; otherwise it continues and Axiom itself refuses to start on the old database. This check is a heuristic and can miss databases created outside the script.

docs.title: Running a Release JAR Directly
docs.text:
Each GitHub release publishes a single uber-jar named apitomy-axiom-<version>.jar. You can download it yourself and run it with:

java -jar apitomy-axiom-3.0.0.jar

The release JAR uses the prod profile: it listens on port 9191 and stores its H2 database in ~/.axiom/data/ (<axiom.home>/data/ if axiom.home is set).

Local access only

Axiom has no authentication, so the release build only accepts connections from the same machine (127.0.0.1). To make it reachable from other machines, set the bind address, for example java -Dquarkus.http.host=0.0.0.0 -jar apitomy-axiom-3.0.0.jar (or QUARKUS_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0), and protect access yourself, for example behind an authenticating reverse proxy.

Upgrading from Axiom 2.x

Axiom 3 cannot use a database created by Axiom 2.x (or older) and refuses to start on one. See Upgrading From Axiom 2.x.

docs.title: Running from Source
docs.text:
To run the current source code, clone the repository and run ./dev.sh (requires Java 25+, Maven 3.9+, Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+ and npm). It builds all modules, then starts the backend on http://localhost:9090 and the Vite UI dev server on http://localhost:9191, which proxies API requests to the backend.

Option Effect --skip-ui Start the backend only --persist Use the persist profile (file-based H2 database in <axiom.home>/data/, default ~/.axiom/data/) instead of the in-memory dev database --dataDir=/path Store the H2 database in /path (implies --persist) --portOffset=N Add N to both ports (for example 100 gives backend 9190 and UI 9291)

Press Ctrl+C to stop both processes.

To build a release JAR yourself, run ./build-release.sh (backend and UI, prod profile). It produces app/target/apitomy-axiom-app-<version>-runner.jar, which the release workflow publishes as apitomy-axiom-<version>.jar. See Building Axiom.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Configuring Axiom — AI engine settings, database profiles, and application properties
  • User Guide — Core concepts, event sources, action types, and advanced usage

docs.title: Apitomy Axiom 3.0.0
docs.text:
Axiom 3.0 is a new major version that puts workflows at the center. Events from GitHub and Jira flow into a durable event stream; subscriptions match them and start or resume workflow runs; workflows orchestrate action types (AI agents, Bash scripts or Node.js code), SDK calls, human tasks in a new Inbox, waits and event correlation. The new Workflow Workbench lets you build all of this together with an AI assistant.

3.0 is a clean break from 2.x: it cannot use a 2.x database. Read Upgrading from 2.x before installing.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Workflows. Visual workflow definitions (powered by Apitomy Flow 3.0) with start, end, action, human-task, wait and receive-event nodes, conditional and parallel branches, versions and publishing.
  • Workflow Workbench. An AI-assisted editor for a workflow together with its action types, tools and subscriptions: AI edits arrive as reviewable, undoable change sets; drafts are validated continuously; action types and tools can be test-run from the workbench; publish when ready.
  • Event stream and subscriptions. GitHub and Jira event sources poll into a durable stream; subscriptions filter events with expressions and start workflows or deliver events to waiting runs, with retries and a full processing audit trail.
  • Runs. A runs list as the landing page, run detail with a live diagram, timeline, trace and lineage, re-run of failed runs, and running a workflow by hand from any stream event.
  • Inbox. Human-task nodes create tasks with structured forms; workflows wait for the answer.
  • Dashboards, tracing and lineage. Custom dashboards, end-to-end trace IDs, correlation IDs in logs, and a lineage view connecting events, runs, tasks, traces and AI usage.
  • Multiple AI engines. Claude Code, OpenCode and the GitHub Copilot CLI, side by side.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
• Workflow definitions with a visual editor, version history with diffs, publishing, and import/export in configuration packs (Components → Workflows).
  • Node types:
  • start, end;
  • action: runs an action type, or calls an Axiom SDK function directly (sdk:<function>);
  • human-task: creates an Inbox task with a form and waits for the answer;
  • wait: pauses for an ISO-8601 duration;
  • receive-event: waits for a matching stream event, with correlation keys, match conditions, output mappings, look-back for events that arrived earlier, and a timeout.
  • Conditional edges (expressions over the run context) and parallel fork/join.
  • Standard inputs. A workflow's Start node declares which standard inputs a run receives: subject (the subject's id, name, type, ref, refSource, repository) and event (the triggering event). A run whose required inputs are not available is not created. Expressions read context.subject.<field> and context.event.<field>.
  • Validation at publish and while editing, including a warning when a node output would overwrite a workflow input.
  • Schedule triggers: run a workflow on a cron schedule against a fixed subject.
  • One active run per subject and workflow; duplicate starts are rejected (manual) or skipped and recorded (subscriptions and schedules).
  • SDK functions, including new axiom_create_subject, axiom_update_subject_body, axiom_list_agents, axiom_list_subject_runs, axiom_get_workflow_run and axiom_set_workflow_run_title.
  • Action nodes that call an SDK function or run an AI agent action type have their own icon and color in the editor and in run diagrams.

docs.title: Workflow Workbench
docs.text:
• Workbench page listing compositions; each composition is a workflow plus its action types, tools and subscriptions, edited as server-side drafts with revision history and restore.
  • AI assistant bound to the composition: it edits the workflow through change sets that are selected on the canvas and can be undone per turn; it can read stream events, evaluate expressions against them, preview subscription filters, analyse runs and traces, and suggest tests.
  • Live validation with "Ask AI to fix this" and "Ask AI about this…" actions.
  • Test-run node and script action types and tools with sample inputs (Tests panel); runs of the published workflow with "Ask AI to analyze" (Runs panel).
  • Subscriptions in compositions. Start the workflow (create-workflow) or feed its receive-event nodes (workflow-dispatch). A matching-events preview shows which recent events a filter matches. Publishing never turns automation on: subscriptions are published disabled and enabled with an explicit Enabled switch.
  • Dependency-aware publishing with conflict detection, and engine/model selection per composition.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
• Runs list (the landing page) with filter chips for status, workflow, subject and labels.
  • Run detail: diagram with the current node, overview (subject, workflow, inputs, labels, trigger event), step timeline, execution trace and lineage.
  • Open in workflow editor from a node in the run diagram opens the workflow with that node selected and centered.
  • Re-run a failed run with the latest published version of its workflow.
  • Run workflow… from any event in the event stream, with suggested workflows, an optional title and labels.
  • Optional run titles, set when starting a run or by the workflow itself (axiom_set_workflow_run_title).
  • Cancel running and waiting runs. Cancelling or failing a run marks its open Inbox tasks Cancelled.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
• Event sources for GitHub (Repository Events API) and Jira (JQL and changelog) poll into a durable event stream, with poll logs and status.
  • Event Stream page: filter by type and actor, live updates, and an event detail page with the processing audit trail, routing outcomes, started runs and lineage.
  • Subscriptions with expression filters, a live preview against recent events (including evaluation errors), routing rules (create-workflow, workflow-dispatch) and a "process events from" time.
  • Failed event processing is retried with backoff and can be retried by hand.
  • A subscription filter that cannot be evaluated against an event is recorded as filter_error and shown as an error. It is not retried automatically; it is retried by hand or when the subscription's filter is changed (#348).
  • The event stream's match badge counts every matched subscription, and the events API exposes per-state processing counts for each event (processingStates) (#346).
  • Expression evaluator for authoring (POST /expressions/evaluate), with the same scopes and context (context.subject, context.event) as a real run, including subscription filters.

docs.title: Action types and tools
docs.text:
• Node.js execution mode: an ES module exporting run(inputs, ctx).
  • Declared, typed inputs and outputs, validated when a workflow is published and when the task runs; workflow nodes map every required input explicitly; {{inputs.<name>}} is the only template placeholder.
  • Per-action-type step and budget limits, timeouts and labels.

docs.title: AI assistant and engines
docs.text:
• Session templates and a subject-scoped assistant; auto-approval rules, subagent views, stop/interrupt, todo and thinking display, cost and token totals.
  • Built-in session templates can be customized: engine, model and environment are editable per installation and can be reset to defaults. Customizations are not included in configuration packs.
  • The configuration assistant validates its drafts and previews workflows, subscriptions and event sources before applying them.
  • Claude Code, OpenCode (as a full interactive assistant engine) and the GitHub Copilot CLI can be used at the same time; per-engine settings in Settings → Engine.

docs.title: Observability and operations
docs.text:
• Custom dashboards with tabs and widgets for workflow runs (runs by status, failed runs with re-run, waiting runs, upcoming schedules, workflows), tasks awaiting input, event operations (event source health, subscription processing, processing failures with retry, event volume, recent events), AI usage (cost summary, breakdown by subject, workflow, engine, model or action type) and application health with per-component checks. Dashboard labels filter subject-related widgets by subject label; global widgets are marked. Widgets refresh live from server events or by polling. Templates (Operations, Event Operations, AI Usage) create a ready-made dashboard, /dashboards opens the default dashboard, and dashboards can be included in configuration packs. See Dashboards.
  • Trace IDs across activity, AI usage, tasks and runs; correlation IDs in server logs; a lineage API and panel.
  • AI usage records the engine, the exact model, and the workflow run and workflow that caused it.
  • Data retention settings for events, traces, runs and inactive subjects.
  • Dark mode.

docs.title: Secrets are no longer injected automatically
docs.text:
In 2.x every secret was passed to every agent and script that did not configure its own environment. In 3.0 a process gets only the variables its environment declares:

  • Declare each secret an action type (or a tool it allows) needs in the action type's Environment, for example GH_TOKEN=${secret:GH_TOKEN}; the Add secret picker fills this in. Session templates have their own Environment.
  • A reference to a secret that does not exist fails the task, test run or session instead of passing the literal ${secret:NAME} text.
  • Validation warns when a script, Node.js code or a tool uses a secret ($GH_TOKEN, process.env.GH_TOKEN) that is not declared.

This keeps credentials away from code and agents that do not need them, and limits what a prompt-injected agent could reveal.

docs.title: Removed features
docs.text:
• Reports and report definitions, including their pages, REST endpoints, SDK functions (axiom_list_reports, axiom_list_report_definitions, axiom_add_report_label, axiom_remove_report_label) and the reportDefinitions section of configuration packs.
  • The AI Manager: its pages, /manager/** endpoints and escalations. Workflows replace manager-driven routing.
  • Projects and their open/close lifecycle, replaced by subjects (see below).
  • Invoking action types directly: manual task creation, the free-form task response endpoint, the invoke-action routing type and the SDK function axiom_create_task. Action types run only from workflow action nodes; human input goes through Inbox tasks.
  • The 2.x event pipeline (/events, the event queue and the Events log page), replaced by the event stream, subscriptions and poll logs.
  • AI edit endpoints and per-editor AI assistants for action types and tools, replaced by the Workflow Workbench.
  • The fixed home dashboard: / now opens the Runs list; dashboards are user-defined.
  • Action type flags userTriggerable, managerTriggerable, emitsEvent and the free-form inputSchema, replaced by declared inputs and outputs.
  • Legacy template placeholders in action types ({{input}}, {{ref}}, {{repository}}, {{subjectName}}, {{subjectId}}, {{eventId}}, {{actionType}}, {{workDir}}, {{apiBaseUrl}}, {{taskId}}) and the ambient AXIOM_SUBJECT_* environment variables for action types. Use {{inputs.<name>}} and map values from the workflow. Assistant session templates are not affected: a subject-scoped session still sets AXIOM_SUBJECT_ID, AXIOM_SUBJECT_NAME, AXIOM_REF and AXIOM_REPOSITORY, its welcome and initial messages support {{subjectName}}, and its system prompt supports {{subjectName}} and {{subjectContext}}.

docs.title: Renamed concepts and API changes
docs.text:
• Projects → Subjects: /projects/** → /subjects/**; projectId → subjectId in tasks, thread entries, activity, AI usage and traces. A subject's description is now a Markdown body.
  • Actors → Agents: /actors/** → /agents/**; Task.assignedActor → assignedAgent; AiUsage.actorId → agentId.
  • System configuration: SystemConfig.engine is removed; use defaultEngine and engines.
  • SDK: *_project* functions are renamed to *_subject*; axiom_close_project, axiom_reopen_project and axiom_list_actors are removed (use axiom_list_agents).
  • Configuration packs are format version 3.0. Import does not check a pack's version, so a 2.x pack is not rejected but may apply only partially. Recreate your configuration instead of importing 2.x packs.
  • Navigation is reorganized: Runs, Subjects, Inbox, Dashboards, Events, Workbench, Logs, Metrics, Components and Settings.

docs.title: Configuration properties
docs.text:
2.x property 3.0 property axiom.ai-engine axiom.agent.default-type axiom.claude-code.* axiom.agent.claude-code.* (max-turns → max-steps) axiom.opencode.* axiom.agent.opencode.* axiom.github.tick-interval axiom.github-v2.tick-interval axiom.jira.tick-interval axiom.jira-v2.tick-interval axiom.manager.*, axiom.reports.poll-interval, axiom.github.poll-interval, axiom.pipeline.poll-interval removed axiom.ai-assistant.timeout-seconds, axiom.assistant.idle-timeout-seconds, axiom.event-source-logs.retention-days removed

axiom.assistant.max-sessions is unchanged. New properties include axiom.home (default ~/.axiom; workspaces, sessions, installed MCP servers, the encryption key and the database live under it), axiom.agent.copilot.*, axiom.agent.opencode.model-discovery.*, axiom.assistant.opencode.*, axiom.events.jira.max-search-pages, axiom.stream-pipeline.*, axiom.workbench.interrupt-timeout-seconds and axiom.workflow.* (schedule-poll-interval, wait-poll-interval). axiom.data-url (the database JDBC URL) is derived from axiom.home; set it only to override the database location.

docs.title: Upgrading from 2.x
docs.text:
Axiom 3.0 starts from a new database schema and cannot use a 2.x database. If it finds one, it refuses to start and tells you to remove it. No 2.x data is migrated (projects, reports, events, tasks and manager configuration are not carried over).

The database lives under the Axiom home, at <axiom.home>/data/axiom (by default ~/.axiom/data/axiom, as before), alongside the rest of Axiom's data. Setting axiom.home (or AXIOM_HOME) moves the database too.

  1. Stop Axiom 2.x.
  2. Back up ~/.axiom if you want to keep the old data.
  3. Delete ~/.axiom/data/ (or <axiom.home>/data/ if you set axiom.home).
  4. Install and start Axiom 3.0.0. It creates a new database.
  5. Recreate your configuration: secrets, event sources, action types, tools, workflows and subscriptions. The Workflow Workbench is the quickest way to rebuild automation as workflows. Declare the secrets each action type needs in its Environment (see Secrets).

From 3.0.0 on, schema changes ship as incremental migrations that are applied automatically at startup.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Java 25.
  • Node.js on the PATH (Axiom runs its MCP tool servers and Node.js action types with it).
  • At least one AI engine CLI for agent work: Claude Code, OpenCode or the GitHub Copilot CLI.
  • Start with java -jar apitomy-axiom-3.0.0.jar; the UI and API are served on http://localhost:9191.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• No authentication. Axiom is intended for local, single-user use. The release build listens on 127.0.0.1 only; if you set quarkus.http.host to accept connections from other machines, protect access yourself (for example behind an authenticating reverse proxy).
  • The Workflow Workbench cannot test a draft workflow end to end; test action types and tools individually and run the published workflow (#469).
  • The workbench cannot delete or disable published items (except enabling and disabling its subscriptions), and existing subscriptions cannot be added to a composition.
  • Retrying failed event routing skips rules that already completed, but a rule can still run twice if Axiom crashes between the rule's side effect and its recorded outcome, or if a subscription's routing rules are edited between attempts (#341).
  • Tasks running when Axiom stops are marked failed at the next startup and the workflow run continues as if the task had failed; they are not resumed. Tasks waiting for human input are kept (#343).
  • Agent health checks and startup checks run subprocesses without the 1 MiB output limit (#344).
  • Schedule triggers assume a single Axiom instance.

docs.title: Notable Fixes
docs.text:
• Deleting a subject workspace never follows symbolic links out of the workspace (#340).
  • Scripts always run in the subject workspace; placeholder substitution is quoting-aware; stderr is captured separately.
  • Inbox tasks complete correctly after a server restart.
  • Setup failures after an agent is assigned no longer leave the task stuck or the agent busy.
  • Cleanup jobs retry on database deadlocks; orphaned processing entries are recovered at startup.
  • GitHub and Jira pollers use HTTP timeouts and shut down cleanly.
  • Workflow scripts, Node.js actions, tool tests, session init scripts, the MCP server npm install, and the workspace disk-usage check enforce their timeouts, close stdin, and kill the whole process tree when the timeout expires (#344). Each keeps at most 1 MiB of output per stream: the beginning and the end, with the middle replaced by [Output truncated]. Scripts and actions should write logs to stderr and print their JSON result last on stdout; a run whose stdout exceeds 1 MiB without a JSON result at its end fails.
  • Jira polling no longer skips changes: the checkpoint only advances after a complete poll, all result pages and full changelogs are fetched, JQL time bounds are timezone-independent, and failed polls are retried (#342).
  • "Process events from" compares the event's own timestamp.
  • Orphaned and incomplete traces are closed; retention leaves no dangling references.
  • Invalid requests return 400 instead of 500 across several endpoints.
  • Assistant session templates expand nested toolsets (#138).
  • AI assistant: correct cumulative session cost, interruption without killing the process, subagent permission routing, and better chat performance in long conversations.

docs.title: Trace ID as Correlation ID Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Every activity row, AI usage row and agent-created task carries the trace ID of the unit of work that produced it, so a user can find all records for a trace.

Architecture: Add trace_id to activity_log and ai_usage, populate it from the trace already in scope at each write, expose it via the API (field + filter), clear it in TraceCleanup. Agents propagate their trace via X-Axiom-Trace-Id / X-Axiom-Parent-Node-Id headers; a request filter validates them into a request-scoped CallerTraceContext, and POST /projects/{id}/tasks joins the caller's trace.

Tech Stack: Java 25, Quarkus, Hibernate Panache, Flyway (H2), JAX-RS generated from OpenAPI, JUnit 5 + RestAssured, React/TypeScript UI, Node MCP server template.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-correlation-id-design.md

  • The caller trace stays in-progress while the task is Pending (TaskTraceFinalizer relies on the open node).
  • Headers with a malformed UUID, an unknown trace, a trace with status completed, or a parent node from a different trace → task gets a new user-action trace (assert trace type via TraceEntity.findById).

  • [ ] Step 3: CallerTraceContext.

/**
 * Request-scoped holder for the trace of the agent (or other caller) making the current API request.
 */
@RequestScoped
public class CallerTraceContext {

    private TraceContext traceContext;

    /**
     * Returns the validated caller trace context, if the request carried one.
     *
     * @return the caller trace context, or empty
     */
    public Optional<TraceContext> get() {
        return Optional.ofNullable(traceContext);
    }

    /**
     * Sets the validated caller trace context.
     *
     * @param traceContext the trace context to use for this request
     */
    public void set(TraceContext traceContext) {
        this.traceContext = traceContext;
    }
}

  • [ ] Step 4: CallerTraceFilter. @Provider, implements ContainerRequestFilter, injects CallerTraceContext. In filter(...): return if TRACE_HEADER is absent; parse the UUID (catch IllegalArgumentException → LOG.debugf and return); in QuarkusTransaction.requiringNew().call(...) load TraceEntity; require non-null and "in-progress".equals(trace.status). Resolve the parent node: if PARENT_NODE_HEADER is present, parse as Long and require TraceNodeEntity with that id and traceId equal to the trace; otherwise use the trace's root node id. On success callerTraceContext.set(new TraceContext(traceId, parentNodeId)); on any failure log at debug and leave it unset. Never fail the request.

docs.title: Workbench Phase 1: Assistant Foundation Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Generalize the assistant session foundation so the Workflow Workbench can reuse it. This phase adds template capabilities in place of the hard-coded axiom-config-assistant checks, a persisted conversation history journal, and per-session MCP tokens.

Architecture: - A SessionCapability enum is declared by built-in template JSON. It flows through the SessionTemplate record, the AssistantSession, and the REST beans, and every hard-coded template-ID check uses it instead. - A HistoryJournal listener appends every session event to history.jsonl in the session directory. - A random per-session token is handed to the @axiom-assistant MCP server, sent as X-Axiom-Session-Token, and required by the only MCP-only endpoint, /assistant/sessions/{id}/validate.

Tech Stack: Java 25, Quarkus 3.40.1, Jackson, JUnit 5, RestAssured, React 19 + TypeScript, Vitest.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-workflow-workbench-design.md, "§1 Architecture → Shared assistant foundation" and "§6 Phasing" item 1.

  • rg is not installed. Use git grep.

  • The Configuration Assistant's behaviour must not change. The only expected change to an existing test is that AssistantValidateEndpointTest sends the token header (Task 4).
  • Capability JSON names: config-items, validation-feedback, composition.
  • Token header name: X-Axiom-Session-Token. Token environment variable for MCP servers: AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN.
  • History file: <sessionDir>/history.jsonl, one JSON object {"type": ..., "data": ...} per line.

package io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.util.EnumSet;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Set;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

/**
 * Verifies capability parsing and the capabilities declared by the built-in templates.
 */
class SessionCapabilityTest {

    private static final ObjectMapper MAPPER = new ObjectMapper();

    @Test
    void parsesKnownNamesAndIgnoresUnknown() throws IOException {
        JsonNode array = MAPPER.readTree("[\"config-items\", \"composition\", \"bogus\"]");
        Set<SessionCapability> parsed = SessionCapability.parse(array);
        assertEquals(EnumSet.of(SessionCapability.CONFIG_ITEMS, SessionCapability.COMPOSITION), parsed);
    }

    @Test
    void missingArrayParsesToEmptySet() {
        assertTrue(SessionCapability.parse(MAPPER.missingNode()).isEmpty());
    }

    @Test
    void jsonNamesRoundTrip() {
        for (SessionCapability capability : SessionCapability.values()) {
            assertEquals(Optional.of(capability), SessionCapability.fromJsonName(capability.jsonName()));
        }
        assertEquals("validation-feedback", SessionCapability.VALIDATION_FEEDBACK.jsonName());
    }

    @Test
    void configAssistantDeclaresItemsAndFeedback() throws IOException {
        assertEquals(EnumSet.of(SessionCapability.CONFIG_ITEMS, SessionCapability.VALIDATION_FEEDBACK),
                capabilitiesOf("axiom-config-assistant.json"));
    }

    @Test
    void otherBuiltInsDeclareNothing() throws IOException {
        assertTrue(capabilitiesOf("general-assistant.json").isEmpty());
        assertTrue(capabilitiesOf("subject-assistant.json").isEmpty());
    }

    private static Set<SessionCapability> capabilitiesOf(String file) throws IOException {
        try (InputStream is = SessionCapabilityTest.class.getResourceAsStream(
                "/templates/assistant-templates/" + file)) {
            return SessionCapability.parse(MAPPER.readTree(is).path("capabilities"));
        }
    }
}

package io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;

import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.EnumSet;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Optional behaviours a session template enables. Code checks capabilities instead of template IDs, so new
 * built-in templates (such as the workbench) can opt in to shared behaviour.
 */
public enum SessionCapability {

    /** File-based configuration items in the working directory, with the items, validate and apply endpoints. */
    CONFIG_ITEMS("config-items"),

    /** Re-validate working-directory items after each tool result and feed problems back to the agent. */
    VALIDATION_FEEDBACK("validation-feedback"),

    /** The session is bound to a workbench composition. */
    COMPOSITION("composition");

    private final String jsonName;

    SessionCapability(String jsonName) {
        this.jsonName = jsonName;
    }

    /**
     * Returns the name used in template JSON and REST payloads.
     *
     * @return the JSON name, for example {@code config-items}
     */
    public String jsonName() {
        return jsonName;
    }

    /**
     * Looks up a capability by its JSON name.
     *
     * @param name the JSON name
     * @return the capability, or empty if the name is unknown
     */
    public static Optional<SessionCapability> fromJsonName(String name) {
        return Arrays.stream(values()).filter(c -> c.jsonName.equals(name)).findFirst();
    }

    /**
     * Parses a JSON array of capability names. Unknown names are ignored, and a missing or non-array node gives
     * an empty set.
     *
     * @param array the JSON node, typically a template's {@code capabilities} field
     * @return an unmodifiable set of capabilities
     */
    public static Set<SessionCapability> parse(JsonNode array) {
        if (array == null || !array.isArray()) {
            return Collections.emptySet();
        }
        EnumSet<SessionCapability> result = EnumSet.noneOf(SessionCapability.class);
        array.forEach(n -> fromJsonName(n.asText()).ifPresent(result::add));
        return Collections.unmodifiableSet(result);
    }
}

package io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant;

import io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant.runtime.InteractiveSessionDriver;
import io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant.runtime.InteractiveSessionDriverFactory;
import io.quarkus.test.InjectMock;
import io.quarkus.test.junit.QuarkusTest;
import io.restassured.http.ContentType;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

import static io.restassured.RestAssured.given;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.containsInAnyOrder;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.empty;
import static org.mockito.ArgumentMatchers.any;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.mock;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.when;

/**
 * Verifies that capabilities, not template IDs, drive config-assistant behaviour and are exposed over REST.
 */
@QuarkusTest
class SessionCapabilityEndpointTest {

    @InjectMock
    InteractiveSessionDriverFactory interactiveSessionDriverFactory;

    private final List<String> created = new ArrayList<>();

    @AfterEach
    void cleanUp() {
        created.forEach(id -> given().delete("/api/v1/assistant/sessions/{id}", id));
    }

    private String createSession(String templateId) throws IOException {
        when(interactiveSessionDriverFactory.createDriver(any()))
                .thenAnswer(i -> mock(InteractiveSessionDriver.class));
        String id = given().contentType(ContentType.JSON)
                .body("{\"templateId\":\"" + templateId + "\",\"name\":\"cap-test\"}")
                .post("/api/v1/assistant/sessions")
                .then().statusCode(200).extract().path("id");
        created.add(id);
        return id;
    }

    @Test
    void configAssistantSessionExposesCapabilitiesAndItems() throws IOException {
        String id = createSession("axiom-config-assistant");
        given().get("/api/v1/assistant/sessions/{id}", id)
                .then().statusCode(200)
                .body("capabilities", containsInAnyOrder("config-items", "validation-feedback"));
        given().get("/api/v1/assistant/sessions/{id}/items", id).then().statusCode(200);
    }

    @Test
    void generalSessionHasNoCapabilitiesAndNoItems() throws IOException {
        String id = createSession("general-assistant");
        given().get("/api/v1/assistant/sessions/{id}", id)
                .then().statusCode(200).body("capabilities", empty());
        given().get("/api/v1/assistant/sessions/{id}/items", id).then().statusCode(400);
    }

    @Test
    void templatesExposeCapabilities() {
        given().get("/api/v1/assistant/templates/{id}", "axiom-config-assistant")
                .then().statusCode(200)
                .body("capabilities", containsInAnyOrder("config-items", "validation-feedback"));
    }
}

    private volatile Set<SessionCapability> capabilities = Collections.emptySet();

    /**
     * Returns the capabilities of the template this session was created from.
     *
     * @return an unmodifiable set, empty if none
     */
    public Set<SessionCapability> getCapabilities() {
        return capabilities;
    }

    /**
     * Sets the capabilities of this session. Called once by the session manager before the session starts.
     *
     * @param capabilities the template's capabilities
     */
    public void setCapabilities(Set<SessionCapability> capabilities) {
        this.capabilities = capabilities.isEmpty()
                ? Collections.emptySet()
                : Collections.unmodifiableSet(EnumSet.copyOf(capabilities));
    }

    /**
     * Returns whether this session has a capability.
     *
     * @param capability the capability
     * @return true if the session's template declares it
     */
    public boolean hasCapability(SessionCapability capability) {
        return capabilities.contains(capability);
    }

/** Behaviours a session template enables. Mirrors the backend `SessionCapability` JSON names. */
export type SessionCapability = "config-items" | "validation-feedback" | "composition";

/**
 * Returns whether a session or template declares a capability.
 *
 * @param target a session info or template object, possibly missing
 * @param capability the capability to look for
 * @returns true if `target.capabilities` contains `capability`
 */
export function hasCapability(
    target: { capabilities?: string[] } | null | undefined,
    capability: SessionCapability,
): boolean {
    return target?.capabilities?.includes(capability) ?? false;
}

package io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant.runtime.InteractiveSessionDriver;
import io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant.runtime.InteractiveSessionDriverFactory;
import io.quarkus.test.InjectMock;
import io.quarkus.test.junit.QuarkusTest;
import io.restassured.http.ContentType;
import jakarta.inject.Inject;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;

import static io.restassured.RestAssured.given;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertNotEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;
import static org.mockito.ArgumentMatchers.any;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.mock;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.when;

/**
 * Verifies the per-session MCP token: generation, hand-off to the MCP server, and enforcement.
 */
@QuarkusTest
class SessionTokenTest {

    private static final String BODY = "{\"type\": \"tool\", \"item\": {\"name\": \"t\"}}";

    @InjectMock
    InteractiveSessionDriverFactory interactiveSessionDriverFactory;

    @Inject
    AssistantSessionManager manager;

    private String sessionId;

    @BeforeEach
    void create() {
        when(interactiveSessionDriverFactory.createDriver(any()))
                .thenAnswer(i -> mock(InteractiveSessionDriver.class));
        sessionId = given().contentType(ContentType.JSON)
                .body("{\"templateId\":\"axiom-config-assistant\",\"name\":\"token-test\"}")
                .post("/api/v1/assistant/sessions").then().statusCode(200).extract().path("id");
    }

    @AfterEach
    void delete() {
        given().delete("/api/v1/assistant/sessions/{id}", sessionId);
    }

    @Test
    void tokenIsPassedToAssistantMcpServer() throws IOException {
        AssistantSession session = manager.getSession(sessionId);
        JsonNode config = new ObjectMapper().readTree(
                Files.readString(session.getSessionDirectory().resolve("mcp-config.json")));
        assertEquals(session.getMcpToken(),
                config.path("mcpServers").path("axiom").path("env").path("AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN").asText());
    }

    @Test
    void tokensAreUniqueAndVerified() {
        AssistantSession session = manager.getSession(sessionId);
        assertTrue(session.getMcpToken().length() >= 43);
        assertTrue(session.verifyMcpToken(session.getMcpToken()));
        assertFalse(session.verifyMcpToken("wrong"));
        assertFalse(session.verifyMcpToken(null));
        String other = given().contentType(ContentType.JSON)
                .body("{\"templateId\":\"axiom-config-assistant\",\"name\":\"token-test-2\"}")
                .post("/api/v1/assistant/sessions").then().statusCode(200).extract().path("id");
        try {
            assertNotEquals(session.getMcpToken(), manager.getSession(other).getMcpToken());
        } finally {
            given().delete("/api/v1/assistant/sessions/{id}", other);
        }
    }

    @Test
    void validateRequiresToken() {
        given().contentType(ContentType.JSON).body(BODY)
                .post("/api/v1/assistant/sessions/{id}/validate", sessionId).then().statusCode(401);
        given().contentType(ContentType.JSON).header("X-Axiom-Session-Token", "wrong").body(BODY)
                .post("/api/v1/assistant/sessions/{id}/validate", sessionId).then().statusCode(401);
        given().contentType(ContentType.JSON)
                .header("X-Axiom-Session-Token", manager.getSession(sessionId).getMcpToken()).body(BODY)
                .post("/api/v1/assistant/sessions/{id}/validate", sessionId).then().statusCode(200);
    }
}

Run: mvn -q -pl app -am test -Dtest=SessionTokenTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false

Expected: a compilation failure, because getMcpToken does not exist.

  • [ ] Step 3: Generate and verify the token in AssistantSession

Add these imports: java.security.MessageDigest, java.security.SecureRandom, java.util.Base64 and java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets. Then add:

    private static final SecureRandom RANDOM = new SecureRandom();

    private volatile String mcpToken = newToken();

    /**
     * Generates a new random session token (32 bytes, URL-safe Base64 without padding).
     *
     * @return the token
     */
    static String newToken() {
        byte[] bytes = new byte[32];
        RANDOM.nextBytes(bytes);
        return Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(bytes);
    }

    /**
     * Sets this session's MCP token. Called once by the session manager, which generates the token before the
     * session is constructed so it can be written into the MCP configuration.
     *
     * @param token the token
     */
    void setMcpToken(String token) {
        this.mcpToken = token;
    }

    /**
     * Returns the secret token this session's MCP servers present to Axiom REST.
     *
     * @return the token
     */
    public String getMcpToken() {
        return mcpToken;
    }

    /**
     * Checks a presented token against this session's token in constant time.
     *
     * @param presented the value of the {@code X-Axiom-Session-Token} header, possibly null
     * @return true if it matches
     */
    public boolean verifyMcpToken(String presented) {
        return presented != null && MessageDigest.isEqual(
                mcpToken.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8), presented.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    }
  • [ ] Step 4: Pass the token to the MCP server

resolveMcpServers runs before the AssistantSession object exists, so the manager generates the token first and hands it to the session with setMcpToken. In AssistantSessionManager.createSession: - Directly after String sessionId = UUID.randomUUID().toString();, add String mcpToken = AssistantSession.newToken();. - Add a String mcpToken parameter to resolveMcpServers after sessionId, and pass it in. - Directly after session.setCapabilities(...), add session.setMcpToken(mcpToken);. - In resolveMcpServers, inside the @axiom-assistant branch, add env.put("AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN", mcpToken); after the AXIOM_ASSISTANT_SESSION_ID line.

package io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;

/**

class HistoryJournalTest {

    private static final ObjectMapper MAPPER = new ObjectMapper();

    private static SseEvent event(String type, String text) {
        ObjectNode data = MAPPER.createObjectNode();
        data.put("text", text);
        return new SseEvent(type, data);

        journal.accept(event("user_message", "hi"));

        assertEquals(2, loaded.size());
        assertEquals("assistant_text", loaded.get(1).type());

        journal.accept(event("user_message", "old"));
        journal.accept(event("conversation_reset", ""));
        journal.accept(event("user_message", "new"));

        List<SseEvent> loaded = HistoryJournal.load(file, MAPPER);
        assertEquals(List.of("conversation_reset", "user_message"),
                loaded.stream().map(SseEvent::type).toList());
    }

    @Test
    void skipsMalformedLinesAndMissingFile(@TempDir Path dir) throws IOException {
        Path file = dir.resolve(HistoryJournal.FILE_NAME);
        assertTrue(HistoryJournal.load(file, MAPPER).isEmpty());
        new HistoryJournal(file, MAPPER).accept(event("user_message", "ok"));
        Files.writeString(file, "{not json\n", StandardOpenOption.APPEND);
        assertEquals(1, HistoryJournal.load(file, MAPPER).size());
    }

    @Test
    void writeFailureDoesNotThrow(@TempDir Path dir) {
        HistoryJournal journal = new HistoryJournal(dir.resolve("missing-dir/history.jsonl"), MAPPER);
        assertDoesNotThrow(() -> journal.accept(event("user_message", "x")));

package io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;
import io.apitomy.axiom.app.assistant.AssistantEventParser.SseEvent;
import org.jboss.logging.Logger;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.StandardOpenOption;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.function.Consumer;

/**
 * Appends every event of an assistant session to a JSON Lines file so that the conversation can be shown again
 * after a server restart. Each line is {@code {"type": ..., "data": ...}}.
 */
public final class HistoryJournal implements Consumer<SseEvent> {

    /** File name of the journal inside the session directory. */
    public static final String FILE_NAME = "history.jsonl";

    private static final Logger LOG = Logger.getLogger(HistoryJournal.class);

    private final Path file;
    private final ObjectMapper mapper;

    /**
     * Creates a journal writing to {@code file}.
     *
     * @param file the journal file; its parent directory must exist
     * @param mapper the JSON mapper
     */
    public HistoryJournal(Path file, ObjectMapper mapper) {
        this.file = file;
        this.mapper = mapper;
    }

    /**
     * Appends one event. Failures are logged and never propagated, so a full disk cannot break a session.
     *
     * @param event the event to record
     */
    @Override
    public synchronized void accept(SseEvent event) {
        ObjectNode line = mapper.createObjectNode();
        line.put("type", event.type());
        line.set("data", event.data());
        try {
            Files.writeString(file, line.toString() + "\n", StandardCharsets.UTF_8,
                    StandardOpenOption.CREATE, StandardOpenOption.APPEND);
        } catch (IOException e) {
            LOG.warnf("Failed to append to history journal %s: %s", file, e.getMessage());
        }
    }

    /**
     * Loads a journal. Like the in-memory history, a {@code conversation_reset} discards earlier events.
     * Malformed lines are skipped.
     *
     * @param file the journal file
     * @param mapper the JSON mapper
     * @return the events, oldest first; empty if the file does not exist
     * @throws IOException if the file exists but cannot be read
     */
    public static List<SseEvent> load(Path file, ObjectMapper mapper) throws IOException {
        List<SseEvent> events = new ArrayList<>();
        if (!Files.exists(file)) {
            return events;
        }
        for (String text : Files.readAllLines(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
            if (text.isBlank()) {
                continue;
            }
            JsonNode line;
            try {
                line = mapper.readTree(text);
            } catch (IOException e) {
                LOG.debugf("Skipping malformed history line in %s", file);
                continue;
            }
            String type = line.path("type").asText("");
            if (type.isEmpty()) {
                continue;
            }
            if ("conversation_reset".equals(type)) {
                events.clear();
            }
            events.add(new SseEvent(type, line.path("data")));
        }
        return events;
    }
}
