import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import {
    Alert, Button, Form, FormGroup, FormHelperText, FormSelect, FormSelectOption, HelperText, HelperTextItem,
    Modal, ModalBody, ModalFooter, ModalHeader, TextArea, TextInput,
} from "@patternfly/react-core";
import { fetchSubjects } from "../../config/api";
import { parseFieldValue, type TestField, testFields, testUnsupportedReason } from "./testRunLogic";

/** Props for {@link TestRunDialog}. */
export interface TestRunDialogProps {
    itemName: string;
    itemType: "action-type" | "tool";
    content: Record<string, unknown>;
    /** Texts typed in the previous run of this item. */
    initialValues: Record<string, string>;
    initialSubjectId?: number;
    /** Called with the parsed inputs, the raw texts and the chosen subject. */
    onRun(inputs: Record<string, unknown>, values: Record<string, string>, subjectId?: number): void;
    onClose(): void;
}

/**
 * Asks for sample inputs (or tool parameters) and an optional subject, then starts a test run.
 */
export function TestRunDialog(props: TestRunDialogProps) {
    const fields: TestField[] = testFields(props.itemType, props.content);
    const unsupported: string | null = testUnsupportedReason(props.itemType, props.content);
    const [values, setValues] = useState<Record<string, string>>(props.initialValues);
    const [errors, setErrors] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
    const [subjectId, setSubjectId] = useState<string>(props.initialSubjectId ? String(props.initialSubjectId) : "");
    const [subjects, setSubjects] = useState<{ id: number; name: string }[]>([]);
    const noun: string = props.itemType === "tool" ? "parameters" : "inputs";

    useEffect(() => {
        fetchSubjects(1, 100).then((r) => setSubjects(r.items.map((s) => ({ id: s.id, name: s.name }))))
            .catch(console.error);
    }, []);

    const run = () => {
        const nextErrors: Record<string, string> = {};
        const inputs: Record<string, unknown> = {};
        for (const field of fields) {
            const parsed = parseFieldValue(field, values[field.name] ?? "");
            if (parsed.error) {
                nextErrors[field.name] = parsed.error;
            } else if (parsed.value !== undefined) {
                inputs[field.name] = parsed.value;
            } else if (field.required) {
                nextErrors[field.name] = "Required.";
            }
        }
        setErrors(nextErrors);
        if (Object.keys(nextErrors).length === 0) {
            props.onRun(inputs, values, subjectId ? Number(subjectId) : undefined);
        }
    };

    return (
        <Modal isOpen variant="medium" onClose={props.onClose} aria-labelledby="test-run-title">
            <ModalHeader title={`Test ${props.itemName}`} labelId="test-run-title" />
            <ModalBody>
                {unsupported ? <Alert isInline variant="info" title={unsupported} /> : (
                    <Form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); run(); }}>
                        {fields.length === 0 && <p className="axiom-text-subtle">No {noun} are declared.</p>}
                        {fields.map((field) => {
                            const multiline: boolean = field.type === "object" || field.type === "array";
                            const id: string = `test-field-${field.name}`;
                            const onChange = (_e: unknown, v: string) => setValues((prev) => ({ ...prev, [field.name]: v }));
                            return (
                                <FormGroup key={field.name} label={field.name} isRequired={field.required} fieldId={id}>
                                    {multiline
                                        ? <TextArea id={id} aria-label={field.name} value={values[field.name] ?? ""}
                                            onChange={onChange} rows={4} resizeOrientation="vertical" />
                                        : <TextInput id={id} aria-label={field.name} value={values[field.name] ?? ""}
                                            onChange={onChange} />}
                                    <FormHelperText>
                                        <HelperText>
                                            {errors[field.name]
                                                ? <HelperTextItem variant="error">{errors[field.name]}</HelperTextItem>
                                                : <HelperTextItem>{field.type}{field.description ? ` — ${field.description}` : ""}</HelperTextItem>}
                                        </HelperText>
                                    </FormHelperText>
                                </FormGroup>
                            );
                        })}
                        <FormGroup label="Subject" fieldId="test-subject">
                            <FormSelect id="test-subject" value={subjectId} onChange={(_e, v) => setSubjectId(v)}>
                                <FormSelectOption value="" label="None — run in a temporary directory" />
                                {subjects.map((s) => <FormSelectOption key={s.id} value={String(s.id)} label={s.name} />)}
                            </FormSelect>
                        </FormGroup>
                    </Form>
                )}
            </ModalBody>
            <ModalFooter>
                {!unsupported && <Button variant="primary" onClick={run}>Run</Button>}
                <Button variant="link" onClick={props.onClose}>{unsupported ? "Close" : "Cancel"}</Button>
            </ModalFooter>
        </Modal>
    );
}

If PatternFly's focus trap fails in jsdom (as in WorkbenchListPage.test.tsx), mock Modal the same way that test does. Use elementToFocus on the first field (#test-field-<first>) when there is one, so the Close button is not focused first.

import { type ReactNode, useState } from "react";
import { Button, ExpandableSection, Label, Spinner } from "@patternfly/react-core";
import {
    AngleDownIcon, AngleRightIcon, AngleUpIcon, CheckCircleIcon, ExclamationCircleIcon, ExclamationTriangleIcon,
} from "@patternfly/react-icons";
import type { CompositionTestRun } from "../../config/compositions";

/** Props for {@link TestOutputStrip}. */
export interface TestOutputStripProps {
    /** Runs, newest first. */
    runs: CompositionTestRun[];
    collapsed: boolean;
    onToggle(): void;
    onOpenItem(itemId: number): void;
    /** Controls shown at the right of the header (e.g. the Test… button). */
    actions?: ReactNode;
}

function StatusIcon({ status }: { status: CompositionTestRun["status"] }) {
    switch (status) {
        case "running":
            return <Spinner size="sm" aria-label="running" />;
        case "passed":
            return <CheckCircleIcon aria-label="passed" color="var(--pf-t--global--icon--color--status--success--default)" />;
        case "failed":
            return <ExclamationCircleIcon aria-label="failed" color="var(--pf-t--global--icon--color--status--danger--default)" />;
        default:
            return <ExclamationTriangleIcon aria-label="error" color="var(--pf-t--global--icon--color--status--warning--default)" />;
    }
}

/**
 * One-line summary of a run.
 * @param run the run
 * @returns the summary text
 */
export function runSummary(run: CompositionTestRun): string {
    if (run.status === "running") {
        return "Running…";
    }
    if (run.message) {
        return run.message;
    }
    if (run.problems && run.problems.length > 0) {
        return run.problems[0];
    }
    if (run.itemType === "action-type" && run.outputs) {
        return `Outputs: ${JSON.stringify(run.outputs)}`;
    }
    return "";
}

function Details({ run }: { run: CompositionTestRun }) {
    const [scriptOpen, setScriptOpen] = useState<boolean>(false);
    return (
        <div className="axiom-test-strip__details">
            <h4>Inputs</h4>
            <pre>{JSON.stringify(run.inputs ?? {}, null, 2)}</pre>
            {run.outputs && <><h4>Outputs</h4><pre>{JSON.stringify(run.outputs, null, 2)}</pre></>}
            {(run.problems ?? []).length > 0 && (
                <><h4>Problems</h4><ul>{run.problems?.map((p) => <li key={p}>{p}</li>)}</ul></>
            )}
            {run.stdout && <><h4>stdout</h4><pre>{run.stdout}</pre></>}
            {run.stderr && <><h4>stderr</h4><pre>{run.stderr}</pre></>}
            {run.resolvedScript && (
                <ExpandableSection toggleText="Resolved script" isExpanded={scriptOpen}
                    onToggle={(_e, open) => setScriptOpen(open)}>
                    <pre>{run.resolvedScript}</pre>
                </ExpandableSection>
            )}
        </div>
    );
}

/**
 * Collapsible list of the composition's recent test runs, by the user and the AI.
 */
export function TestOutputStrip({ runs, collapsed, onToggle, onOpenItem, actions }: TestOutputStripProps) {
    const [open, setOpen] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set<string>());
    const toggle = (id: string) => setOpen((prev) => {
        const next = new Set<string>(prev);
        if (next.has(id)) {
            next.delete(id);
        } else {
            next.add(id);
        }
        return next;
    });
    return (
        <section className="axiom-test-strip" aria-label="Test output">
            <div className="axiom-test-strip__header">
                <Button variant="plain" size="sm" onClick={onToggle}
                    aria-label={collapsed ? "Expand test output" : "Collapse test output"}
                    icon={collapsed ? <AngleUpIcon /> : <AngleDownIcon />} />
                <span className="axiom-workbench__pane-title">Test output</span>
                <Label isCompact>{runs.length}</Label>
                <span className="axiom-workbench__spacer" />
                {actions}
            </div>
            {!collapsed && (
                <div className="axiom-test-strip__body">
                    {runs.length === 0 && (
                        <p className="axiom-text-subtle axiom-test-strip__empty">
                            No test runs yet. Use Test… on an action type or tool, or ask the AI to test one.
                        </p>
                    )}
                    <ul className="axiom-test-strip__list">
                        {runs.map((run) => (
                            <li key={run.id}>
                                <div className="axiom-test-strip__row">
                                    <Button variant="plain" size="sm" aria-label={open.has(run.id) ? "Hide details" : "Show details"}
                                        aria-expanded={open.has(run.id)} onClick={() => toggle(run.id)}
                                        icon={open.has(run.id) ? <AngleDownIcon /> : <AngleRightIcon />} />
                                    <StatusIcon status={run.status} />
                                    <Button variant="link" isInline onClick={() => onOpenItem(run.itemId)}>{run.itemName}</Button>
                                    {run.author === "ai" && <Label isCompact color="purple">AI</Label>}
                                    <span className="axiom-text-subtle">
                                        {new Date(run.startedAt).toLocaleTimeString()}
                                        {run.durationMs !== undefined && run.status !== "running" ? ` · ${run.durationMs} ms` : ""}
                                        {run.exitCode !== undefined ? ` · exit ${run.exitCode}` : ""}
                                    </span>
                                    <span className="axiom-test-strip__summary">{runSummary(run)}</span>
                                </div>
                                {open.has(run.id) && <Details run={run} />}
                            </li>
                        ))}
                    </ul>
                </div>
            )}
        </section>
    );
}

docs.title: Workbench Phase 5b: AI-Suggested Tests Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: The AI may no longer run action types or tools. It can only suggest a test (draft + sample inputs); the suggestion appears in the Test output strip with a Run… button that opens the Test dialog pre-filled, and only the user decides whether anything executes.

Architecture: The MCP-only POST /compositions/{id}/agent/test route and the test_action_type / test_tool MCP tools are removed. A new MCP-only POST /compositions/{id}/agent/test-suggestions route stores a CompositionTestRun with the new status suggested (author ai, inputs, nothing executed) in the existing in-memory run store and fires the existing composition-test-run SSE event. A new MCP tool suggest_test(type, name, inputs) calls it. The UI renders suggested runs with a Run… button.

Tech Stack: as Phase 5 (Java 21/Quarkus, React/PatternFly, Node MCP server).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-workflow-workbench-design.md, amended by the user's decision (2026-10-13): only the user runs tests, because action types and tools can make permanent changes (GitHub issues, PRs, …). Builds on docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-workbench-phase5-testing.md.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• All Phase 5 Global Constraints still apply (contract-first REST, never ./build.sh/mvn clean/mvn install, test commands, code style, commits directly on feat/workflow-first, never push).
  • The AI must have no way to execute an action type or tool: no MCP tool, no MCP-only route, no allowed tool. Bash(jq *) stays the only shell permission.
  • New run status value: suggested. A suggested run has author: "ai", turnId (current turn), inputs, startedAt, and no durationMs, exitCode, stdout, stderr, outputs, problems or message.
  • Suggestions do not take a concurrency-cap permit and never call DraftTestRunner.
  • Exact texts:
  • MCP tool name: suggest_test; parameters type (action-type | tool, required), name (required), inputs (object, optional).
  • MCP tool result: Suggested a test of <type> <name> with inputs <json>. The user can run it from the Test output strip; ask them to tell you the result.
  • Template rule (replaces the Phase 5 "Test action types and tools you create…" rule): - You cannot run action types or tools. After creating or changing a node or script action type or a tool, call suggest_test with realistic sample inputs so the user can run it. Never claim it works until the user reports a passing run.
  • Working-loop step 3 becomes: 3. Create or update action types and tools with upsert_item and fix every INVALID result. For each node or script action type and each tool you create or change, call suggest_test with realistic sample inputs.
  • Strip: suggested row label Suggested by AI, summary Inputs: <json>, button Run….

docs.title: Run a Workflow from a Stream Event Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: On the event detail page (/events/stream/:id), the user can choose Run workflow…, pick any published workflow (workflows a subscription runs for this event listed first), optionally set a title, labels and inputs, and start a run from that event exactly as a subscription would. Runs started by the event (by subscriptions or manually) are listed in a new Runs tab.

Architecture: Extract the event → subject → run code from EventStreamOrchestrator.routeToCreateWorkflow into one shared method used by both subscriptions and the new manual endpoint. Manual runs pass EventOrigin(event.id, null) (no ledger entry) and get the label trigger=manual. Runs are listed by the existing runs endpoint with a new triggerEventId filter. Suggestions come from subscriptions whose create-workflow rules ran (ledger completed) for the event.

Tech Stack: Java 21/Quarkus/Panache, JUnit 5 + REST Assured; React 18 + PatternFly 6 + Vitest.

Spec: user decisions (2026-10-14): Run workflow… only on the event detail page; picker offers all published workflows with suggested ones first; results shown in a new Runs tab (no change to the processing trail).

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Contract-first REST (common/api/src/main/resources/openapi.json, edited programmatically, additions only); impl classes implement generated interfaces; generated beans for bodies.
  • Never run ./build.sh, mvn clean, mvn install. Backend tests: mvn -q -pl app -am test -Dtest=<Classes> -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false. UI (in ui/): timeout 250 npx tsc -b --noEmit, timeout 280 npx vitest run [paths].
  • Java: 4-space indent, Javadoc on public methods, explicit types, JUnit 5. Conventional commits on feat/workflow-first, no AI attribution, never push.
  • Subscription-triggered behaviour must not change (same subject resolution, same context.event, same ledger/outcome records, same conflict handling).
  • Manual runs: label trigger=manual (merged with user labels; the user cannot override trigger), EventOrigin(event.id, null), no ledger entry. Conflict (an active run of the same workflow for the subject) → HTTP 409 with the existing conflict message; unknown event or workflow → 404; workflow without a published version or invalid inputs → 400 (existing behaviour of triggerWorkflow).

docs.title: Workbench Chat Cards Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: In the workbench chat, show the AI's workbench tool calls as compact, readable cards ("Updated action type x · VALID", "Proposed 4 workflow changes", "Suggested a test for y") that link to what they affected, fold read-only calls into one quiet line, and keep the raw call one click away.

Architecture: AssistantMessageList/AssistantChatPanel gain an optional renderToolUse hook; when it returns content, it replaces the generic AssistantToolUseBlock (the Configuration Assistant is unchanged). The workbench supplies a WorkbenchToolCard renderer built from a pure describeToolCall function that parses the tool name, input and result text. Consecutive read-only workbench calls are grouped by a pure groupToolCalls pass. One small backend change makes upsert_item report created vs updated.

Tech Stack: React 18 + PatternFly 6 + Vitest (ui/), Java/Quarkus (one field), Node MCP server.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-workflow-workbench-design.md §2 "Right pane: chat" ("Compact cards for workbench tool calls, for example 'Updated action type add-comment' or 'Proposed 4 workflow changes'. Each card links to its tab.").

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Contract-first REST for the one schema change (AgentItemResult.created); never run ./build.sh, mvn clean, mvn install. Backend tests: mvn -q -pl app -am test -Dtest=<Classes> -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false. UI (in ui/): timeout 250 npx tsc -b --noEmit, timeout 280 npx vitest run [paths].
  • Code style: 4-space indent, doc comments on exported functions/public Java methods, explicit types, JUnit 5.
  • Conventional commits on feat/workflow-first, no AI attribution, never push.
  • Tool names: workbench MCP tools arrive as mcp__workbench__<tool> (Claude Code) or workbench_<tool> (OpenCode). Both must be recognised; anything else falls back to the generic block.
  • The Configuration Assistant and every non-workbench chat keep the generic AssistantToolUseBlock.
  • Every card expands to the raw input and result (reuse AssistantToolUseBlock inside the expansion) — nothing is hidden.
  • Permission prompts, errors and running (no result yet) calls must still be visible: a call that is waiting for permission is never replaced by a card (render the generic block).
  • Card texts (exact):
Tool Card text Link upsert_item, created Created <kind> <name> + status label open item tab upsert_item, updated Updated <kind> <name> + status label open item tab remove_item Removed <kind> <name> — propose_workflow_changes, applied Proposed <n> workflow change(s) + first 3 op summaries joined by , (+ and <k> more) open workflow tab, select first touched node propose_workflow_changes, rejected Workflow changes rejected: <reason> (danger) open workflow tab suggest_test Suggested a test for <kind> <name> open the suggestion's Run… (by item) evaluate_expression Evaluated <expression> → <value or error> — list_stream_events Looked at <n> stream event(s) — get_stream_event Read stream event <id> — read-only group (get_composition, get_item, validate_composition, axiom_*) Read the composition, Read <kind> <name>, Checked the composition, Looked up existing items; a group of several: Read <n> things with the list in the expansion —

<kind> is action type / tool / workflow. Status label: VALID (green), VALID with warnings (orange), INVALID (red). Op summaries: added <node name or id>, removed <id>, connected <a> → <b>, disconnected <edge id>, updated <id> (by op type; unknown op types → changed <id>).

docs.title: Task 2: describeToolCall and groupToolCalls (pure logic)
docs.text:
Files: Create ui/src/pages/workbench/toolCards.ts + toolCards.test.ts.

Interfaces (produced):

export type WorkbenchTool = "get_composition" | "get_item" | "upsert_item" | "remove_item"
    | "propose_workflow_changes" | "validate_composition" | "suggest_test" | "list_stream_events"
    | "get_stream_event" | "evaluate_expression" | "axiom_list_action_types" | "axiom_get_action_type"
    | "axiom_list_tools" | "axiom_get_tool" | "axiom_list_secrets";

/** Strips `mcp__workbench__` / `workbench_`; null when the name is not a workbench tool. */
export function workbenchTool(toolName: string): WorkbenchTool | null;

export type CardTarget =
    | { kind: "item"; itemType: "action-type" | "tool" | "workflow"; name: string }
    | { kind: "workflow"; nodeId?: string }
    | { kind: "suggestion"; itemType: "action-type" | "tool"; name: string };

export interface ToolCard {
    readOnly: boolean;
    /** Plain text of the card (exact texts in the plan's Global Constraints); used by tests and tooltips. */
    text: string;
    /** The leading verb phrase, e.g. "Updated action type"; the component renders it before `name`. */
    lead: string;
    /** Item, node or expression shown in monospace after `lead`, if any. */
    name?: string;
    /** Text after the name, e.g. op summaries or "→ value". */
    detail?: string;
    status?: "VALID" | "VALID with warnings" | "INVALID";
    variant: "default" | "danger";
    target?: CardTarget;
}

/** Describes a finished workbench tool call; null for unknown tools or calls without a result yet. */
export function describeToolCall(toolName: string, input: Record<string, unknown> | undefined,
                                 result: string | undefined, isError: boolean | undefined): ToolCard | null;

export interface ToolCallRef { id: string; toolName: string; card: ToolCard | null }
/** Groups consecutive read-only cards; non-read-only cards and null cards stay single. */
export function groupToolCalls(calls: ToolCallRef[]): ToolCallRef[][];

text always equals [lead, name, detail].filter(Boolean).join(" ").

Parsing rules (from server.js result formats): - upsert_item: first line ^(VALID with warnings|VALID|INVALID): (\S+?)/(.+?) \((created|updated), → status, type, name, created. Older results without (created|updated, → treat as Updated. - propose_workflow_changes: result starts with APPLIED → count input.changeSet.ops.length (input may be a JSON string — parse it), summaries from the ops; starts with REJECTED → danger card with the text after the first :. target.nodeId = first op's node id (op.node?.id ?? op.nodeId ?? op.id). - remove_item, suggest_test, get_item: from input.type/input.name. - evaluate_expression: result OK (<type>): <json> → → <json>; ERROR: <msg> → → error: <msg> (danger). - list_stream_events: count result lines (No stream events found. → 0). - isError === true → danger card with the first result line.

docs.title: Workbench Runs Tab and Run Analysis Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: The workbench shows the runs of the composition's (published) workflow in a new Runs tab of the bottom panel (next to Tests), lets the user open a run in a dialog with Flow's WorkflowViewer and the failing task's output and log, and lets the user ask the AI to analyze a failed run. The AI gets read-only MCP tools to read the composition's runs, a run's details (history, failure, task output and log) and its trace.

Architecture: The composition's workflow item's baseItemId is the published WorkflowDefinition id (null when never published). UI: the bottom strip becomes a tabbed panel (Tests | Runs). Runs are fetched with the existing GET /workflow/runs?definitionId= and refreshed (debounced) on the workflow-updated SSE event. The run dialog reuses the instance mapping from WorkflowRunDetailPage (extracted into a shared helper). MCP: new read-only tools in axiom-workbench-mcp/server.js call the existing public REST routes; the composition's definition id comes from the agent composition route.

Tech Stack: Java/Quarkus, Node MCP server, React/PatternFly/Vitest, @apitomy/flow-ui WorkflowViewer.

Spec: user decisions (2026-10-14): runs of the composition's workflow only (all versions); run details in a dialog with WorkflowViewer; "Ask AI to analyze" prefills the chat (the user sends).

  • The AI tools are read-only: they never start, cancel or change runs.
  • Exact UI texts: bottom tabs Tests and Runs (each with a count badge); Runs empty states: Publish the workflow to see its runs here. (no published definition) and No runs of this workflow yet.; run row action / dialog button Ask AI to analyze; dialog title Run #<id>: <title>; link Open run page.
  • Chat prefill for Ask AI (exact shape): Analyze run #<id> of workflow `<name>` (status: <status> at node `<currentNodeName>`): <failureReason or first failed task output line>. Find the cause and fix the workflow or its components. — omit the at node … part when unknown and the : <reason> part when there is no reason.

docs.title: Standard Workflow Inputs Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: A workflow's Start node declares which of two standard inputs (subject, event) it needs; Axiom satisfies exactly the declared ones when it creates a run, and refuses to create a run whose required inputs it cannot satisfy. Supplied/custom run inputs and Start defaultValues are removed.

Architecture: A new StandardInputs registry (Axiom app module) defines the inputs, their types and how to resolve them. WorkflowExecutionService builds the initial run context from the registry instead of hard-coded keys. Publish rules, the new-workflow scaffold, a new shadowing warning and the assistant reference all read the same registry. The Flow engine is unchanged.

Tech Stack: Java 25, Quarkus, Hibernate/Panache, JUnit 5 + RestAssured (@QuarkusTest), Apitomy Flow 3.0.2 (io.apitomy.flow.model.*), React + PatternFly 6 + Vitest (UI), OpenAPI 3.1 contract-first REST.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-standard-workflow-inputs-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Standard inputs are exactly subject (type object) and event (type object).
  • subject contains exactly id, name, type, ref, refSource, repository; missing/blank values are null.
  • A run's initial context contains only the standard inputs declared on its Start node.
  • Required-but-unsatisfiable message, verbatim: Cannot start workflow "<definition name>": required input(s) not available: <comma-separated names> returned as HTTP 400 with JSON body {"message": "..."}.
  • Shadowing warning code: SHADOWS_WORKFLOW_INPUT; message: Output '<key>' of node '<node name>' overwrites the workflow input '<key>' for later nodes.
  • Standard input names are not reserved; reading an undeclared standard input is not an error.
  • REST changes are contract-first: edit common/api/src/main/resources/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1, minimal diffs, no nullable), then implement the generated interfaces. Never add @Path to impl classes.
  • Schema changes edit app/src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__baseline.sql in place (no V2__).
  • Never run ./build.sh, mvn clean or mvn install. Backend tests: mvn -q -pl app -am test -Dtest=<Classes> -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false, results in app/target/surefire-reports/*.txt. UI (cwd ui/): timeout 250 npx tsc -b --noEmit, timeout 280 npx vitest run.
  • Commit only when the task's tests pass: chain with &&. Conventional commits, no AI attribution.
  • Java style: 4-space indent, Javadoc on public methods, explicit types (no ambiguous var).
  • Markdown docs wrap at 110 characters (except tables).

package io.apitomy.axiom.app;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;
import io.apitomy.axiom.core.entities.StreamEventEntity;
import io.apitomy.axiom.core.entities.SubjectEntity;
import io.apitomy.flow.model.Workflow;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.UUID;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertNull;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

/** Unit tests for the standard workflow inputs registry. */
class StandardInputsTest {

    private static final ObjectMapper MAPPER = new ObjectMapper();

    private static Workflow workflow(String startInputsJson) throws Exception {
        return MAPPER.readValue("""
            {"id": "w", "name": "W",
             "nodes": [
               {"id": "s", "type": "start", "name": "Start", "config": {"inputs": %s}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 0}},
               {"id": "e", "type": "end", "name": "End", "config": {}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 100}}],
             "edges": [{"id": "x", "source": "s", "target": "e", "priority": 0, "isDefault": false}]}
            """.formatted(startInputsJson), Workflow.class);
    }

    private static SubjectEntity subject() {
        SubjectEntity s = new SubjectEntity();
        s.id = 7L;
        s.name = "PR 12";
        s.type = "pull-request";
        s.ref = "https://github.com/o/r/pull/12";
        s.refSource = "github";
        s.repository = " ";
        return s;
    }

    @Test
    void registryListsSubjectAndEvent() {
        assertEquals(List.of("subject", "event"), StandardInputs.ALL.stream().map(StandardInputs.StandardInput::name).toList());
        assertEquals("object", StandardInputs.find("subject").orElseThrow().type());
        assertTrue(StandardInputs.find("ref").isEmpty());
    }

    @Test
    void subjectValueHasExactlyTheSixFieldsWithBlankAsNull() {
        Map<String, Object> value = StandardInputs.subjectValue(subject());
        assertEquals(List.of("id", "name", "type", "ref", "refSource", "repository"), List.copyOf(value.keySet()));
        assertEquals(7L, value.get("id"));
        assertEquals("PR 12", value.get("name"));
        assertNull(value.get("repository"));
    }

    @Test
    void eventValueIsTheEnvelope() {
        StreamEventEntity e = new StreamEventEntity();
        e.id = UUID.randomUUID();
        e.type = "issue.created";
        e.source = "github";
        e.eventSourceId = "gh";
        e.ref = "r";
        e.timestamp = Instant.parse("2026-10-15T00:00:00Z");
        e.payload = "{\"a\": 1}";
        ObjectNode node = StandardInputs.eventValue(e, MAPPER);
        assertEquals("issue.created", node.path("type").asText());
        assertEquals(1, node.path("payload").path("a").asInt());
        assertFalse(node.has("actor"));
    }

    @Test
    void resolvesOnlyDeclaredInputs() throws Exception {
        StandardInputs.Resolution r = StandardInputs.resolve(
                workflow("[{\"name\": \"subject\", \"type\": \"object\", \"required\": true}]"), subject(),
                MAPPER.readTree("{\"type\": \"t\"}"));
        assertEquals(List.of("subject"), List.copyOf(r.context().keySet()));
        assertTrue(r.missingRequired().isEmpty());
    }

    @Test
    void optionalUnavailableEventIsAbsentAndRequiredIsReported() throws Exception {
        StandardInputs.Resolution optional = StandardInputs.resolve(
                workflow("[{\"name\": \"event\", \"type\": \"object\", \"required\": false}]"), subject(), null);
        assertFalse(optional.context().containsKey("event"));
        assertTrue(optional.missingRequired().isEmpty());

        StandardInputs.Resolution required = StandardInputs.resolve(
                workflow("[{\"name\": \"event\", \"type\": \"object\", \"required\": true}]"), subject(), null);
        assertEquals(List.of("event"), required.missingRequired());
    }

    @Test
    void noDeclaredInputsGivesEmptyContext() throws Exception {
        JsonNode event = MAPPER.readTree("{}");
        assertTrue(StandardInputs.resolve(workflow("[]"), subject(), event).context().isEmpty());
    }
}

package io.apitomy.axiom.app;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;
import io.apitomy.axiom.core.entities.StreamEventEntity;
import io.apitomy.axiom.core.entities.SubjectEntity;
import io.apitomy.flow.model.NodeConfig;
import io.apitomy.flow.model.NodeType;
import io.apitomy.flow.model.Workflow;
import io.apitomy.flow.model.WorkflowNode;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * The standard workflow inputs: the only inputs a Start node may declare, and the only values Axiom puts into a
 * new run's context. A run receives exactly the standard inputs its Start node declares.
 */
public final class StandardInputs {

    /** The subject the run is about. */
    public static final String SUBJECT = "subject";
    /** The stream event that started the run. */
    public static final String EVENT = "event";

    /**
     * A standard input.
     *
     * @param name         the input name
     * @param type         the Start input type
     * @param description  what the value is
     * @param availability when Axiom can provide it
     */
    public record StandardInput(String name, String type, String description, String availability) {
    }

    /** The fields of the {@code subject} input, in order. */
    public static final List<String> SUBJECT_FIELDS = List.of("id", "name", "type", "ref", "refSource", "repository");

    /** All standard inputs. */
    public static final List<StandardInput> ALL = List.of(
            new StandardInput(SUBJECT, "object",
                    "The subject the run is about: " + String.join(", ", SUBJECT_FIELDS)
                            + " (id is a number; the others are strings or null)",
                    "always"),
            new StandardInput(EVENT, "object",
                    "The event that started the run: id, type, source, eventSourceId, ref, timestamp, actor, payload",
                    "only when the run was started from a stream event"));

    /**
     * The result of resolving a workflow's declared inputs.
     *
     * @param context         the initial run context (declared and available inputs only)
     * @param missingRequired declared required inputs that are not available, in declaration order
     */
    public record Resolution(Map<String, Object> context, List<String> missingRequired) {
    }

    private StandardInputs() {
    }

    /**
     * Finds a standard input by name.
     *
     * @param name the input name
     * @return the input, or empty when the name is not a standard input
     */
    public static Optional<StandardInput> find(String name) {
        return ALL.stream().filter(i -> i.name().equals(name)).findFirst();
    }

    /**
     * Returns the standard input names.
     *
     * @return the names
     */
    public static Set<String> names() {
        return ALL.stream().map(StandardInput::name).collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet());
    }

    /**
     * Builds the {@code subject} input value: exactly {@link #SUBJECT_FIELDS}, blank strings as null.
     *
     * @param subject the run's subject
     * @return the value (insertion-ordered, may contain nulls)
     */
    public static Map<String, Object> subjectValue(SubjectEntity subject) {
        Map<String, Object> value = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        value.put("id", subject.id);
        value.put("name", blankToNull(subject.name));
        value.put("type", blankToNull(subject.type));
        value.put("ref", blankToNull(subject.ref));
        value.put("refSource", blankToNull(subject.refSource));
        value.put("repository", blankToNull(subject.repository));
        return value;
    }

    /**
     * Builds the {@code event} input value: the event envelope, with actor and payload parsed as JSON.
     *
     * @param event  the stream event
     * @param mapper the JSON mapper
     * @return the value
     */
    public static ObjectNode eventValue(StreamEventEntity event, ObjectMapper mapper) {
        ObjectNode node = mapper.createObjectNode();
        node.put("id", event.id.toString());
        node.put("type", event.type);
        node.put("source", event.source);
        node.put("eventSourceId", event.eventSourceId);
        node.put("ref", event.ref);
        node.put("timestamp", event.timestamp != null ? event.timestamp.toString() : null);
        try {
            if (event.actor != null) {
                node.set("actor", mapper.readTree(event.actor));
            }
            if (event.payload != null) {
                node.set("payload", mapper.readTree(event.payload));
            }
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Invalid JSON in stream event " + event.id + ": " + e.getMessage(), e);
        }
        return node;
    }

    /**
     * Resolves the Start node's declared inputs for a new run. Undeclared and unknown names are ignored here
     * (publish rejects unknown names).
     *
     * @param workflow the workflow being started
     * @param subject  the run's subject
     * @param event    the {@code event} value when started from a stream event, else null
     * @return the context to start with and any required inputs that are not available
     */
    public static Resolution resolve(Workflow workflow, SubjectEntity subject, JsonNode event) {
        Map<String, Object> context = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        List<String> missing = new ArrayList<>();
        for (NodeConfig.Field field : startInputs(workflow)) {
            String name = field.name();
            Object value = switch (name == null ? "" : name) {
                case SUBJECT -> subjectValue(subject);
                case EVENT -> event;
                default -> null;
            };
            if (find(name).isEmpty()) {
                continue;
            }
            if (value != null) {
                context.put(name, value);
            } else if (field.required()) {
                missing.add(name);
            }
        }
        return new Resolution(context, missing);
    }

    private static List<NodeConfig.Field> startInputs(Workflow workflow) {
        if (workflow.nodes() == null) {
            return List.of();
        }
        for (WorkflowNode node : workflow.nodes()) {
            if (node.type() == NodeType.START && node.typedConfig() instanceof NodeConfig.Start start) {
                return start.inputs();
            }
        }
        return List.of();
    }

    private static String blankToNull(String value) {
        return value == null || value.isBlank() ? null : value;
    }
}

docs.text:
Files: - Modify: app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/RunRequest.java - Modify: app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/WorkflowExecutionService.java (constants ~line 66-70; overloads ~lines 115-172; applyStartInputDefaults ~175-200; startRun ~200-330) - Modify: app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/EventStreamOrchestrator.java (startRunFromEvent ~770-810; routeToCreateWorkflow ~724) - Modify: app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/rest/SubjectsResourceImpl.java (~390) - Modify: app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/rest/StreamEventsResourceImpl.java (~215) - Modify: app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/rest/WorkflowDefinitionsResourceImpl.java (rerunWorkflowRun ~505-528) - Modify: app/src/main/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/WorkflowScheduleTriggerScheduler.java (startRun ~166-176) - Rewrite: app/src/test/java/io/apitomy/axiom/app/WorkflowTriggerInputGuardTest.java - Modify tests: WorkflowRunMetadataTest.java, WorkflowInstanceResourceTest.java, and every test that no longer compiles (see Step 6)

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 1 StandardInputs.resolve, StandardInputs.eventValue, StandardInputs.EVENT. - Produces: - record RunRequest(String title, Map<String, String> labels) with RunRequest.EMPTY. - WorkflowExecutionService.triggerWorkflow(long subjectId, long definitionId, RunRequest request, EventOrigin origin) — when origin != null, the event input is built from StreamEventEntity.findById(origin.eventId()). - WorkflowExecutionService.triggerWorkflow(long subjectId, long definitionId) (unchanged). - The triggerWorkflow(..., Map<String, Object> extraContext, ...) overloads are removed. - EventStreamOrchestrator.startRunFromEvent(StreamEventEntity, long, RunRequest, Long) (signature unchanged; no longer builds the event node). - Stored workflow_run.inputs = JSON of the resolved context without event; null when empty.

  • [ ] Step 1: Write the failing integration test — replace the whole of WorkflowTriggerInputGuardTest.java with:
package io.apitomy.axiom.app;

import io.apitomy.axiom.core.entities.StreamEventEntity;
import io.apitomy.axiom.core.entities.WorkflowRunEntity;
import io.quarkus.narayana.jta.QuarkusTransaction;
import io.quarkus.test.junit.QuarkusTest;
import io.restassured.http.ContentType;
import jakarta.inject.Inject;
import jakarta.ws.rs.WebApplicationException;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.UUID;

import static io.restassured.RestAssured.given;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.equalTo;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.nullValue;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertThrows;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

/** A run's initial context holds exactly the declared standard inputs; required ones must be available. */
@QuarkusTest
class WorkflowTriggerInputGuardTest {

    @Inject
    WorkflowExecutionService service;

    @Inject
    EventStreamOrchestrator orchestrator;

    /** Start → wait (keeps the run active so its context can be read) → end, with the given Start inputs. */
    private static String content(String inputs) {
        return """
            {"id": "in-wf", "name": "Inputs WF",
             "nodes": [
               {"id": "s1", "type": "start", "name": "Start", "config": {"inputs": %s}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 0}},
               {"id": "w1", "type": "wait", "name": "Hold", "config": {"duration": "PT1H"}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 100}},
               {"id": "e1", "type": "end", "name": "End", "config": {}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 200}}],
             "edges": [
               {"id": "x1", "source": "s1", "target": "w1", "priority": 0, "isDefault": false},
               {"id": "x2", "source": "w1", "target": "e1", "priority": 0, "isDefault": false}]}
            """.formatted(inputs);
    }

    private static final String SUBJECT_REQUIRED = "[{\"name\": \"subject\", \"type\": \"object\", \"required\": true}]";
    private static final String EVENT_REQUIRED = "[{\"name\": \"event\", \"type\": \"object\", \"required\": true}]";
    private static final String EVENT_OPTIONAL = "[{\"name\": \"event\", \"type\": \"object\", \"required\": false}]";

    private static UUID event() {
        UUID id = UUID.randomUUID();
        QuarkusTransaction.requiringNew().run(() -> {
            StreamEventEntity e = new StreamEventEntity();
            e.id = id;
            e.sourceEventId = "inputs-" + id;
            e.source = "github";
            e.eventSourceId = "conn-inputs";
            e.type = "issue.created";
            e.ref = "test/inputs-event-" + id;
            e.timestamp = Instant.now();
            e.payload = "{\"n\": 5}";
            e.createdOn = Instant.now();
            e.persist();
        });
        return id;
    }

    @Test
    void contextHoldsOnlyTheDeclaredSubject() {
        long subjectId = TestFixtures.createSubject("inputs-subject-only");
        long defId = TestFixtures.createDefinition("Inputs Subject Only", content(SUBJECT_REQUIRED));
        given().contentType(ContentType.JSON).body("{\"workflowDefinitionId\": %d}".formatted(defId))
                .when().post("/api/v1/subjects/" + subjectId + "/workflow")
                .then().statusCode(200)
                .body("context.subject.id", equalTo((int) subjectId))
                .body("context.subject.name", equalTo("inputs-subject-only"))
                .body("context.subject.repository", nullValue())
                .body("context.ref", nullValue())
                .body("context.subjectId", nullValue())
                .body("context.event", nullValue())
                .body("inputs.subject.ref", equalTo("test/inputs-subject-only"));
    }

    @Test
    void noDeclaredInputsGivesAnEmptyContext() {
        long subjectId = TestFixtures.createSubject("inputs-none");
        long defId = TestFixtures.createWaitDefinition("Inputs None");
        WorkflowRunEntity run = QuarkusTransaction.requiringNew().call(() ->
                service.triggerWorkflow(subjectId, defId, RunRequest.EMPTY, null));
        given().when().get("/api/v1/workflow/runs/" + run.id)
                .then().statusCode(200).body("context.subject", nullValue()).body("inputs", nullValue());
    }

    @Test
    void requiredEventWithoutAnEventFailsWithNamedInput() {
        long subjectId = TestFixtures.createSubject("inputs-no-event");
        long defId = TestFixtures.createDefinition("Needs Event", content(EVENT_REQUIRED));
        given().contentType(ContentType.JSON).body("{\"workflowDefinitionId\": %d}".formatted(defId))
                .when().post("/api/v1/subjects/" + subjectId + "/workflow")
                .then().statusCode(400)
                .body("message", equalTo(
                        "Cannot start workflow \"Needs Event\": required input(s) not available: event"));
        long runs = QuarkusTransaction.requiringNew().call(() ->
                WorkflowRunEntity.count("subjectId = ?1 and definitionId = ?2", subjectId, defId));
        assertEquals(0, runs);
    }

    @Test
    void failureMessageIsTheExceptionMessage() {
        long subjectId = TestFixtures.createSubject("inputs-no-event-msg");
        long defId = TestFixtures.createDefinition("Needs Event Msg", content(EVENT_REQUIRED));
        WebApplicationException e = assertThrows(WebApplicationException.class, () ->
                QuarkusTransaction.requiringNew().call(() ->
                        service.triggerWorkflow(subjectId, defId, RunRequest.EMPTY, null)));
        assertTrue(e.getMessage().contains("required input(s) not available: event"), e.getMessage());
    }

    @Test
    void optionalEventIsAbsentWithoutAnEvent() {
        long subjectId = TestFixtures.createSubject("inputs-optional-event");
        long defId = TestFixtures.createDefinition("Optional Event", content(EVENT_OPTIONAL));
        given().contentType(ContentType.JSON).body("{\"workflowDefinitionId\": %d}".formatted(defId))
                .when().post("/api/v1/subjects/" + subjectId + "/workflow")
                .then().statusCode(200).body("context.event", nullValue());
    }

    @Test
    void eventStartedRunGetsTheEventButNotInItsStoredInputs() {
        UUID eventId = event();
        long defId = TestFixtures.createDefinition("Event Run",
                content("[{\"name\": \"subject\", \"type\": \"object\", \"required\": true},"
                        + " {\"name\": \"event\", \"type\": \"object\", \"required\": true}]"));
        given().contentType(ContentType.JSON).body("{\"workflowDefinitionId\": %d}".formatted(defId))
                .when().post("/api/v1/stream/events/" + eventId + "/runs")
                .then().statusCode(200)
                .body("context.event.type", equalTo("issue.created"))
                .body("context.event.payload.n", equalTo(5))
                .body("inputs.event", nullValue())
                .body("inputs.subject.id", org.hamcrest.Matchers.notNullValue());
    }
}

  • [ ] Step 3: Change RunRequest — replace the record with:
package io.apitomy.axiom.app;

import java.util.Map;

/**
 * Optional parameters for starting a workflow run. A run's inputs are not supplied: Axiom resolves the standard
 * inputs its Start node declares (see {@link StandardInputs}).
 *
 * @param title  run title; null for none
 * @param labels run labels; null for none
 */
public record RunRequest(String title, Map<String, String> labels) {

    /** An empty request. */
    public static final RunRequest EMPTY = new RunRequest(null, null);
}

  • [ ] Step 4: Rewrite context building in WorkflowExecutionService

  • Delete the PROTECTED_INPUTS constant and the whole applyStartInputDefaults method (with its Javadoc).

  • Delete the two triggerWorkflow overloads that take Map<String, Object> extraContext (the ones at ~lines 139 and 157, with their Javadoc). Keep triggerWorkflow(long, long, RunRequest, EventOrigin) and triggerWorkflow(long, long).
  • In startRun, replace everything from Map<String, Object> context = new HashMap<>(); through applyStartInputDefaults(workflow, context); with:
        JsonNode eventValue = null;
        if (origin != null && origin.eventId() != null) {
            StreamEventEntity event = StreamEventEntity.findById(origin.eventId());
            if (event != null) {
                eventValue = StandardInputs.eventValue(event, objectMapper);
            }
        }
        StandardInputs.Resolution resolution = StandardInputs.resolve(workflow, subject, eventValue);
        if (!resolution.missingRequired().isEmpty()) {
            String message = "Cannot start workflow \"" + definition.name + "\": required input(s) not available: "
                    + String.join(", ", resolution.missingRequired());
            // The message constructor keeps getMessage() meaningful for schedule trigger outcomes.
            throw new WebApplicationException(message,
                    Response.status(400).entity(Map.of("message", message)).build());
        }
        Map<String, Object> context = new HashMap<>(resolution.context());
  1. Replace entity.inputs = toJsonOrNull(request.inputs()); with:
        Map<String, Object> storedInputs = new LinkedHashMap<>(resolution.context());
        storedInputs.remove(StandardInputs.EVENT); // the event is linked as the run's trigger
        entity.inputs = storedInputs.isEmpty() ? null : toJsonOrNull(storedInputs);

  1. Add imports as needed: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode, io.apitomy.axiom.core.entities.StreamEventEntity, java.util.LinkedHashMap. Remove imports that become unused (NodeConfig only if no longer referenced elsewhere in the file — check with grep).

  2. [ ] Step 5: Update the callers

EventStreamOrchestrator — in the private startRunFromEvent(StreamEventEntity, Long, long, RunRequest, Long) delete the event-node building (the extraContext map, the try/catch that builds eventNode, and the effective request) so the method body becomes:

        WorkflowRunEntity run = QuarkusTransaction.requiringNew().call(() ->
                workflowExecutionService.triggerWorkflow(subjectId, definitionId, request,
                        new EventOrigin(event.id, ledgerId)));
        LOG.infof("Created workflow (definition %d) for event %s on subject %d",
                definitionId, event.id, subjectId);

        sseEvents.fire(SseEvent.subjectUpdated(subjectId));
        return run;

Update both Javadocs of startRunFromEvent (@param request run title and labels; "the run's event input is the event when its Start node declares event"). In routeToCreateWorkflow replace new RunRequest(null, null, null, null) with RunRequest.EMPTY.

SubjectsResourceImpl.triggerSubjectWorkflow — build the request without inputs:

        RunRequest request = new RunRequest(data.getTitle(),
                toStringMap(data.getLabels() != null ? data.getLabels().getAdditionalProperties() : null));

StreamEventsResourceImpl.triggerStreamEventWorkflow — RunRequest request = new RunRequest(data.getTitle(), labels);

WorkflowDefinitionsResourceImpl.rerunWorkflowRun — delete the inputs lines and build new io.apitomy.axiom.app.RunRequest(original.title, labels). Keep the event/no-event branching.

WorkflowScheduleTriggerScheduler.startRun — temporarily ignore attempt.inputs() (Task 3 removes it):

    private void startRun(Attempt attempt) {
        workflowExecutionService.triggerWorkflow(attempt.subjectId(), attempt.definitionId(),
                new RunRequest(null, Map.of("trigger", "schedule")), null);
    }

(Remove the now-unused TypeReference import if nothing else uses it.)

  • [ ] Step 6: Fix the remaining tests

Run mvn -q -pl app -am test-compile 2>&1 | grep ERROR and fix every compile error: - new RunRequest(a, b, c, d) → new RunRequest(a, b) (drop inputs and extra context). - Calls to the removed triggerWorkflow(..., Map extraContext, ...) overloads: if the test only needed an event, start the run through orchestrator.startRunFromEvent(event, definitionId, RunRequest.EMPTY, null) with a persisted StreamEventEntity (see event() in Step 1) and declare event on the Start node; if it passed other keys, the behaviour no longer exists — delete that test.

Then update behaviour tests: - WorkflowRunMetadataTest: delete contextContainsSubjectNameAndRepository, suppliedInputsCannotOverrideRepositoryOrSubjectName, extraContextCannotOverrideRepository and nullRepositoryYieldsEmptyString (covered by Task 1 and Step 1); in suppliedMetadataIsPersisted drop the inputs part and assert only title and labels. - WorkflowInstanceResourceTest: delete appliesStartInputDefaultsForInputsNotSupplied and any test that posts inputs. - WorkflowScheduleTriggerSchedulerTest.firstFiringCreatesSubjectAndStartsRun: delete the line assertTrue(runs.get(0).inputs.contains("high"), "static inputs are passed to the run"); (the trigger's inputs are now ignored; Task 3 removes them). - Any test workflow whose nodes read context.ref, context.subjectId, context.subjectName or context.repository must declare subject on its Start node and read context.subject.<field> instead; WorkflowRunTitleTest.workflowSdkNodeSetsItsOwnRunTitle changes its title expression to 'Checking ' += context.subject.name and declares subject.

  • [ ] Step 7: Run the full backend suite

Run: mvn -q -pl app -am test > /tmp/opencode/apptest.log 2>&1; grep -L "Failures: 0, Errors: 0" app/target/surefire-reports/*.txt Expected: no file names printed. Fix any failure caused by tests relying on the old always-injected keys (same rule as Step 6).

package io.apitomy.axiom.app.validation;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import io.apitomy.flow.model.Workflow;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.util.Optional;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

/** Start input publish rules: only standard inputs, with their types, and no defaults. */
class WorkflowContentRulesStartInputsTest {

    private static Optional<String> violation(String inputs) throws Exception {
        Workflow wf = new ObjectMapper().readValue("""
            {"id": "w", "name": "W",
             "nodes": [{"id": "s", "type": "start", "name": "Start", "config": {"inputs": %s}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 0}},
                       {"id": "e", "type": "end", "name": "End", "config": {}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 100}}],
             "edges": [{"id": "x", "source": "s", "target": "e", "priority": 0, "isDefault": false}]}
            """.formatted(inputs), Workflow.class);
        return WorkflowContentRules.startInputViolation(wf);
    }

    @Test
    void standardInputsAreValidAndEventMayBeRequired() throws Exception {
        assertTrue(violation("[{\"name\": \"subject\", \"type\": \"object\", \"required\": true},"
                + " {\"name\": \"event\", \"type\": \"object\", \"required\": true}]").isEmpty());
        assertTrue(violation("[{\"name\": \"event\", \"required\": false}]").isEmpty());
    }

    @Test
    void nonStandardNameIsRejected() throws Exception {
        assertEquals(Optional.of("Start node input 'ref' is not a standard input. A Start node may declare only: "
                + "subject, event."), violation("[{\"name\": \"ref\", \"type\": \"string\"}]"));
    }

    @Test
    void wrongTypeIsRejected() throws Exception {
        assertEquals(Optional.of("Start node input 'subject' must have type 'object', not 'string'."),
                violation("[{\"name\": \"subject\", \"type\": \"string\"}]"));
    }

    @Test
    void defaultValueIsRejected() throws Exception {
        assertEquals(Optional.of("Start node input 'event' cannot declare a defaultValue; Axiom provides "
                + "standard inputs itself."),
                violation("[{\"name\": \"event\", \"type\": \"object\", \"defaultValue\": {}}]"));
    }
}

  • [ ] Step 3: Implement the rules — in WorkflowContentRules delete OPTIONAL_BUILT_IN_INPUTS and replace the body of startInputViolation's loop (after the INPUT_NAME_PATTERN check, which stays) with:
            Optional<StandardInputs.StandardInput> standard = StandardInputs.find(name);
            if (standard.isEmpty()) {
                return Optional.of("Start node input '" + name + "' is not a standard input. A Start node may "
                        + "declare only: " + StandardInputs.ALL.stream().map(StandardInputs.StandardInput::name)
                                .collect(java.util.stream.Collectors.joining(", ")) + ".");
            }
            Object type = input.get("type");
            if (type != null && !type.toString().isBlank() && !standard.get().type().equals(type.toString())) {
                return Optional.of("Start node input '" + name + "' must have type '" + standard.get().type()
                        + "', not '" + type + "'.");
            }
            if (input.containsKey("defaultValue") && input.get("defaultValue") != null) {
                return Optional.of("Start node input '" + name + "' cannot declare a defaultValue; Axiom "

    /**
     * Builds declared output names for the given action types.
     *
     * @param actionTypes the action type entities
     * @return action type name to output names
     */
    public static Map<String, Set<String>> actionTypeOutputs(List<ActionTypeEntity> actionTypes) {
        Map<String, Set<String>> result = new HashMap<>();
        for (ActionTypeEntity at : actionTypes) {
            Set<String> outputs = new HashSet<>();
            if (at.outputs != null) {
                at.outputs.forEach(f -> outputs.add(f.name));
            }
            result.put(at.name, outputs);

        return result;

    private static Map<String, Set<String>> pendingOutputs(Iterable<JsonNode> actionTypes) {
        Map<String, Set<String>> result = new HashMap<>();
        if (actionTypes == null) {
            return result;
        }
        for (JsonNode item : actionTypes) {
            String name = item.path("name").asText("");
            if (name.isBlank()) {
                continue;
            }
            Set<String> outputs = new HashSet<>();
            item.path("outputs").forEach(o -> {
                String n = o.path("name").asText("");
                if (!n.isBlank()) {
                    outputs.add(n);
                }
            });
            result.put(name, outputs);
        }
        return result;
    }

    private static Map<String, Set<String>> overlayOutputs(Map<String, Set<String>> base,
                                                          Map<String, Set<String>> pending) {
        Map<String, Set<String>> result = new HashMap<>(base != null ? base : Map.of());
        result.putAll(pending);
        return result;
    }

    /**
     * A node output that overwrites a declared workflow input.
     *
     * @param nodeIndex the node's index in {@code content.nodes}
     * @param key       the context key written
     * @param message   the warning message
     */
    public record ShadowProblem(int nodeIndex, String key, String message) {

        /** @return the JSON path of the node's config relative to the workflow item */
        public String path() {
            return "content.nodes[" + nodeIndex + "].config";
        }
    }

    /**
     * Finds nodes whose statically known outputs would overwrite an input declared on the Start node: action
     * node outputs (renamed by their {@code contextKey}), the action type's declared outputs the node does not
     * rename, human-task outputs and receive-event output mappings. {@code sdk:} results are not declared and
     * are not checked.
     *
     * @param workflow          the workflow
     * @param actionTypeOutputs action type name to declared output names; null to skip action type outputs
     * @return one problem per node and overwritten input
     */
    public static List<ShadowProblem> shadowProblems(Workflow workflow, Map<String, Set<String>> actionTypeOutputs) {
        List<ShadowProblem> problems = new ArrayList<>();
        List<WorkflowNode> nodes = workflow.nodes() != null ? workflow.nodes() : List.of();
        Set<String> declared = new HashSet<>();
        for (WorkflowNode node : nodes) {
            if (node.type() == NodeType.START && node.config() != null) {
                try {
                    if (node.typedConfig() instanceof NodeConfig.Start start) {
                        start.inputs().forEach(f -> addKey(declared, f.name()));
                    }
                } catch (RuntimeException e) {
                    // Malformed config is reported by the engine validator.
                }
            }
        }
        if (declared.isEmpty()) {
            return problems;
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < nodes.size(); i++) {
            WorkflowNode node = nodes.get(i);
            Set<String> written = new java.util.LinkedHashSet<>();
            try {
                switch (node.typedConfig()) {
                    case NodeConfig.Action action -> {
                        Set<String> renamed = new HashSet<>();
                        action.outputs().forEach(f -> {
                            addKey(written, f.effectiveContextKey());
                            addKey(renamed, f.name());
                        });
                        if (actionTypeOutputs != null && action.actionType() != null) {
                            actionTypeOutputs.getOrDefault(action.actionType(), Set.of()).stream()
                                    .filter(o -> !renamed.contains(o)).forEach(o -> addKey(written, o));
                        }
                    }
                    case NodeConfig.HumanTask task -> task.outputs().forEach(f -> addKey(written, f.effectiveContextKey()));
                    case NodeConfig.ReceiveEvent receive -> receive.outputs().forEach(m -> addKey(written, m.contextKey()));
                    default -> {
                    }
                }
            } catch (RuntimeException e) {
                continue;
            }
            for (String key : written) {
                if (declared.contains(key)) {
                    problems.add(new ShadowProblem(i, key, "Output '" + key + "' of node '" + node.name()
                            + "' overwrites the workflow input '" + key + "' for later nodes."));
                }
            }
        }
        return problems;
    }

docs.title: Workbench Subscriptions Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Compositions can hold subscription items that start (create-workflow) or feed (workflow-dispatch) their own workflow; publishing creates them disabled and an explicit Enabled switch turns automation on.

Architecture: subscription joins the composition item types (contract enums, CompositionItems, CompositionService). CompositionValidator adds composition-specific subscription rules. CompositionPublisher adds the subscription→workflow dependency and controls enabled/processEventsFrom before the pack import. A new endpoint toggles enabled. The existing POST /subscriptions/preview gains error info and backs a new AI tool and a UI panel. The workbench UI gets a Subscriptions group and a subscription editor.

Tech Stack: Java 25, Quarkus, Panache, JUnit 5 + RestAssured; OpenAPI 3.1 contract-first (generated JAX-RS interfaces/beans in io.apitomy.axiom.api.beans); Node (workbench MCP server, node:test); React 19 + PatternFly 6 + Vitest.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-workbench-subscriptions-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Item type JSON name: subscription. Draft content = pack form {name, description, filterExpression, routing, labels}.
  • Validation codes, verbatim: FOREIGN_WORKFLOW_ROUTE (error), ENABLED_IGNORED (warning), OVERLAPPING_SUBSCRIPTION (warning).
  • ENABLED_IGNORED message, verbatim: Subscriptions are published disabled; enable them in the workbench after publishing.
  • Publish never changes an existing subscription's enabled or processEventsFrom; new ones are created with enabled = false.
  • Enable endpoint: PUT /compositions/{compositionId}/items/{itemId}/enabled, body {"enabled": boolean}; 404 unknown item; 409 not a subscription or not published; enabling sets processEventsFrom = now.
  • Preview: existing POST /subscriptions/preview with limit: 200; response gains errorCount and firstError.
  • New workbench tool name: preview_subscription; allowed tool mcp__workbench__preview_subscription.
  • New prompt rule, verbatim: - Never say the automation is live: published subscriptions stay disabled until the user enables them in the workbench.
  • Contract-first REST: edit common/api/src/main/resources/openapi.json with minimal textual diffs (no reformatting, no nullable); implement generated interfaces; no @Path on impl classes.
  • Never run ./build.sh, mvn clean or mvn install. Backend: mvn -q -pl app -am test -Dtest=<Classes> -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false; full suite: mvn -q -pl app -am test > /tmp/opencode/apptest.log 2>&1; grep -L "Failures: 0, Errors: 0" app/target/surefire-reports/*.txt (expect no output; delete stale reports first). UI (cwd ui/): timeout 250 npx tsc -b --noEmit, timeout 280 npx vitest run. Node: node --test app/src/test/node/*.test.js.
  • LineageTest.queryCountDoesNotGrowWithFanOut is known-flaky: if it alone fails, re-run once.
  • Commit only when the task's suites pass; chain with &&. Conventional commits; no AI attribution.
  • Java: 4-space indent, Javadoc on public methods, explicit types. TS: JSDoc on exported functions.
  • Markdown docs wrapped at 110 characters (except tables).

    private CompositionItemEntity subscription(long compositionId, String name, String routingJson,
                                               boolean withEnabled) throws Exception {
        CompositionItemEntity item = service.addBlank(compositionId, ConfigItemType.SUBSCRIPTION, name);
        ObjectNode content = (ObjectNode) service.contentOf(item);
        content.put("filterExpression", "event.type == 'pr.created'");

    private static List<ConfigProblem> codes(List<ConfigProblem> problems, String code) {

    /**
     * Validates one item in configuration-pack form: the generic configuration checks plus the composition's own
     * rules (for subscriptions: routes only to this composition's workflow, no draft {@code enabled}, and a
     * warning when another enabled subscription already starts the workflow).
     *
     * @param compositionId the composition id
     * @param type the item type
     * @param packItem the item in configuration-pack form
     * @param context the validation context
     * @return the problems
     */
    public List<ConfigProblem> validateItem(long compositionId, ConfigItemType type, ObjectNode packItem,
                                            ValidationContext context) {
        List<ConfigProblem> problems = new ArrayList<>(validationService.validate(type, packItem, context));
        if (type == ConfigItemType.SUBSCRIPTION) {
            problems.addAll(subscriptionProblems(compositionId, packItem));
        }
        return problems;
    }

    private List<ConfigProblem> subscriptionProblems(long compositionId, JsonNode subscription) {
        List<ConfigProblem> problems = new ArrayList<>();
        List<CompositionItemEntity> items = service.items(compositionId);
        String workflowName = items.stream().filter(i -> ConfigItemType.WORKFLOW.jsonName().equals(i.itemType))
                .map(i -> i.name).findFirst().orElse(null);
        if (subscription.has("enabled")) {
            problems.add(ConfigProblem.warning("enabled", "ENABLED_IGNORED",
                    "Subscriptions are published disabled; enable them in the workbench after publishing."));
        }
        JsonNode routing = subscription.path("routing");
        for (int i = 0; i < routing.size(); i++) {
            JsonNode rule = routing.get(i);
            if (!"create-workflow".equals(rule.path("type").asText())) {
                continue;
            }
            boolean own = !rule.has("workflowDefinitionId") && workflowName != null
                    && workflowName.equals(rule.path("workflowDefinitionName").asText());
            if (!own) {
                problems.add(ConfigProblem.error("routing[" + i + "]", "FOREIGN_WORKFLOW_ROUTE",
                        "A create-workflow rule must start this composition's workflow: set "
                                + "workflowDefinitionName to '" + workflowName + "'."));
            }
        }
        if (workflowName != null && !CompositionItems.referencedWorkflows(subscription).isEmpty()) {
            WorkflowDefinitionEntity definition = WorkflowDefinitionEntity.find("name", workflowName).firstResult();
            if (definition != null) {
                Set<Long> owned = items.stream()
                        .filter(i -> ConfigItemType.SUBSCRIPTION.jsonName().equals(i.itemType) && i.baseItemId != null)
                        .map(i -> i.baseItemId).collect(Collectors.toSet());
                for (EventSubscriptionEntity other : EventSubscriptionEntity.<EventSubscriptionEntity>list("enabled", true)) {
                    if (!owned.contains(other.id) && startsWorkflow(other, definition.id)) {
                        problems.add(ConfigProblem.warning("routing", "OVERLAPPING_SUBSCRIPTION",
                                "Enabled subscription '" + other.name + "' already starts workflow '"
                                        + workflowName + "'."));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return problems;
    }

    private boolean startsWorkflow(EventSubscriptionEntity subscription, long definitionId) {
        if (subscription.routing == null) {
            return false;
        }
        try {
            for (JsonNode rule : mapper.readTree(subscription.routing)) {
                if ("create-workflow".equals(rule.path("type").asText())
                        && rule.path("workflowDefinitionId").asLong(-1) == definitionId) {
                    return true;
                }
            }
        } catch (JsonProcessingException e) {
            return false;
        }
        return false;
    }

Use RoutingRule.TYPE_CREATE_WORKFLOW instead of the literal if importable. Then make validateAll call validateItem(compositionId, type, packItem(item), context) and validateContent call validateItem(compositionId, type, CompositionItems.toPackItem(type, name, content, mapper), context(compositionId)). In CompositionPublisher.publish, replace validationService.validate(ConfigItemType.fromName(item.itemType), validator.packItem(item), context) with validator.validateItem(compositionId, ConfigItemType.fromName(item.itemType), validator.packItem(item), context) (remove the now-unused validationService field from the publisher if nothing else uses it).

  • [ ] Step 4: Run tests — focused (Step 2) then the full backend suite. Expected: pass.

    /**
     * Enables or disables the published subscription of a subscription item. Enabling sets
     * {@code processEventsFrom} to now, so events before this moment are not processed.
     *
     * @param compositionId the composition id
     * @param itemId the item id
     * @param enabled the new state
     * @return the item
     * @throws IllegalStateException when the item is not a published subscription
     */
    @Transactional
    public CompositionItemEntity setEnabled(long compositionId, long itemId, boolean enabled) {
        CompositionItemEntity item = item(compositionId, itemId);
        if (!ConfigItemType.SUBSCRIPTION.jsonName().equals(item.itemType) || item.baseItemId == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Only a published subscription can be enabled or disabled");
        }
        EventSubscriptionEntity subscription = EventSubscriptionEntity.findById(item.baseItemId);
        if (subscription == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("The published subscription no longer exists");
        }
        subscription.enabled = enabled;
        if (enabled) {
            subscription.processEventsFrom = Instant.now();
        }
        subscription.modifiedOn = Instant.now();
        return item;
    }

    /**
     * Publishing never changes whether a subscription runs: a new one is created disabled, and an existing one
     * keeps its enabled state and processEventsFrom (the pack import would otherwise reset them).
     */
    private static void applyPublishedState(ObjectNode packItem) {
        packItem.remove("enabled");
        packItem.remove("processEventsFrom");
        EventSubscriptionEntity existing = EventSubscriptionEntity.<EventSubscriptionEntity>find("name",
                packItem.path("name").asText()).firstResult();
        if (existing == null) {
            packItem.put("enabled", false);
            return;
        }
        packItem.put("enabled", existing.enabled);
        if (existing.processEventsFrom != null) {
            packItem.put("processEventsFrom", existing.processEventsFrom.toString());
        }
    }

/**
 * Formats a subscription filter preview: counts, errors and the matched events (at most 20).
 * @param {object} r the SubscriptionPreviewResponse
 * @returns {string} the summary
 */
function formatSubscriptionPreview(r) {
    const results = r.results || [];
    const matches = results.filter(x => x.matched);
    const lines = [`${matches.length} of ${results.length} recent events match (${r.totalMatched ?? 0} in all events).`];
    if (r.errorCount) {
        lines.push(`${r.errorCount} event(s) could not be evaluated; first error: ${r.firstError}`);
    }
    for (const m of matches.slice(0, 20)) {
        const e = m.event || {};
        const actor = e.actor && e.actor.login ? ` by ${e.actor.login}` : "";
        lines.push(`- ${e.id} ${e.type} ${e.ref}${actor} at ${e.timestamp}`);
    }
    return lines.join("\n");
}
