    /**
     * Fetches a single page of issues (with changelog expansion) across multiple projects
     * that have been updated since the given timestamp. Results are ordered by
     * {@code updated ASC}. Callers must follow {@code nextPageToken} in the response
     * (until it is absent or {@code isLast} is true) to retrieve the full result set.
     *
     * <p>The JQL lower bound is the given {@code since} minus a two-minute buffer (covering
     * modest clock skew), expressed in epoch milliseconds so it is independent of the Jira
     * user's profile timezone. Project keys are quoted. Duplicates resulting from the overlap
     * are removed by source-event de-duplication downstream.</p>
     *
     * @param baseUrl       Jira Cloud base URL (e.g., https://myorg.atlassian.net)
     * @param projects      list of project keys to search
     * @param since         only return issues updated at or after (approximately) this time
     * @param credentials   email:api_token for Basic auth
     * @param nextPageToken the page token from the previous page, or {@code null} for the first page
     * @param extraFieldIds field IDs of the configured extra fields to request in addition to
     *                      {@link #SEARCH_FIELDS}
     * @return API result with one page of the search response
     */
    public ApiResult fetchIssuesPage(String baseUrl, List<String> projects, Instant since,
                                     String credentials, String nextPageToken, List<String> extraFieldIds) {
        Instant bufferedSince = since.minus(QUERY_OVERLAP);
        String jql = projectClause(projects) + " AND updated >= " + bufferedSince.toEpochMilli()
                + " ORDER BY updated ASC";
        String url = baseUrl + "/rest/api/3/search/jql";

        try {
            ObjectNode body = objectMapper.createObjectNode();
            body.put("jql", jql);
            body.put("maxResults", SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE);
            body.put("expand", "changelog");
            if (nextPageToken != null && !nextPageToken.isBlank()) {
                body.put("nextPageToken", nextPageToken);
            }
            ArrayNode fields = body.putArray("fields");
            SEARCH_FIELDS.forEach(fields::add);
            if (extraFieldIds != null) {
                extraFieldIds.stream().filter(id -> !SEARCH_FIELDS.contains(id)).forEach(fields::add);
            }

            String jsonBody = objectMapper.writeValueAsString(body);
            return doPost(url, jsonBody, credentials);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            LOG.errorf(e, "Failed to build Jira search request");
            return ApiResult.exception(e, "POST", url, null);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Builds the JQL project clause with every key quoted ({@code "} and {@code \} escaped).
     *
     * @param projects project keys
     * @return e.g. {@code project in ("A", "B")}
     */
    static String projectClause(List<String> projects) {
        return projects.stream()
                .map(key -> "\"" + key.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"") + "\"")
                .collect(Collectors.joining(", ", "project in (", ")"));
    }

    /**
     * Fetches all statuses visible to the user ({@code GET /rest/api/3/status}), used to map status IDs to
     * status categories.
     *
     * @param baseUrl     Jira Cloud base URL
     * @param credentials email:api_token for Basic auth
     * @return API result whose data is the array of statuses
     */
    public ApiResult fetchStatuses(String baseUrl, String credentials) {
        return doGet(baseUrl + "/rest/api/3/status", credentials);
    }

    /**
     * Fetches all fields ({@code GET /rest/api/3/field}), used to resolve configured extra field names to IDs.
     *
     * @param baseUrl     Jira Cloud base URL
     * @param credentials email:api_token for Basic auth
     * @return API result whose data is the array of fields
     */
    public ApiResult fetchFields(String baseUrl, String credentials) {
        return doGet(baseUrl + "/rest/api/3/field", credentials);
    }

Replace fetchIssueComments with:

    /**
     * Fetches all comments of an issue, following {@code startAt} pagination of
     * {@code /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment}. Used when the comment list embedded in search results is
     * incomplete.
     *
     * @param baseUrl     Jira Cloud base URL
     * @param issueKey    issue key (e.g., PROJ-123)
     * @param credentials email:api_token for Basic auth
     * @return API result whose data is an array of all comments (oldest first), or the failing page's result
     */
    public ApiResult fetchIssueComments(String baseUrl, String issueKey, String credentials) {
        ArrayNode comments = objectMapper.createArrayNode();
        String commentUrl = baseUrl + "/rest/api/3/issue/"
                + URLEncoder.encode(issueKey, StandardCharsets.UTF_8).replace("+", "%20") + "/comment";
        int startAt = 0;
        for (int pages = 0; pages < MAX_COMMENT_PAGES; pages++) {
            ApiResult page = doGet(commentUrl + "?orderBy=created&startAt=" + startAt
                    + "&maxResults=" + COMMENT_PAGE_SIZE, credentials);
            if (!page.success()) {
                return page;
            }
            JsonNode values = page.data().path("comments");
            int fetched = values.isArray() ? values.size() : 0;
            if (fetched > 0) {
                values.forEach(comments::add);
            }
            startAt += fetched;
            if (fetched == 0 || startAt >= page.data().path("total").asInt(0)) {
                return ApiResult.ok(comments, "GET", commentUrl, null, null);
            }
        }
        LOG.warnf("Comments of %s exceed %d pages; only the first %d are used",
                issueKey, MAX_COMMENT_PAGES, comments.size());
        return ApiResult.ok(comments, "GET", commentUrl, null, null);
    }

    /**
     * Builds the per-poll normalization context: the status-category lookup and the configured extra
     * fields resolved to field IDs. A failed status lookup falls back to status-name matching; a failed
     * field lookup keeps the names without IDs (changelog events still work); names unknown to Jira are
     * ignored.
     *
     * @param baseUrl         Jira base URL without trailing slash
     * @param credentials     email:api_token credentials
     * @param extraFieldNames configured {@code extraFields}
     * @return the context
     */
    JiraNormalizationContext buildContext(String baseUrl, String credentials, List<String> extraFieldNames) {
        JiraStatusCategories categories;
        ApiResult statuses = apiClient.fetchStatuses(baseUrl, credentials);
        if (statuses != null && statuses.success()) {
            categories = JiraStatusCategories.fromStatuses(statuses.data());
        } else {
            LOG.warnf("Jira status-category lookup failed for %s (%s); falling back to status-name matching",
                    baseUrl, statuses != null ? statuses.errorMessage() : "no response");
            categories = JiraStatusCategories.empty();
        }

        Map<String, String> extraFields = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        if (extraFieldNames != null && !extraFieldNames.isEmpty()) {
            ApiResult fields = apiClient.fetchFields(baseUrl, credentials);
            if (fields != null && fields.success()) {
                JiraFieldCatalog catalog = JiraFieldCatalog.fromFields(fields.data());
                for (String name : extraFieldNames) {
                    String id = catalog.idFor(name);
                    if (id != null) {
                        extraFields.put(name, id);
                    } else {
                        LOG.warnf("Jira field '%s' in extraFields is unknown on %s; ignored", name, baseUrl);
                    }
                }
            } else {
                LOG.warnf("Jira field lookup failed for %s (%s); extra field values are taken from the "
                        + "changelog only", baseUrl, fields != null ? fields.errorMessage() : "no response");
                extraFieldNames.forEach(name -> extraFields.put(name, null));
            }
        }
        return new JiraNormalizationContext(categories, extraFields);
    }

    /**
     * Strips surrounding whitespace and trailing slashes from a base URL.
     *
     * @param url the URL, may be null
     * @return the normalized URL, or null
     */
    static String stripTrailingSlash(String url) {
        if (url == null) {
            return null;
        }
        String trimmed = url.trim();
        while (trimmed.endsWith("/")) {
            trimmed = trimmed.substring(0, trimmed.length() - 1);
        }
        return trimmed;
    }

     * Returns the issue with its complete comment list, fetching all comments when the embedded list is

    JsonNode withAllComments(String baseUrl, JsonNode issue, String credentials) {

                    key, all.statusCode());
            return issue;
        }
        if (all == null || !all.success()) {
            return null;
        }
        ObjectNode copy = ((ObjectNode) issue).deepCopy();
        ObjectNode newComment = ((ObjectNode) copy.get("fields")).putObject("comment");
        newComment.put("startAt", 0);

    private static void validateExtraFields(JsonNode extraFields, List<ConfigProblem> problems) {
        if (extraFields.isMissingNode() || extraFields.isNull()) {

package io.apitomy.axiom.app.validation;

/**
 * Normalizes event-source base URLs before they are stored.
 */
public final class BaseUrls {

    private BaseUrls() {
    }

    /**
     * Trims whitespace and strips trailing slashes, so URLs can be joined with absolute API paths.
     *
     * @param url the URL as entered, may be null
     * @return the normalized URL, or null
     */
    public static String normalize(String url) {
        if (url == null) {
            return null;
        }
        String trimmed = url.trim();
        while (trimmed.endsWith("/")) {
            trimmed = trimmed.substring(0, trimmed.length() - 1);
        }
        return trimmed;
    }
}

docs.title: Task 10: tools/jira-groundtruth.py
docs.text:
A cleaned-up version of the spike script (/tmp/axiom-test/groundtruth.py). It reads raw Jira activity for a project (or one issue), derives the sourceEventIds Axiom should have stored using the same rules as the normalizer, compares them with the events stored for an event source, runs the spike's field-quality checks, and reports schema-validation results from StreamEvent.validationErrors.

Files: - Create: tools/jira-groundtruth.py

Interfaces: - Consumes: Jira REST v3 (/search/jql, /issue/{key}/changelog, /issue/{key}/comment); Axiom GET {axiom}/api/v1/stream/events?filterEventSourceId=…&limit=500&page=N returning {items: StreamEvent[]} with optional validationErrors. - Produces: CLI python3 tools/jira-groundtruth.py AXIOM_URL --jira-url URL --project KEY --source ID --since ISO [--issue KEY] [--extra-field NAME ...]; exit code 0 when nothing is missing and no event failed validation, 1 otherwise. Credentials: JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_API_TOKEN.

  • [ ] Step 1: Write the script with its doctests

tools/jira-groundtruth.py:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare raw Jira activity with the events Axiom ingested for a Jira event source.

Usage:
    JIRA_EMAIL=me@example.com JIRA_API_TOKEN=... \\
        python3 tools/jira-groundtruth.py http://localhost:9590 \\
        --jira-url https://myorg.atlassian.net --project PROJ --source jira-test \\
        --since 2026-10-21T14:00:00Z [--issue PROJ-1] [--extra-field "Story Points"]

--since must be the event source's baseline (first-poll) time: Axiom does not ingest earlier activity.
Exit code 0 when no expected event is missing and no stored event failed schema validation, 1 otherwise.
"""
import argparse
import base64
import collections
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone

UPDATED_FIELDS = {'summary', 'description', 'priority', 'resolution', 'duedate', 'fix version', 'component'}
DONE_NAMES = {'done', 'closed', 'resolved'}
ISO_SUFFIX = 'Z'


def parse_ts(value):
    """Parse a Jira or ISO timestamp into an aware datetime.

    >>> parse_ts('2026-10-21T14:53:07.835+0000').isoformat()
    '2026-10-21T14:53:07.835000+00:00'
    >>> parse_ts('2026-10-21T14:53:07Z').isoformat()
    '2026-10-21T14:53:07+00:00'
    """
    if not value:
        return None
    if value.endswith('Z'):
        value = value[:-1] + '+0000'
    for fmt in ('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z', '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z'):
        try:
            return datetime.strptime(value, fmt)
        except ValueError:
            pass
    raise ValueError(f'Unparseable timestamp: {value}')


def epoch_millis(value):
    """Epoch milliseconds of a Jira timestamp.

    >>> epoch_millis('2026-10-21T14:53:56.781+0000')
    1792594436781
    """
    dt = parse_ts(value)
    return int(dt.timestamp() * 1000)


def item_event_count(item, extra_fields):
    """Number of events the normalizer emits for one changelog item.

    >>> item_event_count({'field': 'labels', 'fromString': 'a', 'toString': 'a b c'}, set())
    2
    >>> item_event_count({'field': 'Comment', 'fromString': 'gone', 'toString': None}, set())
    1
    >>> item_event_count({'field': 'Story Points', 'toString': '5'}, {'story points'})
    1
    >>> item_event_count({'field': 'Intelligence Requested', 'toString': 'x'}, set())
    0
    """
    field = (item.get('field') or '').lower()
    if field in ('status', 'assignee') or field in UPDATED_FIELDS or field in extra_fields:
        return 1
    if field == 'labels':
        before = set((item.get('fromString') or '').split())
        after = set((item.get('toString') or '').split())
        return len(after - before) + len(before - after)
    if field == 'comment':
        return 1 if item.get('fromString') is not None and item.get('toString') is None else 0
    return 0


def expected_history_ids(key, history, extra_fields):
    """sourceEventIds expected for one changelog history entry.

    >>> h = {'id': '9', 'items': [{'field': 'resolution', 'toString': 'Done'}, {'field': 'status'}]}
    >>> expected_history_ids('P-1', h, set())
    ['P-1-9-0', 'P-1-9-1']
    >>> expected_history_ids('P-1', {'id': '8', 'items': [{'field': 'summary'}]}, set())
    ['P-1-8']
    >>> expected_history_ids('P-1', {'id': '7', 'items': [{'field': 'Rank'}]}, set())
    []
    """
    count = sum(item_event_count(item, extra_fields) for item in history.get('items', []))
    if count == 1:
        return [f'{key}-{history["id"]}']
    return [f'{key}-{history["id"]}-{i}' for i in range(count)]


class Jira:
    """Minimal Jira Cloud REST v3 client with retries."""

    def __init__(self, base_url, email, token):
        self.base = base_url.rstrip('/') + '/rest/api/3'
        self.auth = 'Basic ' + base64.b64encode(f'{email}:{token}'.encode()).decode()

    def request(self, path, body=None):
        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
        req = urllib.request.Request(self.base + path, data=data, headers={
            'Authorization': self.auth, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Accept': 'application/json'})
        for attempt in range(5):
            try:
                with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
                    return json.load(resp)
            except (ConnectionResetError, TimeoutError, urllib.error.URLError) as e:
                if isinstance(e, urllib.error.HTTPError) and e.code not in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504):
                    raise
                time.sleep(2 + attempt * 3)
        raise RuntimeError(f'Jira request failed repeatedly: {path}')

    def issues(self, project, since, issue_key=None):
        jql = (f'key = "{issue_key}"' if issue_key else f'project = "{project}"')
        jql += f' AND updated >= {int(since.timestamp() * 1000)} ORDER BY updated ASC'
        out, token = [], None
        while True:
            body = {'jql': jql, 'maxResults': 100, 'fields': ['created', 'status', 'project', 'resolutiondate']}
            if token:
                body['nextPageToken'] = token
            page = self.request('/search/jql', body)
            out += page.get('issues', [])
            token = page.get('nextPageToken')
            if page.get('isLast', True) or not token:
                return out

    def paged(self, path, key):
        values, start = [], 0
        while True:
            sep = '&' if '?' in path else '?'
            page = self.request(f'{path}{sep}startAt={start}&maxResults=100')
            batch = page.get(key, [])
            values += batch
            start += len(batch)
            if not batch or start >= page.get('total', 0):
                return values


def axiom_events(axiom_url, source):
    events, page = [], 1
    while True:
        query = urllib.parse.urlencode({'filterEventSourceId': source, 'limit': 500, 'page': page})
        url = f'{axiom_url.rstrip("/")}/api/v1/stream/events?{query}'
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as resp:
            items = json.load(resp).get('items', [])
        events += items
        if len(items) < 500:
            return events
        page += 1


def is_iso(value):
    return value is None or (isinstance(value, str) and value.endswith(ISO_SUFFIX) and 'T' in value)


def quality(events):
    """Field-quality checks from the ingestion spike; every counter except 'events'/'type:*' should be 0."""
    q = collections.Counter()
    for e in events:
        payload = e.get('payload') or {}
        issue = payload.get('issue') or {}
        source_data = e.get('sourceData') or {}
        q['events'] += 1
        q[f'type:{e["type"]}'] += 1
        if 'project' not in source_data:
            q['missing_sourceData.project'] += 1
        if 'status' not in source_data:
            q['missing_sourceData.status'] += 1
        if issue.get('state') == 'closed' and not issue.get('closedAt'):
            q['closed_state_without_closedAt'] += 1
        if e['type'] == 'issue.closed' and issue.get('state') != 'closed':
            q['closed_event_but_snapshot_open'] += 1
        if e['type'] == 'issue.reopened' and issue.get('state') != 'open':
            q['reopened_event_but_snapshot_closed'] += 1
        if e['type'] in ('issue.assigned', 'issue.unassigned') and not (payload.get('assignee') or {}).get('login'):
            q['assign_event_assignee_no_login'] += 1
        if e.get('actor') is None:
            q['null_actor'] += 1
        for field in ('createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'closedAt'):
            if not is_iso(issue.get(field)):
                q[f'non_iso_issue.{field}'] += 1
            if not is_iso((payload.get('comment') or {}).get(field)):
                q[f'non_iso_comment.{field}'] += 1
        if not is_iso(e.get('timestamp')):
            q['non_iso_timestamp'] += 1
        if issue and not issue.get('title'):
            q['missing_title'] += 1
    return q


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument('axiom_url', help='Axiom base URL, e.g. http://localhost:9590')
    parser.add_argument('--jira-url', required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--project', required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--source', required=True, help='Axiom event source id')
    parser.add_argument('--since', required=True, help='baseline of the event source, ISO-8601')
    parser.add_argument('--issue', help='limit the comparison to one issue key')
    parser.add_argument('--extra-field', action='append', default=[], help='configured extraFields name')
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    email, token = os.environ.get('JIRA_EMAIL'), os.environ.get('JIRA_API_TOKEN')
    if not email or not token:
        parser.error('JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN must be set')
    since = parse_ts(args.since).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    extra = {name.lower() for name in args.extra_field}
    jira = Jira(args.jira_url, email, token)

    events = axiom_events(args.axiom_url, args.source)
    if args.issue:
        events = [e for e in events if e.get('ref', '').endswith('/browse/' + args.issue)]
    stored = {e['sourceEventId'] for e in events}

    expected, ignored_fields = set(), collections.Counter()
    for issue in jira.issues(args.project, since, args.issue):
        key = issue['key']
        if parse_ts(issue['fields']['created']) > since:
            expected.add(f'{key}-created')
        for history in jira.paged(f'/issue/{key}/changelog', 'values'):
            if parse_ts(history['created']) <= since:
                continue
            expected.update(expected_history_ids(key, history, extra))
            for item in history.get('items', []):
                if item_event_count(item, extra) == 0 and (item.get('field') or '').lower() != 'comment':
                    ignored_fields[item.get('field')] += 1
        for comment in jira.paged(f'/issue/{key}/comment?orderBy=created', 'comments'):
            created, updated = parse_ts(comment['created']), parse_ts(comment['updated'])
            if created > since:
                expected.add(f'{key}-comment-{comment["id"]}')
            if updated > created and updated > since:
                expected.add(f'{key}-comment-{comment["id"]}-updated-{epoch_millis(comment["updated"])}')

    missing = sorted(expected - stored)
    unexpected = sorted(stored - expected)
    invalid = [e for e in events if e.get('validationErrors')]
    messages = collections.Counter(m for e in invalid for m in e['validationErrors'])

    print(f'===== {args.project}{" / " + args.issue if args.issue else ""} (source {args.source})')
    print(f'expected events: {len(expected)}, stored events: {len(stored)}')
    print(f'missing ({len(missing)}):', missing[:50])
    print(f'unexpected ({len(unexpected)}):', unexpected[:50])
    print('ignored changelog fields:', ignored_fields.most_common(25))
    print('quality:', json.dumps(dict(sorted(quality(events).items())), indent=1))
    print(f'schema validation: {len(events) - len(invalid)} valid, {len(invalid)} invalid')
    for message, count in messages.most_common(20):
        print(f'  {count:5d}  {message}')
    return 0 if not missing and not invalid else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

docs.title: Task 11: Developer documentation
docs.text:
Plan 1 documents the schema registry, file layout and runtime validation; this task documents the Jira side (issue-state rebuild and its limits, sourceEventId formats, extraFields, status-category rules, Jira sourceData, configuration rules, upgrade notes). The user-guide items of the spec's Documentation section belong to Plan 3 (UI).

Files: - Modify: docs/developer-guide/event-sourcing-design.md (the "Jira event source" bullet list near line 41 and the whole ## Jira section at the end, from line 483)

Interfaces: none.

  • [ ] Step 1: Update the Jira event-source bullets

Replace the "Jira event source:" bullet list with:

**Jira event source:**
- Uses JQL search with changelog expansion (`expand=changelog`)
- Single query covers all configured projects via a `project in ("A", "B")` clause (keys are quoted)
- Field-level change detection from changelog entries; every event carries the issue state as of that event
- ADF-to-plain-text conversion for description and comment bodies
- Configuration: `baseUrl` (e.g., `https://myorg.atlassian.net`; must start with `http://` or `https://`,
  a trailing `/` is removed when saved), `secretName`, `projects` (list of project keys matching
  `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$`), optional `extraFields` (list of Jira field names), `pollInterval`
  • [ ] Step 2: Replace the ## Jira section

Replace everything from ## Jira to the end of the file with:

## Jira

**Event detection:** JQL search with `expand=changelog`, ordered by `updated`. The search requests the fields
used for snapshots (`summary`, `description`, `status`, `assignee`, `reporter`, `labels`, `priority`,
`resolution`, `resolutiondate`, `duedate`, `fixVersions`, `components`, `issuetype`, `project`, `comment`,
`created`, `updated`, `parent`) plus the IDs of the configured `extraFields`. Truncated changelogs are
completed with `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/changelog`; incomplete comment lists (`total` greater than the
number returned) with `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment`. A 404/403 on either falls back to the embedded
data; 5xx, 429 and network errors abort the poll window without advancing the checkpoint.

**Per-poll lookups:** once per event source and poll, `GET /rest/api/3/status` builds a status ID →
category key map, and (only when `extraFields` is configured) `GET /rest/api/3/field` resolves field names to
IDs, ignoring case. Unknown `extraFields` names are ignored with a warning. If the status lookup fails, a
warning is logged and status names `done`, `closed` and `resolved` are treated as done.

**Issue state as of each event:** `JiraIssueHistory` sorts the changelog newest first, starts from the current
issue, and for each entry records the state after that entry and then undoes the entry's items (`to` →
`from`). What remains is the state at creation, used by `issue.created`. Comment events use the state in
effect at the comment's timestamp. Tracked: status (name, ID, category → `state`/`stateDetail`), summary,
description, assignee, labels, resolution and `closedAt`, priority, due date, fix versions, components and
every configured extra field. `updatedAt` of a snapshot is the timestamp of the entry that produced it
(`created` for the creation state). `closedAt` is the time of the most recent resolution change to a
non-null value at or before the snapshot, and null while the resolution is empty.

Limits:
- Fields without changelog history keep their current values in every snapshot.
- A rebuilt description is the changelog's plain/wiki text; the current one is converted from ADF.
- Comment bodies are always the current text (Jira keeps no comment history).
- Extra-field values from the changelog are Jira's display strings (`toString`); current values are rendered
  from the field JSON (`value`, `name`, `displayName` or `key` of objects, arrays joined with `, `, integral
  numbers without a fraction).

**Open/closed:** `state` is `closed` exactly when the status category key is `done`. A status change into
the `done` category emits `issue.closed`, out of it `issue.reopened`, anything else `issue.updated`.

**Changelog classification:**

| Changelog `field` (case-insensitive) | Event Type |
|-------|------------|
| `status` into the done category | `issue.closed` |
| `status` out of the done category | `issue.reopened` |
| other `status` changes | `issue.updated` with `change` |
| `summary`, `description`, `priority`, `resolution`, `duedate`, `Fix Version`, `Component` | `issue.updated` with `change` |
| a name listed in `configuration.extraFields` | `issue.updated` with `change` |
| `assignee` set | `issue.assigned` (`assignee.login` = account ID from `to`) |
| `assignee` cleared | `issue.unassigned` (`assignee.login` = account ID from `from`) |
| `labels` added | `issue.labeled` (one per label) |
| `labels` removed | `issue.unlabeled` (one per label) |
| `Comment` with `fromString` and no `toString` | `issue.comment.deleted` (comment `id` and `author` null, `body` = deleted text; actor = history author) |

**`sourceEventId` formats:**

| Trigger | `sourceEventId` |
|---|---|
| Issue created | `{KEY}-created` |
| Changelog entry producing one event | `{KEY}-{historyId}` |
| Changelog entry producing several events | `{KEY}-{historyId}-{i}` (item order) |
| Comment created | `{KEY}-comment-{commentId}` |
| Comment edited | `{KEY}-comment-{commentId}-updated-{updatedEpochMillis}` (one per edit) |

**Timestamps:** every timestamp in the payload (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `closedAt`, comment timestamps) and
the event `timestamp` are ISO-8601 UTC ending in `Z`.

**`sourceData`** (a selected set, not validated by the event schemas; values follow the snapshot of the
event where history exists):

```json
{
  "jiraId": "7358053",
  "project": {"key": "APICURIO", "name": "Apicurio"},
  "issueType": {"name": "Task"},
  "status": {"name": "Closed", "categoryKey": "done"},
  "priority": {"name": "Major"},
  "resolution": {"name": "Done"},
  "dueDate": "2026-10-30",
  "components": [{"name": "core"}],
  "fixVersions": [{"name": "1.2.0"}],
  "extraFields": {"Story Points": "5"}
}
```

`extraFields` is present only when configured; a configured field with no value is `null`.

**`ref` construction:** `{baseUrl}/browse/{issueKey}`

**Upgrade notes:**
- Existing events and IDs are kept.
- A comment edit that already has an old-format `{KEY}-comment-{id}-updated` event gets one more event under
  the new format after the upgrade (accepted one-time effect).
- Changelog entries that now produce more events (for example a status change plus a resolution change)
  use `-{i}` suffixes; such an entry re-read in the first poll window after the upgrade is stored once more
  under the new IDs (accepted one-time effect, limited to the two-minute query overlap).

**Verification tool:** `tools/jira-groundtruth.py` compares raw Jira activity with the stored events and
reports field-quality problems and schema-validation results (see the script's `--help`).

Run: awk 'length > 110 && !/^\|/ && !/^```/ {print FILENAME": "FNR": "length}' docs/developer-guide/event-sourcing-design.md Expected: no output for the lines you added (tables and code are exempt; pre-existing long lines elsewhere may be left alone).

  • [ ] Step 4: Commit

git commit -m "docs: document Jira issue-state rebuild, event IDs, extraFields and sourceData"

docs.title: Design: Trace ID as the Correlation ID (#427)
docs.text: Part of epic #431 (traceability). Builds on #414 (UUID event IDs) and #415 (trace lifecycle).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Given a trace ID, a user can find every activity row, AI usage row, task and run that belongs to that unit of work, including records that agents create through Axiom APIs.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
• Every unit of work (event processing, task, workflow run, scheduled job run, report) is identified by its trace ID. No new correlation concept is introduced.
  • Every record produced by that work stores the trace ID in a trace_id column.
  • Trace data has a bounded lifetime. When TraceCleanup deletes a trace, it clears trace_id on all records that reference it (it already does this for tasks, scheduled job runs and reports).

docs.title: Database and API
docs.text:
• Migration V66: add nullable trace_id UUID plus an index to activity_log and ai_usage. No foreign key, consistent with the other trace_id columns, since cleanup clears references explicitly.
  • openapi.json:
  • Add traceId (string, format: uuid) to the ActivityLogEntry and AiUsage beans.
  • Add a filterTraceId query parameter to GET /activity and GET /usage/ai. A malformed UUID returns 400, matching filterEventId.
  • Document the optional X-Axiom-Trace-Id and X-Axiom-Parent-Node-Id request headers on the agent-callable write endpoints listed below.

docs.title: Populating trace IDs
docs.text:
• logActivity helpers in EventStreamOrchestrator, TaskExecutionService, ScriptExecutionService, WorkflowExecutionService, ReportExecutionService and ScheduledJobExecutionService gain a traceId parameter. Each call site passes the trace already in scope (task.traceId, run.traceId, report.traceId, or traceCtx.traceId()).
  • handleIgnore and handleEscalation in EventStreamOrchestrator receive the trace context so their activity rows carry the trace ID.
  • AI usage written by TaskExecutionService, ReportExecutionService and ScheduledJobExecutionService stores the trace ID.
  • Report and scheduled-job activity rows set existing ID columns (e.g. projectId) where they apply. Run and report ID columns are out of scope (#424, #425).

docs.title: Agent to Axiom API propagation
docs.text:
• templates/axiom-mcp-server/sdk-server.js (axiomApi) sends X-Axiom-Trace-Id and X-Axiom-Parent-Node-Id, read from AXIOM_TRACE_ID and AXIOM_PARENT_NODE_ID, on every request when those variables are set.
  • A new JAX-RS ContainerRequestFilter reads the headers into a @RequestScoped CallerTraceContext bean. The context is used only if the trace ID is a valid UUID, the trace exists, its status is in-progress, and the parent node (if given) belongs to that trace. Otherwise the headers are ignored, and a debug log is written.
  • POST /projects/{id}/tasks: when a caller trace is present, the new task joins it. The task's traceId is set to the caller's trace and its task node is added under the caller's parent node, instead of a new user-action trace being created. TaskTraceFinalizer (#415) already keeps the trace open while that node is in progress.
  • The other agent write endpoints (POST /projects/{id}/thread, PUT /projects/{id}, PUT /projects/{id}/body, POST /projects/{id}/close, POST /projects/{id}/reopen, POST /projects/{id}/tasks/{taskId}/respond, POST /projects, POST /events, PUT /reports/{id}/labels) store the caller's trace ID on any activity row they write. They do not add trace nodes.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• AI editor and assistant sessions (ActionTypeAiService, ReportAiService, ScriptAiService, ToolAiService, AssistantSessionManager) have no trace today. Their AI usage rows stay unlinked.
  • MDC log correlation (#428), run and report ID columns (#424, #425), lineage view (#430).

docs.title: Accepted risk
docs.text: An agent can keep its trace open by creating tasks that join it. This is accepted because agent-created tasks are deliberate work that belongs to the trace.

docs.title: UI
docs.text: • Activity log and AI usage pages show the trace ID as a link to /logs/traces/:traceId and offer a trace ID filter.

docs.title: Testing (JUnit 5)
docs.text:
• Activity and AI usage filtered by trace ID return the expected rows. A malformed trace ID returns 400.
  • Activity and AI usage written by the task, report and scheduled job paths carry the trace ID.
  • A task created with valid headers joins the caller's trace under the parent node, and the trace stays open until that task finishes.
  • Headers with an unknown, finished or malformed trace are ignored, and a new user-action trace is created.
  • TraceCleanup clears trace_id on activity_log and ai_usage.
  • UI type-check passes.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• New docs/developer-guide/correlation.md describing the model, the headers and how to find all records for a unit of work.
  • Update docs/developer-guide/tracing.md to reference it.

docs.title: Workflow-First Streamlining Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-05 Status: Approved (pending spec review)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Refocus Apitomy Axiom on workflows. The two core use cases are Event → Create Workflow and Event → Dispatch to Workflow, plus a Schedule → Create Workflow trigger. Workflow runs become the primary user-facing object. Projects are replaced by a thin Subject concept. All parallel execution subsystems (reports, scheduled jobs, AI Manager, direct action invocation) are removed.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Reports. These may return later as a Report SDK that a workflow invokes to publish a report to a Subject (listed on the Subject page). Not part of this work.
  • Workflow outputs and sub-workflows.
  • Data migration or backward compatibility of any kind.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• Report definitions and reports: ReportDefinitionEntity, ReportDefinitionVersionEntity, ReportEntity, ReportScheduler, ReportQueueConsumer, ReportExecutionService, ReportAiService, ReportsResourceImpl, ReportDefinitionValidator, related UI pages, tests, and docs.
  • Scheduled jobs: ScheduledJobEntity, ScheduledJobVersionEntity, ScheduledJobRunEntity, ScheduledJobScheduler, ScheduledJobQueueConsumer, ScheduledJobExecutionService, ScheduledJobsResourceImpl, ScheduledJobValidator, related UI pages, tests, and docs.
  • AI Manager: the entire manager module, the manager routing type, confidence thresholds, and decision handling.
  • invoke-action routing type.
  • Manual action invocation from a project/subject page.
  • All Action Type flags (e.g. user-triggerable, manager-triggerable, emits-event).
  • Project lifecycle: ProjectLifecycle, ProjectStatus, and the status column.

docs.title: Action Types
docs.text: Action Types are invoked only from workflow action nodes. There is no other entry point (no events, no UI trigger, no API trigger). Execution fields (executionMode, templates, allowedTools, model, engine, maxSteps, maxBudgetUsd, timeoutSeconds, environment) are retained.

docs.title: Subject (replaces Project)
docs.text:
ProjectEntity is renamed to SubjectEntity. Fields:

  • id, name/title, body, type, refSource, ref, repository, metadata, diskUsageBytes, timestamps.
  • Owns the workspace directory and the thread (ThreadEntryEntity).
  • Has no lifecycle of its own. Subject status is derived: active if any of its runs is running or waiting, otherwise inactive.
  • Workspace cleanup (replacing ClosedProjectCleanup) runs for subjects with no active runs for N days (configurable).

All projectId references (tasks, runs, thread entries, events, AI usage, workflow event subscriptions) become subjectId.

docs.title: Workflow Runs
docs.text:
Workflow runs are the primary UI object. WorkflowRunEntity fields:

  • Existing: id, definitionId, instanceState, status, currentNodeId, failureReason, traceId, triggerEventId, triggerLedgerId, startedOn, completedOn.
  • subjectId — required (non-null) for every run.
  • New: definitionVersion, title, labels (JSON metadata), inputs (JSON).
  • No outputs. Per-node results remain available via each action node's task output. This matches Apitomy Flow (inputs on Start node, no outputs on End node).

title defaults to <definition name> — <subject title> when not provided.

docs.title: Concurrency Rule
docs.text:
At most one active run per (subject, workflow definition). Replaces the old one-active-run-per-project rule. This permits:

  • Sequential runs on the same subject (re-open, retry), sharing workspace and history.
  • Concurrent runs of different definitions on the same subject.

A trigger that would violate the rule is skipped (not queued), and the skip is recorded.

docs.title: Schedule Trigger (new)
docs.text:
A workflow definition may have zero or more schedule triggers:

  • cron expression.
  • subjectName — a fixed subject, required. Created on first firing if it does not exist; reused on every subsequent firing so run history accumulates on that subject.
  • Optional static inputs passed to the run.
  • enabled flag, nextRunAt.

When the trigger fires and the subject already has an active run of the same definition, the firing is skipped and logged.

docs.title: Schema Reset
docs.text:
• Delete all existing Flyway migrations.
  • Create a single baseline V1__baseline.sql representing the new model.
  • No data migration. All existing data is discarded.

docs.title: REST API (contract-first)
docs.text:
All changes start in common/api/src/main/resources/openapi.json, followed by regenerating the JAX-RS interfaces and beans.

  • Remove report, scheduled-job, and manager endpoints and schemas.
  • Remove Action Type flag properties and any "invoke action" endpoints.
  • Rename /projects → /subjects and Project* schemas → Subject*. No aliases.
  • Remove subject status/lifecycle transition endpoints; expose derived active boolean instead.
  • Add run fields subjectId (required), definitionVersion, title, labels, inputs; add filtering of runs by status, definition, subject, and label.
  • Add schedule trigger CRUD under workflow definitions (e.g. /workflows/{definitionId}/triggers/schedules).
  • Remove manager and invoke-action from the routing rule schema.

docs.title: 3. Event Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Source connections (GitHub, Jira) poll and produce stream events (unchanged).
  2. Event subscriptions apply filters, then one of two routing types:
  3. create-workflow: find or create the Subject from the event ref; start a run of the configured definition with subjectId, ref, and event in context. If the subject already has an active run of that definition, skip and record the skip in the routing outcome.
  4. workflow-dispatch: deliver the event to every waiting run on the correlated subject that has a receive-event node subscribed to a matching event type (broadcast — current behavior). If the event does not correlate to a subject, deliver to all waiting runs with a matching event type (current behavior).
  5. Routing outcomes and the processing ledger are retained for auditing.

Events matching no subscription are recorded in the ledger only.

docs.title: Inbox
docs.text: The Inbox is retained only for human-task nodes awaiting a person. Manager escalations and low-confidence decisions no longer exist.

docs.title: 4. UI
docs.text:
• Navigation: Runs (default landing page), Subjects, Workflows, Action Types, Event Sources / Subscriptions, Inbox.
  • Removed pages: Reports, Scheduled Jobs, Manager-related views, run-action-from-project.
  • Runs list: filter by status, definition, subject, labels.
  • Run detail: graph with current node, inputs, tasks (with per-task outputs), triggering event.
  • Subject page: header (ref, metadata, derived active state), timeline of all runs (active and past), thread, workspace. (Future: list of published reports.)
  • Workflow definition editor: new Triggers tab for schedule triggers (cron, fixed subject name, inputs, enabled). Event triggers remain configured via subscriptions.
  • Action Type editor: flags removed.

docs.title: 5. Testing
docs.text:
• Delete tests for removed subsystems (reports, scheduled jobs, manager, invoke-action, project lifecycle).
  • New JUnit 5 tests:
  • Schedule trigger fires → subject created on first firing, reused thereafter.
  • Schedule trigger skipped when the subject has an active run of the same definition.
  • create-workflow: sequential runs on the same subject after completion (scenario B).
  • create-workflow: concurrent runs of different definitions on one subject (scenario C).
  • create-workflow: second run of the same definition on an active subject is skipped and recorded.
  • workflow-dispatch: broadcast to multiple waiting runs on the same subject.
  • Run creation fails without a subjectId.
  • Derived subject active state.
  • Update UI/E2E tests for the Project → Subject rename and removed pages.

docs.title: 6. Documentation
docs.text:
• Rewrite docs/user-guide/concepts.md around the workflow-first model (Subjects, Workflows, Runs, Action Types, Events, Schedule Triggers, Inbox).
  • Update docs/user-guide/workflows.md with schedule triggers and the concurrency rule.
  • Remove reports, scheduled jobs, and Manager user-guide content.
  • Update developer-guide references to projects and the Manager.

docs.title: Configuration Assistant Correctness Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-06 Status: Approved (pending spec review)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Make the Axiom Configuration Assistant produce syntactically and semantically correct Tools, Action Types, Toolsets, Session Templates, Workflows, Event Sources and Subscriptions — and let items created in one session reference each other — by making the server's real validators the single source of truth for the API, the assistant's feedback, a new pre-write validation tool, and Apply.

docs.title: Problems Being Solved
docs.text:
1. The system prompt documents the wrong workflow format (uppercase node types, sourceNodeId/targetNodeId edges, missing content.id/name, wrong human-task config, no Start inputs, no graph rules).
  2. AssistantItemValidator enforces that same wrong format ("START"/"END") and never uses the flow engine's model or WorkflowValidator; live feedback pushes the agent toward the wrong format.
  3. Apply writes entities directly: workflows become published versions without WorkflowValidator or Start input checks; subscriptions skip filter and routing checks.
  4. No way for the agent to validate a draft before writing; only tools and action types have REST validate endpoints.
  5. Prompt errors: wrong action-type placeholders ({{subjectId}} is rejected), wrong event type examples (issues), wrong enabled default for subscriptions, tools named in the prompt missing from allowedTools (axiom_list_secrets, axiom_list_subjects) or nonexistent (axiom_list_agents).
  6. Same-session cross-references fail: toolsets created in the session are unknown to action-type validation; subscriptions need a numeric workflowDefinitionId that does not exist before Apply.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• AI-assisted workflow node layout (prompt keeps simple spacing guidance).
  • Validation of EventSourceFilters include/exclude rules (unused in production).
  • Changes to the general-purpose assistant.

docs.title: 1. Shared Validation Service
docs.text:
ConfigItemValidationService (app module, @ApplicationScoped) is the only place that decides whether a configuration item is valid.

API:

  • List<ConfigProblem> validate(ConfigItemType type, JsonNode item, ValidationContext context)
  • ConfigItemType: TOOL, ACTION_TYPE, TOOLSET, SESSION_TEMPLATE, WORKFLOW, EVENT_SOURCE, SUBSCRIPTION (JSON names: tool, action-type, toolset, session-template, workflow, event-source, subscription).
  • ConfigProblem(severity, path, code, message) — severity error|warning; path is a JSON path such as content.edges[2].source.
  • ValidationContext resolves names of existing tools, toolsets, action types, workflow definitions, event sources and secrets from the database plus items pending in the current assistant session. ValidationContext.databaseOnly() for REST calls; ValidationContext.forSession(sessionDir) for the assistant.

Per-type checks (reusing existing code):

Type Checks Tool Existing ToolValidator Action type Existing ActionTypeValidator; known tools/toolsets come from the context (DB + session) Toolset / session template Required fields; referenced tools/toolsets exist Workflow Requires name and content; deserialize content into the flow engine's Workflow; run WorkflowValidator; Start-input rules (extracted from WorkflowDefinitionsResourceImpl.validateStartInputs into a shared method); each action node's actionType exists in context or is a registered sdk: function; receive-event eventType is a known EventType (warning if unknown) Event source Id matches [a-z0-9-]+; sourceType is github or jira; GitHub configuration.repositories is a non-empty array of owner/repo; Jira configuration.projects is a non-empty array of keys; secretName exists (warning) Subscription filterExpression parses as EL; each routing rule type is create-workflow or workflow-dispatch; create-workflow requires exactly one of workflowDefinitionId (must exist) or workflowDefinitionName (must exist in context); filter comparing event.type to a string that is not a known EventType → warning

Reuse by REST: subscription create/update, workflow definition publish, tool and action-type validate/ create endpoints call the service (databaseOnly() context) instead of their inline checks. Error responses keep their current status codes and shapes.

AssistantItemValidator becomes a thin adapter: walks the session directories, detects types, and delegates to the service with forSession. Its hand-written workflow check is deleted.

docs.title: 2. Pre-Write Validation Tool and Live Feedback
docs.text:
REST (contract-first, openapi.json): POST /api/v1/assistant/sessions/{sessionId}/validate — body { type, item }; response { valid: boolean, problems: ConfigProblem[] }. Uses ValidationContext.forSession for that session; 404 for unknown session.

MCP tool in templates/axiom-assistant-mcp/server.js: axiom_validate_item(type, item) calls the endpoint above. The session ID is provided via an AXIOM_ASSISTANT_SESSION_ID env var in the per-session MCP config generated by AssistantSessionManager. Returns problems with paths plus a one-line next-step hint.

Template allowedTools: add mcp__axiom__axiom_validate_item, mcp__axiom__axiom_list_secrets, mcp__axiom__axiom_list_subjects; use the existing axiom_list_actors (remove references to the nonexistent axiom_list_agents).

Live feedback: after each file-writing tool result, re-validation uses the service. Existing de-duplication (ValidationFeedbackTracker) stays. When the set of problems becomes empty after having been non-empty, send one "all items valid" message.

docs.title: 3. Apply and Cross-References
docs.text:
• Apply builds the configuration pack as today, then imports in dependency order: tools → toolsets → action types → session templates → workflows → event sources → subscriptions.
  • Before any write, every item is validated with the session context; any error aborts Apply (no writes).
  • ImportExportService create/update paths call the same service methods as REST rather than writing entities unchecked. This also covers configuration packs imported via the UI.
  • Workflows: save draft content, then publish through the same publish method the REST endpoint uses (WorkflowValidator + Start-input rules). Failure rolls back the whole Apply transaction (verify Apply is a single transaction; make it one if not).
  • RoutingRule gains optional workflowDefinitionName (openapi + core/.../events/model/RoutingRule). On subscription create/update/import, the server resolves the name to an ID and stores only workflowDefinitionId. Unknown name → validation error. Responses continue to expose workflowDefinitionId.
  • Defaults unchanged: assistant-created event sources and subscriptions are enabled: false unless specified.

docs.title: 4. Prompt, Generated Reference, Examples
docs.text:
Prompt structure (axiom-config-assistant.json):

  1. Role and the working loop: discover (list/get tools) → draft → axiom_validate_item → fix → write → read feedback. For workflows, ensure every referenced action type exists or is in the session.
  2. Hand-written concepts: tool vs action type; how workflow, subscription and event source fit; action types run only from workflow action nodes; event sources/subscriptions are created disabled.
  3. {{reference}} placeholder, replaced at session creation by AssistantReferenceGenerator output built from code:
  4. Workflow: node types (NodeType values), per-type config fields (from the engine's NodeConfig), edge fields, WorkflowValidator rules in plain language, condition syntax (raw EL; variables context, event), Start-input rules.
  5. Action type: prompt and script template placeholders (from ActionTypeValidator's lists), field types, allowed-tool formats, valid mcp__axiom-sdk__ names (from SdkFunctionRegistry).
  6. Events: EventType values, subscription filter variables (event.id, type, source, eventSourceId, ref, timestamp, actor, payload), event-source configuration per source type.
  7. Subscriptions: routing types; workflowDefinitionName option.
  8. Examples: complete known-good JSON for each item type, plus a worked scenario "when a GitHub issue opens, run a triage workflow" (action type, workflow with a branch and a receive-event node, subscription referencing the workflow by name).

Examples are real files under app/src/main/resources/templates/assistant-reference/examples/ loaded by both the generator and tests.

docs.title: 5. Testing (JUnit 5)
docs.text:
• Every example file validates with zero errors; the scenario applies end to end (workflow published, subscription's workflowDefinitionId resolved from the name).
  • Known-bad inputs rejected with useful paths: uppercase START; sourceNodeId edges; missing content.id; {{subjectId}} in a prompt template; filter event.type == 'issues' (warning).
  • Apply: rolls back fully when a workflow fails to publish; resolves workflowDefinitionName; rejects an unknown name; same-session toolset referenced by a same-session action type is accepted.
  • REST: validate endpoint with session context (and 404 for unknown session); subscription create with workflowDefinitionName; existing subscription and workflow-publish tests still pass unchanged.
  • Reference generator output contains every NodeType and EventType value.
  • server.js exposes axiom_validate_item, and the template allows it.

docs.title: Event Source Rename Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-06 Status: Approved (pending spec review)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Replace the "Connection" naming for event sources with "EventSource" naming across the REST API, database, backend, SDK/assistant templates, UI, and docs, matching the "Event Sources" label already used in the UI navigation.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Backward compatibility: no API aliases, no data migration (the schema is a single editable baseline).
  • Renaming non-domain uses of "connection": JDBC/database connections, HTTP/OpenCode client connections, MCP connection code, and Jira's own projects configuration.
  • Behavior changes of any kind.

docs.title: Naming Map
docs.text:
Area From To REST paths /connections, /connections/{connectionId}, …/status, …/logs /event-sources, /event-sources/{eventSourceId}, …/status, …/logs OpenAPI tag (generated interface) Connections (ConnectionsResource) EventSources (EventSourcesResource) Schemas Connection, NewConnection, ConnectionStatus, ConnectionPollLog, ConnectionSearchResults, ConnectionPollLogSearchResults EventSource, NewEventSource, EventSourceStatus, EventSourcePollLog, EventSourceSearchResults, EventSourcePollLogSearchResults Operation IDs listConnections, getConnection, createConnection, updateConnection, deleteConnection, getConnectionStatus, listConnectionPollLogs listEventSources, getEventSource, createEventSource, updateEventSource, deleteEventSource, getEventSourceStatus, listEventSourcePollLogs Query params / properties filterConnectionId, connectionId filterEventSourceId, eventSourceId Tables event_source_connection, connection_poll_log (+ _SEQ) event_source, event_source_poll_log (+ _SEQ) Columns connection_id (poll log, stream event, any other) event_source_id Indexes idx_cpl_connection, idx_cpl_created, idx_stream_event_connection idx_espl_event_source, idx_espl_created, idx_stream_event_event_source Java classes EventSourceConnectionEntity, ConnectionPollLogEntity, ConnectionsResourceImpl, GitHubConnectionPoller, JiraConnectionPoller (+ tests, incl. ConnectionsResourceTest) EventSourceEntity, EventSourcePollLogEntity, EventSourcesResourceImpl, GitHubEventSourcePoller, JiraEventSourcePoller (+ tests, EventSourcesResourceTest) Event field connectionId on StreamEventEntity, event model, event JSON in workflow context; event.connectionId in EL eventSourceId; event.eventSourceId Config assistant connections/ directory, axiom_list_connections, axiom_get_connection, "Connections" prose event-sources/, axiom_list_event_sources, axiom_get_event_source, "Event Sources" Import/export connections section eventSources section UI ConnectionsPage, ConnectionDetailPage, api.ts types/functions, routes /events/connections… EventSourcesPage, EventSourceDetailPage, matching api.ts names, routes /events/sources… Docs "connection(s)" meaning event source "event source(s)"

Fields named after the event-source kind (event.source, sourceType) are unchanged.

docs.title: Approach
docs.text: Single full rename, contract-first, in this order: openapi.json → regenerate → V1__baseline.sql → core → events/* modules → app → templates/assistant → UI → docs. Delivered as a few reviewable commits on feat/workflow-first. The baseline migration is edited in place; MigrationSchemaValidationTest guards entity/schema consistency.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Existing tests renamed with their subjects.
  • New regression tests:
  • GET /api/v1/connections returns 404; GET /api/v1/event-sources returns 200.
  • A subscription filter expression using event.eventSourceId matches an event from that event source.
  • Sidebar "Event Sources" item navigates to /events/sources (Vitest).
  • ./build.sh -Pui passes.
  • Final git grep -i connection (excluding historical docs/superpowers, agentdocs) shows only the non-domain uses listed under Non-Goals.

docs.title: Explicit Action Type Inputs Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-06 Status: Approved (pending spec review)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Make declared inputs the only way data reaches an Action Type, for both script and AI agent execution modes. Remove the ambient placeholders, environment variables and system-prompt content that implicitly inject subject and event data. Every data dependency of an action becomes visible in its declaration and explicitly mapped on the workflow node that uses it.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Placeholders such as {{ref}} existed because the (now removed) AI Manager invoked action types with no declared inputs. Action types now run only from workflow action nodes, which declare inputs and outputs. Today data still reaches actions through four channels:

  1. Template placeholders: prompt {{actionType}}, {{ref}}, {{repository}}, {{subjectName}}, {{workDir}}, {{input}}; script {{subjectId}}, {{eventId}}, {{taskId}}, {{ref}}, {{repository}}, {{subjectName}}, {{apiBaseUrl}}, {{workDir}} (ActionTypeValidator recognized sets; TaskExecutionService.resolvePromptTemplate; ScriptExecutionService.substitutePlaceholders).
  2. Script environment variables AXIOM_SUBJECT_ID, AXIOM_EVENT_ID, AXIOM_REF, AXIOM_REPOSITORY, AXIOM_SUBJECT_NAME (always set, whether or not placeholders are used).
  3. The agent system prompt (TaskExecutionService.buildSystemPrompt) always includes subject name, ref, body and action type name.
  4. Declared inputs via {{inputs.X}}.

Only channel 4 is declared and visible. The Configuration Assistant, following our own examples, produced action types with "inputs": [] that silently depend on channels 1–2, which fail at runtime (not validation) when the subject is not what the action assumes, and cannot be reused on a different target.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Changes to output handling (the auto-appended output contract stays as is).
  • Changes to human-task nodes, sdk: action nodes, or tool definitions (tool templates keep their own parameter substitution).
  • Backward compatibility (pre-1.0; the single baseline schema and seed data are edited in place).

docs.title: 1. Declared inputs are the only template data channel
docs.text:
• In both promptTemplate and scriptTemplate, the only placeholder is {{inputs.X}}, where X is a declared input of the action type.
  • Removed placeholders: {{input}}, {{ref}}, {{repository}}, {{subjectName}}, {{subjectId}}, {{eventId}}, {{actionType}}, {{workDir}}, {{apiBaseUrl}}, {{taskId}}.
  • ActionTypeValidator errors on:
  • any {{…}} placeholder other than {{inputs.X}}, with a message naming the replacement:
    • data (ref, repository, subjectName, subjectId, eventId): "Declare an input <name> and map it from context.<name> on the workflow node" (eventId → map from context.event.id);
    • plumbing in scripts (workDir, apiBaseUrl, taskId): "Use $AXIOM_WORK_DIR / $AXIOM_API_URL / $AXIOM_TASK_ID";
    • actionType, input, and plumbing in prompts: "Not available; remove it" (agents already run in the workspace);
  • {{inputs.X}} where X is not a declared input.
  • Script {{inputs.X}} keeps its current quote-aware, environment-variable-based substitution (AXIOM_INPUT_X). Prompt {{inputs.X}} keeps inline rendering (InputBindingResolver).

docs.title: 2. Runtime plumbing via environment variables only
docs.text:
• Script processes keep: AXIOM_API_URL, AXIOM_TASK_ID, AXIOM_WORK_DIR, resolved secrets, the action type's environment, and the AXIOM_INPUT_* variables used by script input substitution.
  • Agent processes never had AXIOM_API_URL, AXIOM_TASK_ID or AXIOM_WORK_DIR; agents get data only through declared inputs.
  • Removed from script and agent process environments: AXIOM_SUBJECT_ID, AXIOM_EVENT_ID, AXIOM_REF, AXIOM_REPOSITORY, AXIOM_SUBJECT_NAME.
  • The working directory remains the subject workspace (runtime location, not data).

docs.title: 3. Agent prompts
docs.text:
Final prompt sent to the agent = rendered promptTemplate + generated Inputs section + existing output contract (when outputs are declared).

  • Inputs section (new, InputBindingResolver.buildInputsSection(List<ActionTypeField> inputs, Map<String, Object> values)): heading ## Inputs, then one entry per declared input that has a value, in declaration order: name, type, description (if any), and the value. Strings are rendered as-is; numbers and booleans as text; objects and arrays as pretty-printed JSON in a fenced block. All declared inputs with values are listed, including ones also referenced inline (decision B). Omitted when no declared input has a value.
  • System prompt (buildSystemPrompt): no subject data. Contains only: the action type name and description, and that the current working directory is the task's workspace.
  • The automatic output contract (InputBindingResolver.buildOutputContract) is unchanged.

docs.title: 4. Workflow context and node input mappings
docs.text:
• Every run's initial context contains subjectId, subjectName, ref, repository (from the subject; empty string when null), plus event when started by an event. All five are protected from being overridden by supplied run inputs (extend PROTECTED_INPUTS).
  • Node mapping rules for action nodes whose actionType is a declared action type (not sdk:):
  • every required declared input must have a key in the node's config.inputs → error UNMAPPED_REQUIRED_INPUT at content.nodes[i].config.inputs;
  • every key in config.inputs must be a declared input → error UNKNOWN_INPUT_MAPPING at content.nodes[i].config.inputs.<key>;
  • optional declared inputs may be left unmapped; at runtime they are absent: not listed in the Inputs section, and {{inputs.X}} for them renders as an empty string.
  • Enforced in ConfigItemValidationService (needs action type declarations, so the context must expose them — see §6) and at publish time via the same shared rule (WorkflowContentRules gains a check that takes a lookup of action type declarations), and at run time defensively: a task whose required input resolved to nothing fails with a clear message.

docs.title: 5. Updating existing content
docs.text:
• Seed data (SeedDataInitializer): rewrite seeded action types (e.g. close-subject) to declare inputs.
  • Assistant: bundled examples (templates/assistant-reference/examples/) use declared inputs mapped from context.*; AssistantReferenceGenerator documents the single placeholder, the plumbing environment variables, the context keys, the mapping rules and the generated Inputs section; the system prompt guidance adds "declare inputs for everything an action operates on" and "do not write your own output-format instructions — Axiom appends them".
  • AI helpers (ActionTypeAiService, ScriptAiService) prompt text updated to the new model.
  • UI: placeholder autocomplete (PlaceholderCompletionProvider) offers only {{inputs.X}} for the action type's declared inputs (and the plumbing env vars in script mode).
  • Docs: user guide (action types, workflows) and developer guide updated.

docs.title: 6. Validation context
docs.text: ValidationContext gains action type declarations (name → declared input names and required flags) from the database and the pending pack/session, so workflow mapping rules can be checked before Apply. Publish-time checking reads declarations from the database.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• ActionTypeValidator: each removed placeholder is rejected with its replacement hint; undeclared {{inputs.X}} rejected; declared {{inputs.X}} accepted.
  • Workflow validation: unmapped required input → UNMAPPED_REQUIRED_INPUT; unknown mapping key → UNKNOWN_INPUT_MAPPING; unmapped optional input accepted; same results at publish time.
  • Agent prompt: contains the rendered template, an Inputs section listing all valued inputs (including inline- referenced ones), and the output contract; object values rendered as JSON; unmapped optional inputs absent; system prompt contains no subject name, ref or body.
  • Script execution: AXIOM_REF, AXIOM_REPOSITORY, AXIOM_SUBJECT_NAME, AXIOM_SUBJECT_ID, AXIOM_EVENT_ID absent from the environment; AXIOM_API_URL, AXIOM_TASK_ID, AXIOM_WORK_DIR present; {{inputs.X}} substitution still shell-safe.
  • Run context contains repository and subjectName; supplied inputs cannot override any of the five protected keys.
  • Assistant examples still validate with no errors and apply end to end; seeded action types validate.

docs.title: Node.js Execution Mode for Action Types Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-07 Status: Approved (pending spec review)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Add a third Action Type execution mode, node, in which the action is a JavaScript ES module exporting run(inputs, ctx). Inputs arrive as typed JSON values and outputs are returned as an object, removing the shell quoting, heredoc and jq friction that script-mode actions suffer when moving JSON around.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Built-ins only: no npm packages.
  • Code is an ES module that exports run (not a function body, not a free-form script).

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text: npm dependencies; TypeScript; an AI-edit helper for code; sandboxing (node actions have the same trust level as scripts); converting existing script actions.

docs.title: Authoring
docs.text:
• executionMode: "node"; code stored in a new codeTemplate field. No placeholders: any {{…}} is a validation error.
  • The module exports async function run(inputs, ctx) (a synchronous run returning an object is also accepted).
  • inputs: declared inputs as JSON values (string, number, boolean, object, array). Unmapped optional inputs are absent from the object.
  • ctx:
  • ctx.workDir — the subject workspace (also the process working directory);
  • ctx.apiUrl — Axiom REST API base URL;
  • ctx.taskId — the task ID;
  • ctx.log(...args) — writes to stderr (shown in the execution log);
  • ctx.exec(cmd, args, options?) — runs a command without a shell; resolves to {stdout, stderr, exitCode}; rejects on non-zero exit unless options.allowFailure === true; options.input (string) is written to the command's stdin when given.
  • Returns a plain object containing the declared outputs.
  • Secrets and the action type's environment are in process.env (same rules as script mode).

docs.title: Execution
docs.text:
• Axiom writes the code to action.mjs in a fresh temporary directory together with the bundled runner axiom-node-runner.mjs (classpath resource), and runs node <tmp>/axiom-node-runner.mjs <tmp>/action.mjs with the subject workspace as working directory. The temporary directory is deleted afterwards.
  • Inputs are written to the runner's stdin as one JSON object.
  • The runner imports the module, checks run is a function, awaits run(inputs, ctx), checks the result is a plain object (not null, not an array), and prints JSON.stringify(result) as the final stdout line.
  • Output extraction (last JSON object on stdout), type and required-output validation are unchanged.
  • Same process handling as script mode: timeout, killing the process tree, stderr captured separately into the execution log, subject workspace as working directory (temporary directory when there is no subject), and blank required inputs counting as missing.

docs.title: Validation (ActionTypeValidator, node mode)
docs.text:
• codeTemplate required.
  • Any {{…}} → error: "Node actions receive inputs as run(inputs, ctx); placeholders are not supported."
  • Static import specifiers (import … from '…', import '…', import('…'), require('…')) must be node:* or a Node built-in module name (from a fixed list of built-ins); otherwise error naming the specifier.
  • Must export run: matches export async function run, export function run, export const run, export let run, or an export { … run … } list; otherwise error.
  • Syntax: node --check on the code (as .mjs) with a 10 s timeout; failure → error with node's message; node unavailable → warning "Syntax not checked: Node.js not found".
  • inputs.<name> property reads of undeclared names → warning.
  • promptTemplate / scriptTemplate are not required in node mode.

docs.title: API (contract-first, openapi.json)
docs.text:
• executionMode enum gains node (in ActionType and NewActionType).
  • ActionType / NewActionType gain codeTemplate (string).
  • Database: action_type.code_template (TEXT) in V1__baseline.sql; import/export carries the field.

docs.title: UI
docs.text:
• Action Type editor: execution mode "Node.js"; a JavaScript code editor (Monaco, javascript language) replaces the script editor in that mode, seeded with a starter module exporting run; help text covers inputs, ctx and built-ins only.
  • Assistant Action Type preview: shows the code with JavaScript highlighting.

docs.title: Assistant
docs.text:
• Generated reference documents node mode, the run(inputs, ctx) contract, ctx, built-ins only, and when to prefer node (JSON reshaping, HTTP calls) vs script (short shell pipelines).
  • New bundled example action-types/fetch-repo-labels.json (node mode, uses ctx.exec("gh", …)), validated and applied end to end by AssistantReferenceTest.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
• Runner writes one leading stderr line, then the stack: Action failed: <message>; Action module does not export run(); run() must return an object, got <type>.
  • node not on PATH at run time → task fails: "Node.js is required to run node action types but was not found on PATH."
  • Timeout → process tree killed, task fails with the timeout message.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Runner (real node): typed inputs (array, object, number); returned object becomes outputs; ctx.log only on stderr; ctx.exec("echo", ["a b"]) keeps one argument; $(…) in an exec argument is not executed; throw / missing run / non-object result fail with the messages above; working directory honoured.
  • Validator: placeholder rejected; import x from "lodash" and require("axios") rejected; node:fs and fs accepted; missing run rejected; syntax error reported; valid module accepted.
  • End to end: a workflow action node using a node action type completes with typed outputs.
  • REST and import/export round-trip codeTemplate.
  • Assistant example validates and applies.
  • UI (Vitest): Node.js mode shows the code editor; the assistant preview shows the code.

docs.title: Workflow Workbench: Integrated AI Developer Experience — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-08 Status: Approved (brainstorming) Related: Apitomy Flow spec apitomy-flow/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-ai-assisted-editing-design.md (commit c20d5af), handoff notes in agentdocs/handoff/.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Axiom's Configuration Assistant is a chat that writes JSON files into a private directory and applies them at the end. The Workflow Workbench is an integrated, AI-based experience for composing a workflow together with the action types and tools that support it. The user and the AI edit the same live drafts, and their edits interleave throughout the session.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Audience Goal-to-workflow creation first, then continued iteration in the same session ("A-first, then B"). Concurrency Interleaved turns. The user edits freely; AI changes land as discrete, highlighted, undoable revisions. While the AI works, only the action types and tools it touches in that turn are locked. Draft state Server-side composition drafts in the database, with a revision history. Publish is partial and the session continues. AI runtime One long-running interactive session (AssistantSession + InteractiveSessionDriver, claude-code and opencode). The agent edits only through MCP tools. It has no file-write tools. Workflow edits by AI Flow ChangeSets, validated server-side with Flow's Java ChangeSets.apply, accumulated per turn into one combined change set, delivered to the editor. Layout A new three-pane workbench page: composition tree, tabbed editors, chat. Focus mode and break-out window. Testing in the loop v1: run draft action types and tools with sample inputs, and evaluate EL expressions against real events. Follow-up: whole-workflow dry run. Event stream The agent can list and read real stream events and evaluate EL against them. No redaction in v1. Configuration Assistant Kept. Both features share a refactored foundation built on template capabilities. v1 item types Workflow (exactly one per composition), action types, tools. Event sources, subscriptions, toolsets and session templates stay with the Configuration Assistant.

docs.title: Dependencies on Apitomy Flow
docs.text:
The workbench uses Apitomy Flow 3.0.1 (io.apitomy:apitomy-flow-engine and @apitomy/flow-ui, both published). Flow's user guide docs/user-guide/ai-assisted-editing.md is the reference. What Axiom uses:

  • Content revisions: computeContentRevision(workflow) (TS) and ContentRevision.of(JsonNode) (Java), "sha256:" + hex(SHA-256(JCS(stripLayout(workflow)))).
  • Change sets: ChangeSet / ChangeOp (with unset) and the error codes target-missing, duplicate-id, edge-endpoint-missing, malformed, read-only, stale. Java: ChangeSets.apply(JsonNode, JsonNode) / applyChecked(...) returning ChangeSetResult.Applied(ObjectNode) or Rejected(ChangeSetError). Java does not position added nodes.
  • Editor handle (React 19 ref): propose, apply, withdraw, replace(workflow, origin?), clearHighlights, getSnapshot(). No method throws.
  • Editor props: onChange(workflow, { contentRevision, origin }), onProposalResolved(id, outcome), onSelectionChange({ nodeIds, edgeIds }), highlightApplied (default true) and appliedChangeLayout: 'place' | 'tidy' (default 'place').
  • SPI: actionTypes (a new array or provider reloads the catalog without a remount; unknown action types show as unresolved), openActionType({ value, resolved }) (Open / Create… in the Properties panel), contextActions(FlowContext) (host menu items on canvas, node, edge, selection and Problems rows), and validate.

Axiom rules: - The server computes contentRevision over exactly the Flow Workflow JSON it sends to the editor, with no Axiom-specific fields. It hashes and sends the stored JSON as-is (ContentRevision.of(JsonNode)), never a re-serialized Java object, so that null values and key sets match what the browser hashes. - Change sets the agent writes use author: "agent:axiom-workbench". - Nodes added by the agent have no position on the server until the editor places them and onChange saves the placed document.

docs.title: Composition model (new database tables, added to V1__baseline.sql)
docs.text:
• CompositionEntity:
  • id, name, goal (the user's first request, kept for recaps), engine, model;
  • assistantSessionId;
  • turnState (idle | ai-working) and currentTurnId;
  • pendingChangeSet (JSON, nullable) and pendingTurnId;
  • applyMode (live | review), defaulting to live;
  • createdAt, updatedAt.
  • CompositionItemEntity:
  • id, compositionId, type (workflow | action-type | tool), name;
  • baseItemId and baseContentRevision (the hash of the published item's JSON when it was loaded or last published), set when the draft edits an existing item;
  • content (JSON) and contentRevision;
  • lastAuthor, lastTurnId, publishedAt, publishedRevision.
  • CompositionRevisionEntity:
  • id, itemId, content, contentRevision;
  • author (user | ai), turnId (null for user edits), createdAt.

For workflows, content is the Flow Workflow document and contentRevision is Flow's hash. For action types and tools, content is the item JSON and contentRevision is the same hash scheme applied to the item JSON (SHA-256 of the JCS form).

docs.title: Shared assistant foundation (refactor)
docs.text:
• Template capabilities replace every check of the template ID axiom-config-assistant:
  • config-items: the current file-based items, validate and apply endpoints, and the working-directory subfolders.
  • validation-feedback: the current listener that re-validates files after each tool result.
  • composition: binds the session to a composition and enables the workbench MCP server.
  • The Configuration Assistant template declares config-items and validation-feedback, and its behaviour does not change. The UI's isConfigAssistant becomes a capability check.
  • Persisted conversation history: every normalized event is appended to ${axiom.home}/assistant/sessions/<id>/history.jsonl. After a restart the chat is rebuilt from that file. Composition sessions are not deleted at startup.
  • MCP authentication: each session gets a random token, passed to its MCP server process in an environment variable and sent as an X-Axiom-Session-Token header. Composition and workbench endpoints require it when the call comes from MCP. Calls from the UI are unaffected.

docs.title: MCP server axiom-workbench (new)
docs.text:
Location: app/src/main/resources/templates/axiom-workbench-mcp/server.js. It is installed like axiom-assistant and receives AXIOM_COMPOSITION_ID and the token. Its tools:

Tool Purpose get_composition Items with names, types, status and problems, plus the workflow document and its contentRevision. get_item(type, name) Full draft content. propose_workflow_changes(changeSet) Validate the change set and add it to this turn's accumulated change set. Returns the resulting contentRevision and any problems, or a ChangeSetError. upsert_action_type(item), upsert_tool(item) Save a whole-item draft revision (author ai, current turn). Returns the problems. remove_item(type, name) Remove a draft from the composition. It does not delete the published item. validate_composition Validate all drafts against the drafts plus the database. test_action_type(name, inputs, subjectId?), test_tool(name, params, subjectId?) Run the draft and return the outputs, stdout, stderr, exit code, duration and output-validation problems. list_stream_events(type?, eventSourceId?, ref?, limit<=20) Compact summaries: id, type, source, ref, actor, time and top-level payload keys. get_stream_event(eventId, path?) The normalized event, optionally narrowed to path. Large values are truncated with a marker. evaluate_expression(expression, scope, eventId?, context?) Evaluate EL with the engine's evaluator. Returns the value or the error. Read-only discovery The list and get tools of axiom-assistant, for database items and secret names.

Within a turn, propose_workflow_changes builds on the turn's accumulated workflow: the first change set's baseRevision is the revision at the start of the turn, and each later one uses the revision returned by the previous call. The server stores the combined change set as the concatenation of the ops, with the base revision from the start of the turn.

docs.title: Template axiom-workbench (built in)
docs.text:
• Capabilities: composition.
  • MCP: @axiom-workbench.
  • Allowed tools: all mcp__workbench__* tools, read-only shell (ls, cat, jq), and no Write or Edit.
  • System prompt: the working loop, then the generated reference (reused from AssistantReferenceGenerator and extended with the ChangeSet op reference), then the prompt rules. The rules include:
  • Edit workflows only with change sets, and read get_composition first.
  • Before writing an EL expression that reads event data, inspect a real event of that type with get_stream_event and check the expression with evaluate_expression. If no event of that type exists, say so and use the documented event schema.
  • Test action types and tools you create with test_action_type or test_tool before finishing a turn.
  • The existing rules: prefer node, declare inputs, correlate receive-event nodes, do not describe the output format in prompts.
