WorkbenchReferenceTest asserts that each rule is present.

docs.title: The turn loop
docs.text:
1. The user sends a message. The client flushes its pending workflow onChange save, then posts the message.
  2. The server sets turnState = ai-working and creates a turnId. It builds a preamble that includes:
  3. the workflow's contentRevision;
  4. a summary of user edits since the AI's last turn, built from diffs of user-authored revisions;
  5. the current selection, if the client sent one.
  6. The agent works through MCP:
  7. Action type and tool upserts are saved as revisions immediately and pushed to the UI over SSE.
  8. Workflow change sets accumulate on the server.
  9. On turn_complete, if a combined change set exists, the server publishes a composition-changeset SSE event. The client then calls handle.apply(cs) (live mode) or handle.propose(cs) (review mode):
  10. On success, onChange with an agent: origin saves the revision with the turn's turnId.
  11. If the result is stale, the server re-prompts the agent once with the diff and the new revision. A second stale result ends the turn with a chat notice.
  12. The server sets turnState = idle and releases the locks.

Only the editor commits workflow change sets: the server never writes a combined change set into the draft itself, because Java does not position added nodes. If no editor is open when a turn ends (for example, the browser was closed), the combined change set is stored on the composition as the pending change set and sent to the editor the next time the workbench opens. The editor applies or proposes it as usual; a stale result discards it and posts a chat notice offering to ask the agent again. A newer turn replaces any pending change set.

docs.title: Publish
docs.text:
• POST /compositions/{id}/publish {items[]} builds a configuration pack from the selected drafts and runs ImportExportService.importOrUpdatePack in a single transaction. Workflows are published as part of it.
  • Checks before publishing:
  • Every selected draft is valid. Warnings are allowed.
  • A selected workflow's new action-type dependencies are also selected or already exist.
  • The published item's current JSON still hashes to the draft's baseContentRevision. If it does not, the item was changed outside the workbench, and the server returns a conflict that the user confirms with force.
  • On success, the server sets publishedAt and publishedRevision on the items. The session continues.

docs.title: Routes and entry points
docs.text:
• /workbench lists compositions and has a New composition button.
  • /workbench/:id is the workbench. With ?chrome=none, it is used for break-out windows.
  • Open in workbench… on WorkflowDefinitionDetailPage creates a composition seeded with the workflow, its action types, and the tools those action types reference in allowedTools.
  • A Workbench entry under Configuration in AppSidebar.

docs.title: Left pane: composition tree
docs.text:
• The workflow, then action types, then tools. Each item shows:
  • a status icon (valid, warnings or errors);
  • an unpublished-changes dot;
  • an AI badge if the last turn changed it.
  • + Action type and + Tool create a blank draft or add an existing item.
  • A revision list for the selected item, with author and turn. Selecting a revision shows a diff and offers Restore, which creates a new user revision.
  • A Publish… dialog with per-item checkboxes. Changed, valid items are preselected, and required dependencies are checked automatically.

docs.title: Centre pane: tabbed editors
docs.text:
• Workflow tab: the Flow WorkflowEditor with a ref handle.
  • onChange saves a revision, debounced by 500 ms and flushed before each AI turn.
  • onSelectionChange records the selection as context for the AI.
  • spi.openActionType opens the action type's tab (Open), or creates a blank draft with that name and opens it (Create…) when the value is unresolved.
  • spi.validate calls draft validation on the server.
  • spi.actionTypes is an array of database action types merged with draft ones. It is replaced whenever a draft action type is created, renamed or has its inputs or outputs changed, so the palette and the unresolved markers update without a remount.
  • spi.contextActions adds Ask AI about this… on node, edge, selection and canvas menus, and Ask AI to fix this on Problems rows. Each pre-fills the chat input with a description of the target (ids, names, the problem text) and records the menu's contentRevision with the message. The items are disabled while the AI is working and hidden when context.readOnly.
  • appliedChangeLayout is a workbench preference (Place new nodes or Tidy after AI changes), stored in localStorage, default 'place'.
  • Action type tab: the new ActionTypeEditor component, extracted from ActionTypeDetailPage. It takes value and onChange. ActionTypeDetailPage is refactored to use it.
  • Tool tab: the new ToolEditor component, extracted from the tool detail page in the same way.
  • During an AI turn: items the AI has touched in the current turn are read-only, with a banner, and refresh live. All other items stay editable.
  • Bottom strip (collapsible):
  • Problems for the active item. Clicking one jumps to the node or field.
  • Test output: test runs and expression evaluations by the user or the AI.
  • A Test… button on action type and tool tabs opens a sample-input form.

docs.title: Right pane: chat
docs.text:
• It reuses AssistantChatPanel.
  • Compact cards for workbench tool calls, for example "Updated action type add-comment" or "Proposed 4 workflow changes". Each card links to its tab.
  • A turn header with Undo AI turn:
  • It restores the previous revision of every action type and tool the turn changed.
  • For the workflow, it calls handle.replace(<workflow revision saved before the turn>, 'host'). This is a new undoable step, so Ctrl+Z restores the AI's version. It is offered only when the workflow's latest saved revision is the one the turn produced (no user or host onChange since). Otherwise it leaves the workflow alone and says so in chat. Flow has no host-callable undo, and none is needed.
  • A mode toggle, Apply live (the default) or Review changes.

docs.title: Maximizing space
docs.text:
• Focus mode: a toolbar toggle (Ctrl+Shift+F) hides the app masthead and sidebar. It is persisted in localStorage.
  • Break out: opens /workbench/:id?chrome=none in a new window. The original tab shows a "Bring back here" notice.
  • Resizable, collapsible panes: drag splitters between the panes. The side panes collapse to rails, and the chat rail shows an AI-working or unread indicator. Sizes are persisted. A Maximize canvas action collapses both side panes.

docs.title: Session lifecycle
docs.text: Compositions persist. After a restart, the chat is restored from history.jsonl. On the next message, the agent process starts again with a recap: the goal, a composition summary and the last 20 messages. Deleting a composition discards its unpublished drafts, after a confirmation.

docs.title: §3 REST API (openapi-first, tag Compositions)
docs.text:
• GET/POST /compositions and GET/PATCH/DELETE /compositions/{id}.
  • POST accepts {name, goal?, engine?, seedWorkflowId?}.
  • PATCH accepts name and applyMode.
  • GET /compositions/{id}/items and POST /compositions/{id}/items. POST creates a blank draft or adds an existing item.
  • GET/PUT/DELETE /compositions/{id}/items/{itemId}. PUT takes {content, baseRevision} and returns 409 if baseRevision is not current.
  • GET /compositions/{id}/items/{itemId}/revisions and POST .../revisions/{revId}/restore.
  • UI turn routes:
  • POST /compositions/{id}/messages, with {message, nodeIds?, edgeIds?}. Starts a turn; 409 if one is running.
  • POST /compositions/{id}/interrupt.
  • POST /compositions/{id}/changeset-resolution, with {turnId, outcome}. outcome is one of applied, accepted, rejected or stale.
  • Agent routes, for MCP. Each requires the X-Axiom-Session-Token header of the composition's live workbench session and returns 401 otherwise:
  • GET /compositions/{id}/agent/composition: the turn, goal, current workflow and its revision, and a summary of every item with its problems.
  • GET /compositions/{id}/agent/items/{itemType}/{itemName} and DELETE on the same path.
  • PUT /compositions/{id}/agent/items, with {type, content}.
  • POST /compositions/{id}/agent/workflow/changesets. The body is a ChangeSet. It returns {applied, contentRevision?, problems[], error?}, where error is a ChangeSetError.
  • POST /compositions/{id}/validate.
  • POST /compositions/{id}/test/action-type and POST /compositions/{id}/test/tool.
  • POST /compositions/{id}/turns/{turnId}/undo.
  • POST /compositions/{id}/publish.
  • Conversation: reuse the assistant session endpoints via assistantSessionId.
  • POST /expressions/evaluate, with body {expression, scope, eventId?, context?}. scope is one of:
  • edge-condition;
  • action-input;
  • human-task-title;
  • correlation-subscription-key;
  • correlation-event-key;
  • receive-event-match;
  • receive-event-output.

Each scope builds the same EL variables the engine provides at that point. - New SSE event types: - composition-item-changed, with {compositionId, itemId, contentRevision, author, turnId}; - composition-turn, with {compositionId, turnId, state}; - composition-changeset, with {compositionId, turnId, changeSet}.

docs.title: §4 Error handling
docs.text:
• Change set rejected during a turn: the MCP tool returns the ChangeSetError and the validation problems, and the agent fixes them within the turn. Nothing is sent to the client.
  • Stale at the end of a turn: the server re-prompts the agent once. A second stale result ends the turn with a notice.
  • Client apply fails for another reason: the client shows an error card with Reload workflow from server, which calls handle.replace.
  • Two windows on one composition: saves carry baseRevision, and a mismatch returns 409 with the notice "Changed elsewhere — reload". Only the window holding the workflow editor lease (a heartbeat, 30 seconds) can edit the workflow. Other windows show it read-only.
  • Agent error or process exit: the turn ends, turnState resets to idle, and the locks are released. A Restart agent button resumes the session with a recap.
  • Server restart during a turn: at startup, compositions in ai-working reset to idle, and any accumulated change set is discarded. Action type and tool revisions saved during the turn keep their turnId, so Undo AI turn still works.
  • Publish: it is all-or-nothing. Failures return 422 with problems per item, and the session is kept. Missing dependencies are blocked in the dialog and on the server. A base conflict needs confirmation.
  • Test runs:
  • They use the existing timeouts and truncate output.
  • They run in a scratch workspace, unless the user chooses a subject.
  • Tests of agent-mode action types cost money and are recorded in AiUsageEntity.
  • Event tools: an unknown event or path returns a clear message. Payloads are truncated.

docs.title: §5 Testing
docs.text:
All Java tests use JUnit 5 and the isolated axiom.home.

  • Composition service:
  • revisions and turn tagging;
  • undo of a turn;
  • 409 on a stale baseRevision;
  • restart recovery from ai-working.
  • Change-set endpoint:
  • delegation to Flow ChangeSets.apply;
  • validation against drafts plus the database;
  • accumulation and the base revision used for the combined set;
  • a single stale re-prompt.
  • contentRevision parity: Axiom's stored hash equals Flow's for the documents it sends. The test reuses Flow's conformance fixtures.
  • Publish:
  • partial selection;
  • dependency blocking;
  • base conflict;
  • a single transaction.
  • /expressions/evaluate: every scope, against StreamEventEntity fixtures.
  • Capabilities refactor: the existing Configuration Assistant tests pass unchanged.
  • WorkbenchReferenceTest: the prompt rules are present, and the change-set examples are valid according to Flow.
  • MCP server: a Node test of the mapping from tools to REST calls and of the token header.
  • UI (vitest, pure logic):
  • tree status;
  • publish dependency selection;
  • the turn and lock reducer;
  • the undo-AI-turn decision;
  • persistence of pane sizes and focus mode.
  • Manual (Chrome DevTools MCP): go from a goal to a workflow with an action type and a tool, interleave manual edits, trigger the stale path, publish, and use a break-out window.

docs.title: §6 Phasing
docs.text:
1. Foundation: template capabilities, persisted history, MCP token. The Configuration Assistant is unchanged.
  2. Composition backend, in two plans:
  3. 2a: the apitomy-flow-engine 3.0.1 upgrade, entities and revisions, the UI-facing REST API, draft validation and publish.
  4. 2b: the turn loop, change-set endpoint and pending change sets, MCP-only routes with the token guard, session restore, /expressions/evaluate, the stream-event tools, and the axiom-workbench MCP server, template and reference. Scope:
  5. entities, REST, revisions, draft validation and publish;
  6. /expressions/evaluate and the stream-event tools;
  7. the axiom-workbench MCP server, template and reference.
  8. Carried over from the Phase 1 review: one shared session-token guard for every MCP-called endpoint; MCP-only routes, so MCP calls never share a route with UI calls; startup cleanup must keep COMPOSITION session directories (and their history.jsonl); restoring a session passes its token and capabilities at construction and normalizes missing event data; move journal writes out of the event lock.
  9. Flow 3.0.1 upgrade (UI): upgrade @apitomy/flow-ui to 3.0.1 and adapt the existing editor, viewer and diff usages; wire openActionType on WorkflowDefinitionDetailPage. The Java apitomy-flow-engine upgrade to 3.0.1 is done at the start of Phase 2, because the change-set endpoint needs ChangeSets and ContentRevision. This phase can run before or alongside Phase 2.
  10. Workbench UI:
  11. the page, tree and tabs;
  12. the extracted ActionTypeEditor and ToolEditor;
  13. chat integration, apply and review modes, and undo of an AI turn;
  14. focus mode, break-out and resizable panes.
  15. Testing in the loop: test runs from the UI and from MCP, and the test output strip.

docs.title: Out of scope for v1 (planned follow-ups)
docs.text:
• Whole-workflow dry run using flow-ui's simulator.
  • Inline one-shot AI helpers in the editors, including a helper for node codeTemplate.
  • Event sources, subscriptions and toolsets in the workbench.
  • The copilot engine. It needs interactive session support.
  • Simultaneous (non-turn-based) editing by the user and the AI.

docs.title: Workbench: Testing Workflows — Design
docs.text: Status: proposed (not scheduled). Follows Phase 5 (test runs of action types and tools) and Phase 5b (the AI only suggests tests). Tracking issue: https://github.com/Apitomy/apitomy-axiom/issues/469

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Let the user test the composition's draft workflow from the workbench before publishing it, in two layers:

  1. Layer 1 — Simulate (routing check, in the browser). Re-enable Apitomy Flow's Simulate feature in the workbench canvas and make it practical by pre-filling it from real data.
  2. Layer 2 — Dry run (the real engine, server-side). Run the draft workflow through Axiom's real workflow engine with every action stubbed, and show the result in Apitomy Flow's WorkflowViewer.

Layer 1 ships first; layer 2 is a later phase.

docs.title: Decisions (agreed 2026-10-14)
docs.text: Topic Decision Starting data Pre-fill from real data (a real stream event of the workflow's trigger type, and the outputs of the action types' last passing test runs). The user can always replace it with their own JSON. Actions in a dry run Always stubbed in v1. Nothing with side effects runs. No "run for real" option. Showing a dry run Apitomy Flow's WorkflowViewer (path taken, current node, per-visit inputs/outputs). Order Layer 1 first, layer 2 later. Who runs tests Only the user (Phase 5b rule). The AI may suggest a simulation/dry run, never start one.

docs.title: What Simulate is
docs.text: Flow's Simulate (see apitomy-flow/docs/user-guide/visual-editor.md, "Simulation and Condition Testing") runs the workflow's routing in the browser: the user enters a sample start context (JSON), then Steps/Runs; at action, human-task and receive-event nodes it pauses for a mock output (JSON); waits pass through. It uses a browser subset of Jakarta EL and is explicitly an authoring aid, not the engine.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• Re-enable Simulate in ui/src/pages/workbench/WorkflowTab.tsx (remove simulate: false from EDITOR_FEATURES). The properties dialog mode stays; Flow brings the side panel back while simulating.
  • Pre-filled start context. A Start context helper next to the Simulate panel (or a menu on the workbench canvas toolbar, depending on what Flow allows hosts to inject — see Open questions):
  • From a real event: pick from recent stream events of the workflow's trigger type (default: the most recent); the context is built the way the engine builds a run's start context from an event (same mapping as production — reuse the backend's event-to-context mapping through a small endpoint, do not reimplement it in the UI).
  • My own JSON: an editor with the last value the user used.
  • Mock outputs from test runs. When the simulation pauses at an action node, offer the outputs of that action type's last passing test run (Phase 5 run store) as the mock output, editable before continuing. If Flow's simulation API does not let the host supply a mock-output default, this needs a Flow change.
  • No AI changes in layer 1 (optional: a suggest_simulation tool is deferred to layer 2's suggestion).

docs.title: Needs from Apitomy Flow (to confirm)
docs.text:
• A host hook to set/replace the simulation's sample start context.
  • A host hook to provide a default mock output when the simulation pauses at a node. If missing, add them in a Flow 3.x release (Flow is ours).

docs.title: Layer 2: Dry run on the real engine
Behaviour
docs.text:
• Start: a Dry run… dialog (workflow tab and the Test output strip) with the trigger data — a real stream event (default: most recent of the trigger type) or custom JSON — and one stub per action node:
  • default stub = the action type's last passing test run outputs; editable JSON per node;
  • nodes without a stub show a warning; the run fails at that node with a clear message if reached.
  • Engine: the draft workflow (with draft action types resolved from the composition) runs in Axiom's real workflow engine in dry-run mode:
  • action nodes never execute; their output is the stub, then validated against the action type's declared outputs (exactly as a real task's output is);
  • input bindings into actions are evaluated and validated (required inputs, types) and recorded;
  • edge conditions, defaults, fork/join, EL — all real engine behaviour;
  • wait nodes complete immediately (recorded as skipped waits);
  • human task and receive event nodes use a stub too (provided up front in the dialog; default {} with a warning), so a dry run never blocks. (Interactive pausing is a possible follow-up.)
  • no side effects: no tasks are queued for agents, no events are emitted, no subject workspaces are touched, nothing is written to the regular runs tables (see Open questions for storage).
  • Result: a dry-run entry in the Test output strip (status passed/failed/error, duration, the node that failed and why). Its details dialog shows Apitomy Flow's WorkflowViewer with the draft workflow and a WorkflowInstance built from the dry run's history (visited nodes, edges taken, per-visit inputs and outputs, the failing node highlighted red), plus the final context as highlighted JSON.
  • AI: a suggest_dry_run(trigger?, stubs?) MCP tool, mirroring suggest_test: stores a suggested dry run; the user reviews and edits trigger/stubs in the Dry run dialog and runs it. The workbench prompt rule: suggest a dry run after significant workflow changes; never claim the workflow works until the user reports a passing dry run.

docs.title: Backend sketch
docs.text:
• POST /compositions/{id}/workflow/dry-run (UI route) and POST /compositions/{id}/agent/dry-run-suggestions (MCP-only, token guarded), contract-first in openapi.json.
  • A WorkflowDryRunner that drives the engine with a stub task executor instead of TaskExecutionService, in memory, bounded (step limit, time limit), sharing the per-composition concurrency cap with test runs.
  • Results stored in the existing in-memory run store (CompositionTestRuns) with itemType: "workflow" and a history/instance payload compatible with Flow's WorkflowInstance.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
1. Can Axiom's workflow engine run fully in memory with a pluggable task executor, or does it require persisted run/task rows? If rows are required: a separate dry-run table, or a flag + cleanup.
  2. Which Flow host hooks exist today for the simulation context and default mock outputs (layer 1)?
  3. Should the trigger picker in both layers share one component (recommended)?
  4. How is the "workflow's trigger type" determined for a draft (subscription vs. start node inputs)? Needed to filter real events.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Running real actions in a dry run (v1 always stubs).
  • AI-initiated execution of any kind.
  • Testing AI Agent action types.

docs.title: Standard Workflow Inputs — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-15 Status: Approved in discussion; awaiting spec review

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Make a workflow's Start node the complete, explicit contract for what a run receives. A workflow declares which of a small set of standard inputs it needs; when Axiom creates a run it satisfies the declared inputs and nothing else. A run whose required inputs cannot be satisfied is not created.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Standard inputs Exactly two: subject (object) and event (object) subject fields id, name, type, ref, refSource, repository — nothing else Undeclared inputs Not provided: a run's initial context contains only the declared standard inputs Custom inputs Removed: a Start node may declare only standard inputs Supplied run inputs Removed everywhere (dialog, REST, schedule triggers, re-runs) defaultValue on Start inputs Removed (rejected at publish) Required but unsatisfiable Run creation fails; no run is created New-workflow scaffold Declares subject and event, both required

docs.title: Current State (for reference)
docs.text:
• Axiom always puts subjectId, subjectName, ref, repository (and event when started from an event) into every run's context, declared or not (WorkflowExecutionService.triggerWorkflow).
  • Start inputs may be custom; supplied run inputs (RunRequest.inputs) join the context; protected names are ignored; applyStartInputDefaults applies defaultValues.
  • The Flow engine (NodeValueResolver.validateStartInputs) only checks that required inputs are present and non-null; it does not check types or reject undeclared keys.
  • Publish rules (WorkflowContentRules.startInputViolation): valid identifier names; event, subjectName and repository may not be required.

docs.title: 1. Standard Inputs Registry
docs.text:
A new class io.apitomy.axiom.app.StandardInputs (next to WorkflowExecutionService, its main user) is the single source of truth. Each entry has a name, a type, a description and a resolver:

Input Type Value Satisfied when subject object {id, name, type, ref, refSource, repository} snapshot of the run's subject at run creation; absent values are null always (every run has a subject) event object the triggering event envelope (id, type, source, eventSourceId, ref, timestamp, actor, payload) — unchanged from today the run was started from a stream event: subscription create-workflow, Run workflow… on an event, or a re-run of an event-started run

subject.id is a number; the other subject fields are strings or null.

The registry is used by: run creation (resolution), publish/validation rules, the new-workflow scaffold, and the assistant reference generator. Adding a standard input or a subject field later is a registry change.

docs.title: 2. Run Creation
docs.text:
WorkflowExecutionService.triggerWorkflow builds the initial context from the Start node's declared inputs:

  1. For each declared input, ask the registry to resolve it for this run (subject + optional origin event).
  2. Satisfied → put it in the context under its name.
  3. Not satisfied and optional → leave it out (no key).
  4. Not satisfied and required → collect it.
  5. If any were collected, fail before creating the run with HTTP 400 and the message Cannot start workflow "<name>": required input(s) not available: <names>.

Undeclared standard inputs are never put in the context. PROTECTED_INPUTS and applyStartInputDefaults are removed. The event value continues to come from EventStreamOrchestrator.startRunFromEvent, but as the event origin passed to resolution rather than as free-form extraContext; RunRequest.extraContext is removed if nothing else needs it.

Failure handling per trigger path (existing mechanisms, new message):

Path Outcome on unsatisfied required input Run workflow… on an event (POST /stream/events/{eventId}/runs) HTTP 400; message shown in the dialog POST /subjects/{subjectId}/workflow (API only) HTTP 400 Re-run (POST /workflow/runs/{runId}/rerun) HTTP 400; shown by the re-run UI Schedule trigger trigger lastOutcome = failed: <message> Subscription create-workflow routing recorded as a failed routing outcome via the existing failure path

Runs that need subject data an action requires but the subject lacks (e.g. no repository) start normally and fail at that node with the existing Missing required input(s): … task error. This is an accepted trade-off of a single subject object.

docs.title: 3. Removing Supplied Inputs
docs.text:
• REST/OpenAPI: remove inputs from TriggerWorkflow (subject and event run creation bodies) and from NewScheduleTrigger / ScheduleTrigger.
  • Java: remove RunRequest.inputs; re-runs no longer copy inputs (they re-resolve from the subject and original event); the schedule scheduler no longer passes static inputs.
  • Database (V1__baseline.sql, edited in place): drop the schedule trigger inputs column. The run's inputs column stays (see below). A persistent database reset is required.
  • UI: remove the Inputs field from Run workflow… (RunWorkflowFromEventModal) and the schedule trigger inputs from WorkflowTriggersTab; remove now-unused parsing helpers.
  • Stored run inputs: workflow_run.inputs and the inputs field on WorkflowInstance / WorkflowRunSummary now hold the resolved standard inputs excluding event (the event is already linked as Triggered by), i.e. {"subject": {...}} when declared. The run Overview's Inputs field shows it as JSON unchanged.
  • SDK: axiom_get_workflow_run keeps returning inputs (now the resolved inputs).

docs.title: 4. Publish and Validation Rules
docs.text:
WorkflowContentRules.startInputViolation (used by WorkflowPublisher and ConfigItemValidationService, so it covers publish and the workbench's propose_workflow_changes) rejects a Start node input when:

  1. its name is not a standard input name (message lists the standard inputs);
  2. its declared type is set and differs from the standard type;
  3. it declares a defaultValue.

The old rule forbidding required on event/subjectName/repository is removed; requiring event is how a workflow says it must be started from an event.

Reading an undeclared standard input (e.g. context.subject without declaring subject) is not checked: a node output with that name may legitimately provide it. Standard input names are not reserved.

docs.title: Shadowing warning
docs.text:
Workflow validation (ConfigItemValidationService.validateWorkflow, which backs the workbench's propose_workflow_changes problems and assistant item validation) adds a warning, code SHADOWS_WORKFLOW_INPUT, when a node would write a context key equal to the name of an input declared on the Start node. The warning is reported at the node and names the node, the key and the input, e.g. Output 'event' of node 'Review' overwrites the workflow input 'event' for later nodes. It does not block publish.

Statically known output keys checked:

  • an action node's declared config.outputs names, and its action type's declared outputs (via the validation context, which gains action-type outputs alongside the existing actionTypeInputs);
  • a receive-event node's output mapping context keys;
  • a human-task node's form field names.

sdk: node results are not declared anywhere and are not checked.

docs.title: 5. New-Workflow Scaffold
docs.text:
WorkflowTemplates.emptyWorkflow declares:

[
  {"name": "subject", "type": "object", "required": true,  "description": "The subject the run is about"},
  {"name": "event",   "type": "object", "required": true,  "description": "The event that started the run"}
]

Used by the workbench and by Components → Workflows → new. A schedule-triggered workflow must remove event or make it optional.

docs.title: 6. Expressions and Built-in Content
docs.text:
context.ref → context.subject.ref, context.subjectId → context.subject.id, context.subjectName → context.subject.name, context.repository → context.subject.repository. Update:

  • AssistantReferenceGenerator text and the SDK node example;
  • ActionTypeValidator hints (e.g. "map it from context.subject.ref");
  • assistant-reference/examples/workflows/issue-triage.json and any other bundled workflows;
  • axiom-config-assistant.json prompt text;
  • user and developer docs.

Engine-supplied values that do not come from the context are unaffected: sdk: nodes still get subjectId and runId from the run, and tasks still get the run's subject.

docs.title: 7. Workbench AI
docs.text:
The generated reference gains a Start inputs section, generated from the registry: a table of the standard inputs with type, availability and (for subject) its fields, followed by the rules:

  • declare only standard inputs; no other inputs and no defaultValue;
  • mark event required only if the workflow must be started from an event (schedule-triggered workflows must not require it);
  • read only declared inputs (context.subject.<field>, context.event.<field>);
  • do not give node outputs the name of a declared input (validation warns: SHADOWS_WORKFLOW_INPUT).

The workbench prompt rule list gets a matching one-line rule.

docs.title: 8. Documentation
docs.text: Rewrite docs/developer-guide/workflow-input-contract.md around the registry (and drop the stale subject Run Workflow dialog text). Update docs/user-guide/workflows.md (inputs, triggers, schedule inputs, Run workflow… dialog), concepts.md, usage-examples.md and workflow-human-task-nodes.md for the new expressions.

docs.title: 9. Testing
docs.text:
• Unit: registry resolution (subject snapshot with nulls; event present/absent); publish rules (unknown name, wrong type, defaultValue, required event now allowed); SHADOWS_WORKFLOW_INPUT warnings for each output source, and none for outputs that do not match a declared input; scaffold content; reference section content.
  • Integration (@QuarkusTest): context contains only declared inputs; optional unsatisfied event is absent; required unsatisfied event fails for each event-less trigger path (subject REST API, schedule trigger outcome, re-run of a run that was not started from an event); stored run inputs excludes event; removed inputs fields are gone from the API.
  • UI (Vitest): Run workflow… has no Inputs field; schedule trigger form has no inputs.
  • Existing tests that rely on context.ref-style keys or supplied inputs are updated.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Per-field requirements on subject.
  • Any additional standard inputs or subject fields (labels, body, metadata, trigger).
  • Changes to the Flow engine.

docs.title: Workbench Subscriptions — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-15 Status: Approved in discussion; awaiting spec review

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Let a workbench composition define the subscriptions that trigger its workflow, so the workbench goes from a goal to working automation. Publishing never turns automation on: the user enables each published subscription explicitly.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Topic Decision Item type New composition item type subscription, any number per composition Routing create-workflow rules must target the composition's own workflow; workflow-dispatch rules allowed Going live Publish creates/updates subscriptions disabled; an explicit Enabled switch in the workbench enables Draft enabled Not part of the draft; ignored on publish, with a validation warning Enabling Sets enabled = true and processEventsFrom = now (no backlog) Republish Never changes a published subscription's enabled state Removing a draft / deleting the composition Published subscription untouched (same as other item types) Filter preview Existing POST /subscriptions/preview over the 200 most recent events, plus error info; AI tool preview_subscription and a UI panel

docs.title: Current State (for reference)
docs.text:
• Composition item types are workflow, action-type, tool (CompositionItems supported set). Publishing builds a configuration pack and calls ImportExportService.importOrUpdatePack, which already imports subscriptions (ConfigItemType.SUBSCRIPTION, pack array subscriptions).
  • Subscriptions (EventSubscriptionEntity): name, description, enabled, filters (EL filter), routing (JSON rules), processEventsFrom (defaults to creation time), labels. Pack/item JSON uses filterExpression for the filter.
  • Routing rules: create-workflow (workflowDefinitionName or workflowDefinitionId) starts runs; workflow-dispatch (no target) delivers events to every run waiting at a matching receive-event node. Without a workflow-dispatch subscription, receive-event nodes never receive events.
  • Subscription matching: SubscriptionFilterEvaluator.matches over EventStreamOrchestrator.filterEventMap (errors count as no match). ExpressionService already has a subscription-filter scope.

docs.title: 1. Subscription Items
docs.text:
• subscription joins the supported composition item types. Content is the pack form: {name, description, filterExpression, routing, labels}.
  • The workbench AI creates and edits them with the existing upsert_item (type: "subscription"); the user edits them in a form editor (Section 6).
  • An enabled field in a draft is ignored and reported as a warning ENABLED_IGNORED: "Subscriptions are published disabled; enable them in the workbench after publishing."
  • New empty subscription items are created with filterExpression: "", routing: [].

docs.title: 2. Validation (composition context, on top of existing subscription validation)
docs.text:
• Error FOREIGN_WORKFLOW_ROUTE: a create-workflow rule that does not use workflowDefinitionName equal to the name of the composition's workflow item (rules with workflowDefinitionId, or another name).
  • workflow-dispatch rules are allowed without further checks.
  • Warning OVERLAPPING_SUBSCRIPTION: another enabled published subscription, not owned by this composition, has a create-workflow rule for this composition's workflow.
  • Publish dependency: a subscription item requires the composition's workflow to be published already or selected in the same publish (same mechanism as action types requiring tools).

docs.title: 3. Publishing and Enabling
docs.text:
• Publish passes subscriptions through the existing pack import. Before import it removes enabled and processEventsFrom from each subscription pack item and sets them from the published subscription (when one exists) or to enabled: false (new; processEventsFrom then defaults to creation time). The import's update path otherwise resets enabled to false.
  • The published-content revision used for "changed outside the workbench" detection excludes enabled and processEventsFrom, so toggling the switch is not an outside change.
  • New endpoint (contract-first): PUT /compositions/{compositionId}/items/{itemId}/enabled with body {"enabled": boolean}.
  • 404 when the item is not in the composition; 409 when it is not a subscription or not yet published.
  • true: sets enabled = true and processEventsFrom = now. false: sets enabled = false.
  • Returns the item, including its published subscription's enabled state.
  • Composition item responses gain enabled (boolean, only for published subscription items) so the UI can show the switch state.
  • The Events → Subscriptions page is unchanged; changes made there are reflected in the switch.

docs.title: 4. Filter Preview
docs.text:
• Reuse the existing POST /subscriptions/preview (previewSubscriptionFilter; used today by the Subscriptions page) with {"filterExpression": ..., "limit": 200}: it evaluates the filter against the most recent events (by timestamp) and returns each with matched, plus totalMatched over all events.
  • Extend its response (contract-first, backward compatible) with errorCount (events on this page whose evaluation threw) and firstError (that first error message). Matching semantics are unchanged (an error is no match), so the Subscriptions page behaves as before.
  • AI tool preview_subscription(filterExpression) in the workbench MCP server: calls the endpoint with limit: 200 and formats "N of M recent events match", the error count/first error, and up to 20 matches (type, ref, actor login, timestamp), one line each.

docs.title: 5. Workbench AI
docs.text:
• Allowed tools gain mcp__workbench__preview_subscription.
  • Workbench reference gains a Subscriptions section:
  • a composition may define subscriptions (upsert_item type subscription);
  • create-workflow only to this composition's workflow, by workflowDefinitionName;
  • add a workflow-dispatch subscription whenever the workflow has receive-event nodes;
  • check filters with preview_subscription (and single events with evaluate_expression, scope subscription-filter);
  • do not set enabled: publishing leaves subscriptions disabled and the user enables them.
  • New prompt rule: "Never say the automation is live: published subscriptions stay disabled until the user enables them in the workbench."

docs.title: 6. UI
docs.text:
• Composition tree: a Subscriptions group listing subscription items; "add" creates an empty item.
  • Subscription editor: name, description, filter expression (monospace text area), routing rules (type select; create-workflow fixed to the composition's workflow), labels; and a Matching events panel that calls the preview endpoint for the current filter (debounced) and shows "N of 200 recent events match", errors, and the matched events linking to /events/stream/{id}.
  • An Enabled switch in the subscription editor header, shown only when the item is published; disabled with a tooltip when the composition's workflow is not published.

docs.title: 7. Testing
docs.text:
• Backend: item type supported; FOREIGN_WORKFLOW_ROUTE, ENABLED_IGNORED, OVERLAPPING_SUBSCRIPTION; publish dependency; publish creates disabled and preserves enabled on update; enable/disable endpoint (404/409, processEventsFrom set on enable); preview endpoint (matches, errors, limit 200).
  • Workbench MCP: preview_subscription formatting (Node test); reference and prompt tests.
  • UI: tree group, editor fields, Matching events panel, Enabled switch states.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Event sources (credentials, webhooks) in the workbench.
  • Disabling or deleting published subscriptions when drafts or compositions are removed.
  • Workbench test runs of subscriptions.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Allow users to customize a limited set of settings on the built-in AI Session Templates without cloning them, while still receiving upstream improvements (system prompts, tools, capabilities) on upgrade.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Editable on built-in templates: model, engine, environment.

All other fields (systemPrompt, mcpServers, allowedTools, workingDirectory, initScript, initScriptType, welcomeMessage, initialMessage, name, description, templateId, capabilities) remain locked. Cloning remains the escape hatch for deeper customization.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
• New Flyway migration V2__session_template_overrides.sql creating table session_template_override:
  • id (PK, sequence-backed, consistent with existing Panache entities)
  • template_id VARCHAR, unique, not null — the built-in template ID
  • model VARCHAR, nullable
  • engine VARCHAR, nullable
  • environment TEXT, nullable — JSON string, same format as SessionTemplateEntity.environment
  • New entity SessionTemplateOverrideEntity in core/.../entities/.
  • Semantics: a null field means "use the built-in default". The environment override replaces the default map (no merging).
  • When all three fields are null/empty after a save, the row is deleted.
  • Rows whose template_id no longer matches a built-in (e.g. a built-in removed in a later release) are ignored at read time.

docs.title: Service Layer (SessionTemplateService)
docs.text:
• getTemplate(id) and listTemplates() return built-ins with overrides merged in. Consumers such as AssistantSessionManager.createSession require no changes.
  • The returned SessionTemplate record gains overriddenFields (Set<String>, values from model, engine, environment; empty for user templates and un-overridden built-ins).
  • New methods:
  • getOverrides(String templateId) — returns current overrides (fields may be null).
  • setOverrides(String templateId, SessionTemplateOverrides overrides) — upserts; returns merged template.
  • clearOverrides(String templateId) — deletes the row if present.
  • Errors: unknown ID → not-found exception; non-built-in ID → IllegalArgumentException (mapped to 400).

docs.title: REST API (contract-first, common/api/src/main/resources/openapi.json)
docs.text:
New path /assistant/templates/{templateId}/overrides (tag Assistant):

Op operationId Request Response Errors GET getSessionTemplateOverrides — 200 SessionTemplateOverrides 404 unknown, 400 not built-in PUT updateSessionTemplateOverrides SessionTemplateOverrides 200 SessionTemplate (merged) 404, 400 DELETE deleteSessionTemplateOverrides — 204 404, 400

New schema SessionTemplateOverrides:

  • model: string, nullable
  • engine: string, nullable
  • environment: object (string → string), nullable; values may use ${secret:NAME}

SessionTemplate schema gains read-only overriddenFields: string[].

The existing PUT/DELETE /assistant/templates/{templateId} continue returning 403 for built-ins.

Implementation in AssistantResourceImpl using generated beans from io.apitomy.axiom.api.beans.

docs.title: Import / Export
docs.text: Overrides are not included in configuration packs. They are treated as deployment-local settings. ImportExportService and ConfigurationPacksPage are unchanged.

docs.title: UI
docs.text:
• ui/src/config/api.ts: add SessionTemplateOverrides type, overriddenFields on SessionTemplate, and getSessionTemplateOverrides / updateSessionTemplateOverrides / deleteSessionTemplateOverrides functions.
  • SessionTemplateDetailPage.tsx:
  • For built-ins, model, engine and the Environment tab are editable; all other fields stay read-only.
  • Save on a built-in calls PUT .../overrides with only the three fields.
  • Overridden fields show a "Modified" label.
  • "Reset to defaults" button (shown only when overriddenFields is non-empty) calls DELETE after confirmation, then reloads.
  • SessionTemplatesPage.tsx: built-ins with non-empty overriddenFields show a "Customized" label next to "Built-in".

docs.title: Testing (JUnit 5)
docs.text:
• Service: merge logic (each field individually, all fields, none), empty save deletes row, clearOverrides, rejection of non-built-in IDs, orphaned override rows ignored.
  • REST: GET/PUT/DELETE happy paths, 404 unknown ID, 400 user template, overriddenFields populated in GET /assistant/templates and GET /assistant/templates/{id}.
  • Session creation: a session created from an overridden built-in uses the overridden model and engine.

docs.title: Event Schemas and Jira Ingestion Fidelity — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-21 Status: Approved design, pending implementation plans

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
A live spike against the Red Hat Jira projects IPT and APICURIO (30-day backfill, 275 issues, 357 events, plus scripted activity on test issue APICURIO-137) compared raw Jira data with what Axiom ingested. For the five changelog fields currently handled, new issues, and new comments, nothing was missed. Event content, however, had these defects:

  1. payload.issue is the issue's state at poll time, not at event time (issue.closed with state: open; comment.created showing text from a later edit).
  2. Repeated comment edits share one sourceEventId, so only the first edit is recorded.
  3. stream_event.source_event_id is globally unique, so two sources watching the same project silently drop each other's events.
  4. sourceData.project is never populated (project is not requested from Jira).
  5. closedAt is always null (resolutiondate is not requested).
  6. Assigned/unassigned events have no login for the assignee.
  7. Issue/comment timestamps use Jira's raw format (…+0000) rather than ISO-8601 …Z.
  8. Comment deletions (recorded in the changelog as field Comment) produce no event.
  9. Priority, resolution, due date, fix version, component, and custom-field changes are ignored.

Latent issues that were not hit in this data: closed/reopened is decided by status name rather than category; comments come only from the embedded (possibly incomplete) list; project keys are unquoted in JQL; baseUrl is not validated; the event-source 400 response has an empty body.

There is also no machine-readable contract for the event format. It exists only as prose in docs/developer-guide/event-sourcing-design.md.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Every Axiom event type has a JSON Schema. Schemas are the runtime contract and the reference for writing EL expressions, and lay the groundwork for future user-defined events.
  • Every ingested event (GitHub and Jira) is validated at runtime. Invalid events are saved and flagged.
  • Jira events accurately describe what happened, as of when it happened.
  • The UI's EL reference is driven by the schemas.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Validating sourceData (it is free-form and source-specific).
  • User-defined event types or schema editing.
  • Autocomplete inside the EL editor.
  • Re-validating or rewriting events stored before the upgrade.
  • Jira links, attachments, or work-item links as event types.
  • Jira Data Center / PAT auth, webhooks, historical backfill.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
One spec, three implementation plans, each shipped as its own PR, in order:

  1. Plan 1: Event schema registry, runtime validation, schema API, per-source unique IDs.
  2. Plan 2: Jira ingestion fixes.
  3. Plan 3: UI EL reference driven by schemas, and validation warnings on Event Detail.

Each plan must build and pass tests on its own.

docs.title: Schema files
docs.text:
Location: core/src/main/resources/schemas/events/. JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Every property has a description, and properties have examples where useful (the UI displays both).

  • envelope.json covers the NormalizedEvent envelope: id, sourceEventId, source, eventSourceId, type, ref, timestamp, actor, payload, sourceData.
  • timestamp is required and must be ISO-8601 UTC ending in Z.
  • sourceData is unconstrained (any value, or absent).
  • defs.json holds the shared definitions: Actor, NormalizedIssue, NormalizedComment, NormalizedPullRequest, Change, NormalizedLabel, and any other shared payload records. Every timestamp property in these definitions uses the …Z format.
  • payloads/<event-type>.json exists for every EventType value (26 today), e.g. issue.closed.json. It describes payload for that type and references defs.json.

The schema depends only on the event type, not the source. Source-specific value differences (e.g. Jira issue.number is "PROJ-1", GitHub's is "123") are expressed only as permissive types (string) and documented in descriptions.

docs.title: EventSchemaRegistry
docs.text:
A CDI @ApplicationScoped bean in core.

  • At startup, loads envelope.json, defs.json, and all payloads/*.json, and builds one assembled schema per event type: the envelope with payload replaced by a reference to that type's payload schema.
  • List<EventTypeSchemaSummary> eventTypes() returns the type and description for each event type.
  • JsonNode schemaFor(String type) returns the assembled schema, or empty for an unknown type.
  • List<String> validate(NormalizedEvent event) serializes the event with the application ObjectMapper and validates it. It returns human-readable errors ($.payload.issue.state: must be one of [open, closed]). An unknown event type is itself an error.
  • New dependency: com.networknt:json-schema-validator (Jackson-based).
  • If loading the schemas fails, startup fails: a broken schema is a bug, not a runtime condition.

docs.title: Runtime validation
docs.text:
In EventStreamService.persistEvent, for every source:

  1. Run registry.validate(event).
  2. If there are errors, save the event anyway, with the errors stored in stream_event.validation_errors (JSON array of strings), and log a warning with the sourceEventId and the errors.
  3. If the validator throws, save the event with a single error describing the exception. Ingestion never stops because of validation.
  4. The result returned to the caller tells it whether the event was valid, so pollers can count invalid events.

GitHub and Jira pollers include the invalid count in the poll-log message, for example 245 events ingested (2 failed schema validation). The checkpoint advances normally.

docs.title: Per-source unique IDs
docs.text:
A Flyway migration (next V number):

  • Adds a nullable column stream_event.validation_errors (CLOB/JSON text).
  • Drops the global unique index on stream_event(source_event_id).
  • Creates a unique index on stream_event(event_source_id, source_event_id).

EventStreamService duplicate checks (persistEvent and existingSourceEventIds) match on (eventSourceId, sourceEventId). The sourceEventId format is unchanged, so existing rows remain valid duplicate keys after the upgrade.

docs.title: API (contract-first)
docs.text:
In common/api/src/main/resources/openapi.json:

  • GET /schemas/events returns EventSchemaSummary[] (type, description).
  • GET /schemas/events/{type} returns the assembled JSON Schema (untyped object). It returns 404 for an unknown type.
  • StreamEvent gains an optional validationErrors: string[].

The paths live under /schemas/events rather than /event-schemas because apitomy-codegen groups paths into resource interfaces by the first word before -, so /event-schemas would collide with /event-sources. The endpoints are implemented by EventSchemasResourceImpl, which implements the generated interface SchemasResource.

docs.title: Drift guards (tests)
docs.text:
• Every EventType value has a payloads/<type>.json file, and there are no extra files.
  • Every assembled schema is itself a valid draft 2020-12 schema.
  • Every existing GitHub and Jira normalizer test output validates with no errors.
  • A reflection-based test lists record components of the payload/defs records that have no corresponding schema property, and fails if there are any.
  • EventStreamService tests cover: an invalid event is saved with errors; a validator exception is saved with an error; the same sourceEventId under two event sources is saved twice; the same sourceEventId under one source is a duplicate.

docs.title: Issue state as of each event
docs.text:
The normalizer rebuilds the issue state as of each event by walking the changelog backwards from the current issue.

  • Input: the current issue from search results, plus the full changelog (fetched via the existing truncated-changelog path when needed), plus all comments.
  • Tracked state: status (name, ID, category, so state and stateDetail), summary (title), description (body), assignee (assignees), labels, resolution and resolution date (closedAt), priority, due date, fix versions, components, and every extraFields value.
  • Algorithm:
  • Sort histories newest first.
  • Start the working copy from the current issue.
  • For each history entry, newest first, snapshot the working copy as the state after that entry, then undo that entry's items (to → from) on the copy.
  • After the loop, the copy is the state at creation, used for issue.created.
  • Comment events get the snapshot in effect at the comment's timestamp.
  • Rules:
  • A rebuilt body uses the changelog's plain/wiki text. The current description is converted from Atlassian Document Format (Jira's rich-text JSON) as today.
  • Fields with no changelog history keep their current values. This limitation is documented.
  • Comment bodies are always the current text (Jira keeps no comment history). The edit-specific sourceEventId identifies the edit.
  • updatedAt on a snapshot is the timestamp of the entry that produced it (or created for the creation snapshot).
  • Resolution date: closedAt is the history timestamp of the most recent resolution change to a non-null value at or before the snapshot. If the resolution was cleared after that, closedAt is null.

docs.title: Open/closed by status category
docs.text:
• JiraEventsApiClient.fetchStatuses() calls GET /rest/api/3/status. The poller builds a status ID → category key map once per source per poll.
  • state is closed when the category key is done.
  • issue.closed and issue.reopened events are emitted on transitions into or out of the done category.
  • If the lookup fails, the poller logs a warning and falls back to the current name match (done/closed/resolved).

docs.title: Requested fields and formatting
docs.text:
• Add project, resolutiondate, status, duedate, and the configured extraFields to the search request's fields. Field names are resolved to field IDs through GET /rest/api/3/field, cached per poll. Unknown names are ignored.
  • All timestamps written to the normalized payload (createdAt, updatedAt, closedAt, comment timestamps) are formatted as ISO-8601 UTC …Z.
  • Assignee Actor on issue.assigned and issue.unassigned events gets login from the changelog item's to/from account ID, and displayName from toString/fromString.

docs.title: Event set and IDs
docs.text:
Trigger Event sourceEventId Issue created after cutoff issue.created KEY-created (unchanged) Changelog entry as today, by field KEY-{historyId} or KEY-{historyId}-{i} (unchanged) Comment created issue.comment.created KEY-comment-{id} (unchanged) Comment edited issue.comment.updated KEY-comment-{id}-updated-{updatedEpochMillis} (new) Changelog field Comment with a fromString and no toString issue.comment.deleted KEY-{historyId} priority, resolution, duedate, Fix Version, Component issue.updated with change KEY-{historyId}[-{i}] A field named in configuration.extraFields issue.updated with change KEY-{historyId}[-{i}]
  • issue.comment.deleted carries a NormalizedComment with id null, body set to the deleted text, and author null. The actor is the history author.
  • extraFields names are matched against the changelog item's field value (the name Jira records in the history), case-insensitively.
  • If an issue's embedded comment list is incomplete (total greater than the number returned), comments are read with fetchIssueComments, paging through all of them.

docs.title: Jira sourceData
docs.text:
A selected set of fields, not validated:

  • jiraId, project{key,name}, issueType{name}, status{name,categoryKey}, priority{name}, resolution{name}, dueDate, components[{name}], fixVersions[{name}].
  • extraFields{<name>: <value as of the snapshot>}, present only when configured.

sourceData values follow the same rebuilt-as-of-the-event rule as the payload where history exists.

docs.title: Configuration hardening
docs.text:
• configuration.projects entries must match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$. JQL quotes each key.
  • configuration.extraFields is optional; when present it must be a list of non-blank strings.
  • baseUrl (Jira and GitHub) must match ^https?://, and a trailing / is stripped when saved.
  • Event-source validation failures return 400 with an error body following the existing Error schema.
  • Fix the stale resolveCredentials Javadoc.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Cleaned-up real fixtures in events/jira/src/test/resources/fixtures/: APICURIO-137 (search result, full changelog, comments, statuses) and two or three IPT issues. Account IDs, names, avatars, and free text are replaced with placeholder values.
  • Every normalizer output in tests is checked against EventSchemaRegistry.
  • Regression tests, one per spike defect: snapshot correctness for every event of APICURIO-137, repeated comment edits, comment deletion, closedAt, assignee login, timestamp format, sourceData.project, category-based closed with a custom done status name, extraFields emission and sourceData values, incomplete comment list, project-key validation and JQL quoting, baseUrl normalization.

docs.title: Manual verification
docs.text:
• tools/jira-groundtruth.py is a cleaned-up version of the spike script.
  • Credentials come from JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN; the Axiom URL is an argument.
  • It compares raw Jira activity with ingested events, and also reports schema validation results from the API.
  • Before Plan 2 is complete, run it against IPT, APICURIO, and APICURIO-137 on an isolated dev.sh instance (port offset, temporary AXIOM_HOME and --dataDir).

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
• A useEventSchemas hook uses the generated API client for GET /schemas/events and GET /schemas/events/{type}, and caches results for the session.
  • A schemaToPaths(schema) utility walks the assembled schema and returns rows of {path, type, description, examples}.
  • It follows $refs.
  • Arrays are shown as [0].
  • sourceData is a single row of type "any (source-specific)".
  • Recursion is bounded.
  • It is unit-tested with Vitest.

docs.title: Subscription Detail page
docs.text:
• Replace the hard-coded field tables in ui/src/pages/SubscriptionDetailPage.tsx (around lines 338 and 763) with an Event fields panel.
  • The panel shows the event types in the subscription's type filter. If there are none, a type picker appears with issue.opened selected.
  • For the selected type, the panel lists paths with type, description, and example. Clicking a path copies it into the EL expression.
  • The existing "common expressions" examples stay.

docs.title: Event Detail page
docs.text: When validationErrors is non-empty, show a warning alert listing the errors.

docs.title: Error Handling Summary
docs.text: Situation Behaviour Schema files fail to load or assemble Startup fails Event fails validation Saved with validation_errors; warning logged; counted in poll log Validator throws Saved with one error describing the exception Status-category lookup fails Warning; fall back to name matching Unknown extraFields name Ignored (documented) Comment fetch fails Same handling as a changelog fetch failure: checkpoint not advanced on 5xx/429/network

docs.title: Upgrade Notes
docs.text:
• Existing events and IDs are kept. validation_errors is null for events stored before the upgrade.
  • Comment edits that already have an old-format -updated event will produce one more event under the new ID format after the upgrade. This is an accepted one-time effect.
  • Two sources watching the same project each receive their own events from the upgrade onward.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• docs/developer-guide/event-sourcing-design.md: schema registry and file layout, runtime validation, the issue-state rebuild and its limits, sourceEventId formats, extraFields, status-category rules, the Jira sourceData shape.
  • User guide: the Event fields panel on the Subscription Detail page, and validation warnings on Event Detail.

docs.title: AI Assistant
docs.text:
The AI Assistant is a conversational interface powered by interactive AI engines that supports arbitrary tasks through configurable session templates. Each template defines a persona, tools, MCP servers, and working directory — so you can create sessions tailored to specific workflows, from generating Axiom configuration to general-purpose coding assistance.

Out of the box, Axiom ships three built-in templates you can start sessions from: a Configuration Assistant for creating and updating tools, action types, toolsets, event sources, subscriptions, workflows, and session templates, a General Assistant for open-ended tasks, and a Subject Assistant for working within the context of a specific subject. A fourth built-in template, Workflow Workbench, drives the AI Assistant of the Workflow Workbench; it only works inside the workbench, so the template picker does not list it. You can also create your own templates to define custom workflows.

AI help in other pages

The AI Assistant is the general conversational interface. The Workflow Workbench has its own AI assistant, built into the workbench page, that works on the workflow, action types and tools of a composition; see Workflow Workbench. The action type and tool editors no longer have their own AI Assistant buttons; use the Workbench or a Configuration Assistant session instead.

Note

The AI Assistant requires at least one registered agent that supports interactive sessions (currently claude-code or opencode). A session template can select which agent type to use; if none is specified, the template falls back to the instance's default agent type. If OpenCode capability checks fail at startup, session creation using an OpenCode-backed template is rejected with a compatibility error.

MCP servers configured on a template are available to both Claude Code and OpenCode sessions. For OpenCode, Axiom writes them to an opencode.json file in the session directory and starts the session's opencode serve process with OPENCODE_CONFIG pointing at it. MCP servers from your global OpenCode configuration are also loaded. If a configured MCP server fails to connect, the session shows a warning message with the error reported by OpenCode.

OpenCode sessions run in the same working directory as Claude Code sessions: the template's working directory if set, otherwise the subject workspace for subject sessions, otherwise a directory created inside the session directory. The template's environment variables and, for subject sessions only, AXIOM_SUBJECT_ID, AXIOM_SUBJECT_NAME, AXIOM_REF, and AXIOM_REPOSITORY are passed to the session's opencode serve process, so they are available to OpenCode's tools and MCP servers. Environment variables (including template secrets) are visible to the agent's tools, for example its shell tool. Like Claude Code with CLAUDE.md, OpenCode also loads project-level configuration (opencode.json, .opencode/, AGENTS.md) from the working directory and its git repository; project-level opencode.json settings are applied after Axiom's generated config and can override them (for example MCP servers or permissions).

For OpenCode sessions, the template's Allowed Tools are written as OpenCode permission rules: listed tools (for example Read(*), Bash(ls *) or mcp__axiom__axiom_list_tools) run without asking, and any other tool asks for approval in the chat. Auto-approval rules apply to these requests. Denying a request makes that tool call fail and ends the current reply; send a new message to continue. When a template has no allowed tools, OpenCode's default permissions apply. With Read(*) allowed, .env files are read without prompting (the same as Claude Code). OpenCode may ask a second time for the same tool call, for example to access a directory outside the session working directory; this prompt appears on the same tool block.

The template's system prompt, including subject context for subject sessions, is applied to both engines. Claude Code receives it with --append-system-prompt; OpenCode receives it as the system prompt of every message, added to OpenCode's own system prompt.

OpenCode sessions use the template's model (in provider/model form, for example github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5), or axiom.agent.opencode.model when the template has none. The model is checked against the providers OpenCode has configured; if it is not available, the chat shows a warning and the session falls back to axiom.agent.opencode.model, or to OpenCode's own default model if that is also unavailable (in which case the session header shows no model).

Each OpenCode session's local server is protected with a generated password (a template value for OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is ignored). If the connection to OpenCode drops, Axiom reconnects and shows a notice that some updates may be missing. If stopping a reply fails, a notice is shown and the session keeps running.

OpenCode sessions support slash commands: type / to list OpenCode's commands (for example /init). Commands run without the template's system prompt, because OpenCode's command endpoint cannot carry one. An unknown /name is sent to the model as ordinary text. /clear starts a fresh OpenCode conversation in the same session. When OpenCode runs a subagent (its task tool), the subagent appears as a subagent card with its progress, and its permission requests appear on that card.

docs.title: Accessing the Assistant
docs.text:
Click the robot icon (AI Assistant) in the top-right corner of the Axiom masthead. The icon throbs until you click it for the first time. It is shown only when an interactive AI engine is available.

This takes you to the AI Assistant page (/assistant), where you can create a new session or resume an existing one.

docs.title: Session Templates
docs.text:
Session templates define the behavior and capabilities of an AI Assistant session. Each template specifies:

Field Purpose Name / Description Display name and summary shown in the template picker. System Prompt Markdown instructions passed to the active interactive engine. Welcome Message First message shown in the chat, attributed to the assistant. Agent Type Optional override selecting which registered agent type (claude-code, opencode) drives sessions created from this template. Falls back to the instance's default agent type when unset. Working Directory Absolute path for the session. If empty, Axiom creates a temporary directory under ~/.axiom/assistant/sessions/. For subject-scoped sessions, defaults to the subject workspace. Initial Message Optional message automatically sent to the AI when a session starts. Supports {{subjectName}} placeholder. Model Optional AI model override (e.g., a specific Claude model). MCP Servers Named MCP server configurations to include in the session. Allowed Tools Tool patterns for --allowedTools (e.g., Read(*), Bash(ls *)). Use @ToolsetName to include all tools from a toolset. Init Script Optional startup script executed when the session is created (see Init Scripts below). Environment Optional key-value environment variables for the interactive engine process, the only variables it gets beyond Axiom's own. Values support ${secret:NAME} syntax; secrets are not injected automatically, and a missing secret stops the session from starting.

docs.title: Built-in Templates
docs.text:
Axiom ships four built-in templates:

  • Axiom Configuration Assistant (axiom-config-assistant) — purpose-built for creating and updating Axiom configuration items (tools, action types, toolsets, event sources, subscriptions, workflows, and session templates) with a two-panel layout and Apply workflow.
  • General Assistant (general-assistant) — a minimal template for open-ended tasks with no sidebar or special behavior.
  • Subject Assistant (subject-assistant) — scoped to a specific Axiom subject, with the working directory set to the subject workspace and access to subject-specific MCP tools for querying tasks, events, and the discussion thread.
  • Workflow Workbench (axiom-workbench) — the template behind the Workflow Workbench's AI Assistant. It works on a workbench composition through the axiom-workbench MCP server; use it from the Workbench rather than from the AI Assistant page.

Built-in templates cannot be deleted, and most of their fields are locked. You can clone the General, Subject and Workflow Workbench templates to create fully editable copies; the Configuration Assistant cannot be cloned.

docs.title: Customizing Built-in Templates
docs.text:
The Engine, Model and Environment of each built-in template can be customized per deployment from the template's detail page. Customized fields are marked Modified, and the template list shows a Customized label. Click Reset to defaults to discard all customizations and restore the shipped values; Axiom asks for confirmation before resetting. For any other change, clone the template instead. Cloning a customized built-in template copies its current (customized) engine, model and environment into the new template.

Customizations are stored in Axiom's database and are not included in configuration packs, so exporting and importing a pack does not carry them over. They are also available through the REST API at /api/v1/assistant/templates/{templateId}/overrides (GET, PUT, and DELETE to reset); template responses list customized fields in overriddenFields.

docs.title: User-Defined Templates
docs.text: You create and manage custom templates from Components > AI Assistant (the AI Assistant Templates page, /session-templates). Click Create Template to add one. Each template supports all the fields listed above, giving you full control over the assistant's persona and capabilities.

docs.title: Init Scripts
docs.text:
Init scripts run once when a session is created, before the interactive engine starts. They execute in the session's working directory and are useful for preparing the environment — cloning a repository, installing dependencies, fetching data, or writing config files that the assistant will need during the conversation.

Script types:

Type Runner Use when Bash /bin/bash Shell commands, git operations, file manipulation, package installs Node.js node Fetching data from APIs, generating config files, complex setup logic

Select the script type from the Init Script tab dropdown when editing a template. Write the script body in the editor below it.

Timeout: Init scripts have a 60-second timeout. If the script does not exit within 60 seconds, or exits with a non-zero status, session creation fails and an error is shown. Keep scripts focused on quick setup tasks — long-running operations should be handled by the assistant itself during the conversation.

Environment: Init scripts do not inherit the template's environment variables. Template environment variables (including resolved ${secret:NAME} references) are injected into the interactive engine process, which starts after the init script finishes. If your init script needs credentials (e.g., for git clone or API calls), they must be available through the server's own environment or set up by other means.

Common use cases:

  • Clone a repository — git clone a repo into the working directory so the assistant can work on it immediately.
  • Install dependencies — run npm install, pip install -r requirements.txt, or mvn dependency:resolve to prepare the project.
  • Write configuration files — generate .env, settings.json, or other config files that the assistant or its tools will need.
  • Fetch context — download issue details, pull request metadata, or other context from external APIs and save it to a file the assistant can read.

Example (bash):

#!/bin/bash
# Clone a specific repo branch into the working directory
git clone --branch main --depth 1 \
  https://${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/my-org/my-repo.git .
npm install

Example (Node.js):

const fs = require("fs");
const resp = await fetch("https://api.github.com/repos/my-org/my-repo/issues/42", {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.GH_TOKEN}` },
});
const issue = await resp.json();
fs.writeFileSync("context.json", JSON.stringify(issue, null, 2));

Security: Init scripts run unsandboxed

Init scripts execute as the same OS user that runs the Axiom server process. There is no sandboxing, filesystem restriction, or network isolation — the only guard is the 60-second timeout. This means anyone who can create or edit a session template can run arbitrary code on the server with the server's full privileges.

Recommendations:

  • Restrict template creation to trusted administrators. Treat the ability to create or edit session templates as equivalent to shell access on the server.
  • If Axiom is deployed in a multi-tenant or untrusted environment, consider running the server under a restricted service account with minimal filesystem and network permissions, or use container-level isolation to limit the blast radius of init scripts.

docs.title: Creating a Session
docs.text:
1. Click New Session on the Assistant page.
  2. A template picker modal appears. Browse or search available templates — each shows its name and description.
  3. Select a template.
  4. A name modal appears with an auto-generated fun name (e.g., "rocket-penguin-waffle"). You can accept or change it.
  5. Click Create to start the session.

Axiom supports a limited number of concurrent sessions (default: 3, configurable via axiom.assistant.max-sessions).

docs.title: Header Toolbar
docs.text:
The session header toolbar provides quick access to session controls and status:

  • Session name — displayed prominently, editable inline via the pencil icon
  • Plan Mode — an orange label appears when the assistant is in plan mode
  • Engine — a label showing the interactive engine (Claude Code or OpenCode)
  • Model — shows the AI model in use for this session
  • Running cost — real-time cost display (e.g., $0.0342) that accumulates per turn; hover to see input and output tokens. When the engine reports no cost, the token count is shown instead
  • Subject — for subject sessions, a label linking to the subject
  • Apply All — imports generated items (Config Assistant sessions only; disabled when no items exist)
  • Allow All — a switch that, after a confirmation, approves every tool request in the session without prompting
  • Auto-approval badge — shield icon with a count of active auto-approval rules (shown when at least one rule exists)
  • End Session — stops the session with a confirmation prompt
  • Open in new window — opens the session in a dedicated browser tab (breakout window) for a focused, full-screen experience

docs.title: Chat Panel
docs.text:
The chat panel is a conversation interface where you interact with the assistant:

  • Your messages appear right-aligned in blue bubbles
  • Assistant messages appear left-aligned in grey, with full markdown rendering (tables, code blocks, lists) via react-markdown
  • Tool use blocks are expandable and color-coded by category:
    • Green — axiom-sdk tools
    • Purple — axiom-tools
    • Orange — plan/agent operations
    • Teal — AskUser interactions

You can send another message while the assistant is still working; it is queued and answered after the current reply. If a message cannot be delivered, the chat shows a "Message was not delivered" notice. When you stop the assistant, OpenCode discards messages that are still queued, while Claude Code answers them after stopping.

While the assistant is working, a Stop button appears next to Send. It stops the current reply without ending the session, so you can continue the conversation. If the reply can't be stopped, the chat shows a notice.

docs.title: Slash Commands
docs.text: Type / in the chat input to see available slash commands. Use arrow keys to navigate the autocomplete list and Tab or Enter to select a command. The available commands are populated from the active interactive session runtime.

docs.title: Permission Prompts
docs.text:
When the assistant needs to use a tool, a permission prompt appears with Allow and Deny buttons. You can also click Allow Pattern... to create an auto-approval rule so similar requests are approved automatically in the future.

With the OpenCode engine, an Always Allow button also appears when OpenCode provides "always" patterns for the request (for example echo * for a bash command). It approves the request and tells OpenCode to approve matching requests for the rest of the session. Hover over the button to see the patterns. Claude Code does not offer this, so the button does not appear there.

Special permission types have dedicated UX:

  • AskUserQuestion — renders structured multi-choice options
  • ExitPlanMode — displays the plan as rendered markdown with Approve and Reject buttons

docs.title: Plan Mode
docs.text: When the assistant enters plan mode, the session header shows visual indicators: an orange border and a "Plan Mode" label. The plan is rendered as markdown, and you can Approve or Reject it before the assistant proceeds.

docs.title: Auto-Approval Rules
docs.text:
Auto-approval rules let you skip repetitive permission prompts for trusted tool operations. Each rule defines:

  • Tool name — the tool to auto-approve (e.g., Read, Bash)
  • Field name (optional) — a specific input field to match
  • Regex pattern (optional) — a regular expression the field value must match

For example, you could auto-approve all Read tool calls where the file path matches /src/.* to avoid approving every source file read individually.

Rules are scoped to the current session and managed via the shield icon in the toolbar. Click the icon to view active rules or delete individual ones.

docs.title: Breakout Window
docs.text: Click the Open in new window icon in the session toolbar to open the session in a dedicated browser tab. This hides the Axiom masthead and sidebar, giving you a focused, full-screen chat experience. The breakout window stays connected to the same session — you can switch between the main window and the breakout at any time.

docs.title: Cost Monitoring
docs.text: The session toolbar displays a running cost for the current session (e.g., $0.0342). This accumulates in real time as the assistant processes each turn, tracking input tokens, output tokens, and duration. Use this to monitor how much a session is consuming, especially for long or complex conversations. The displayed cost is the session's total, including spend from before any /clear.

docs.title: Configuration Assistant
docs.text: The Configuration Assistant template (axiom-config-assistant) provides a specialized workflow for creating and updating Axiom configuration items. It extends the standard session interface with a two-panel layout and an Apply workflow.

docs.title: Two-Panel Layout
docs.text:
• Chat panel (70%) — the standard conversation interface
  • Generated Items sidebar (30%) — displays items the assistant has created

docs.title: Generated Items
docs.text:
As the assistant creates or updates items, they appear in the sidebar. The assistant can work with these types of configuration items:
